1.85.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
vāgdevatā vatāro 'nyaḥ kāliketi prakīrtitā /
tasyā mantraṃ pravakṣyāmi bhuktimuktipradaṃ nṛṇām //
1.85.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
वाग्देवता वतारो ऽन्यः कालिकेति प्रकीर्तिता ।
तस्या मन्त्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं नृणाम् ॥
1.85.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Another incarnation of the goddess of speech is celebrated as Kālikā; / I shall proclaim her mantra, which bestows enjoyment and liberation upon mortals.

1.85.s:
sṛṣṭikriyānvitā śāntirbidvāḍhyā ca tridhā punaḥ /
aruṇākṣyādīpikā ca binduyuktā dvidhā tataḥ //
1.85.d:
सृष्टिक्रियान्विता शान्तिर्बिद्वाढ्या च त्रिधा पुनः ।
अरुणाक्ष्यादीपिका च बिन्दुयुक्ता द्विधा ततः ॥
1.85.m: Śānti combined with the activity of creation, endowed with a dot, three times; / then Aruṇākṣī and Dīpikā, endowed with a dot, twice;

1.85.s:
māyādvayaṃ tataḥ paścāddakṣiṇe kālike padam /
punaśca saptabījāni svāhānto 'yaṃ manūttamaḥ //
1.85.d:
मायाद्वयं ततः पश्चाद्दक्षिणे कालिके पदम् ।
पुनश्च सप्तबीजानि स्वाहान्तो ऽयं मनूत्तमः ॥
1.85.m: after that, two māyā-seeds, then the phrase 'dakṣiṇe kālike', / and again seven seed-syllables, ending with 'svāhā'—this is the supreme mantra.

1.85.s:
bhairavo 'sya ṛṣiśchanda uṣṇikkālī tu devatā /
bījaṃ māyādīrghavartma śaktiruktā munīśvara //
1.85.d:
भैरवो ऽस्य ऋषिश्छन्द उष्णिक्काली तु देवता ।
बीजं मायादीर्घवर्त्म शक्तिरुक्ता मुनीश्वर ॥
1.85.m: Bhairava is its seer; the metre is Uṣṇih; Kālī is the deity; / the seed-syllable is Māyā; Dīrghavartmā is declared as the energy, O lord of sages.

1.85.s:
ṣaḍdīrdhāḍhye bījena vidyāyā aṅgamīritam /
mātṛkārṇāndaśa daśa hṛdaye bhujayoḥ padoḥ //
1.85.d:
षड्दीर्धाढ्ये बीजेन विद्याया अङ्गमीरितम् ।
मातृकार्णान्दश दश हृदये भुजयोः पदोः ॥
1.85.m: With the seed-syllable endowed with the six long vowels, the limb-structure of the vidyā is proclaimed. / Ten syllables of the alphabet each [are to be placed] on the heart, on the two arms, on the two feet;

1.85.s:
vinyasya vyāpakaṃ kuryānmūlamantreṇa sādhakaḥ /
śiraḥ kṛpāṇamabhayaṃ varaṃ hastaiśca bibhratīm //
1.85.d:
विन्यस्य व्यापकं कुर्यान्मूलमन्त्रेण साधकः ।
शिरः कृपाणमभयं वरं हस्तैश्च बिभ्रतीम् ॥
1.85.m: Having placed [them], the practitioner should perform the pervasive ritual placement with the root mantra, / [meditating on her] bearing in her hands a head, a sword, the gesture of fearlessness, and the boon-granting gesture,

1.85.s:
muṇḍasraṅmastakāṃ muktakeśāṃ pitṛvanastitām /
sarvālaṅkṛtavarṇāṃ ca śyāmāṅgīṃ kālikāṃ smaret //
1.85.d:
मुण्डस्रङ्मस्तकां मुक्तकेशां पितृवनस्तिताम् ।
सर्वालङ्कृतवर्णां च श्यामाङ्गीं कालिकां स्मरेत् ॥
1.85.m: Her head garlanded with severed skulls, her hair dishevelled, situated in the cremation ground, / endowed with every ornamental attribute, dark-limbed Kālikā he should recall.

1.85.s:
evaṃ dhyātvā japellakṣaṃ juhuyādayutaṃ tataḥ /
prasūnaiḥ karavīrotthaiḥ pūjāyantramathocyate //
1.85.d:
एवं ध्यात्वा जपेल्लक्षं जुहुयादयुतं ततः ।
प्रसूनैः करवीरोत्थैः पूजायन्त्रमथोच्यते ॥
1.85.m: Having meditated thus, he should recite a hundred thousand times, and then offer ten thousand fire oblations / with blossoms of the karavīra flower. Next, the diagram of worship is described.

1.85.s:
vilikhya pūrvaṃ ṣaṭkoṇaṃ trikoṇatritayaṃ tataḥ /
padmamaṣṭadalaṃ bāhye bhūpuraṃ tatra pūjayet //
1.85.d:
विलिख्य पूर्वं षट्कोणं त्रिकोणत्रितयं ततः ।
पद्ममष्टदलं बाह्ये भूपुरं तत्र पूजयेत् ॥
1.85.m: Having drawn first a six-pointed figure, and then a group of three triangles, / an eight-petalled lotus outside, and a bhūpura there, he should worship [the deities].

1.85.s:
jayā ca vijayā cāpi ajitā cāparājitā /
nityā vilāsinī vāpi dogdhyaghorā ca maṅgalā //
1.85.d:
जया च विजया चापि अजिता चापराजिता ।
नित्या विलासिनी वापि दोग्ध्यघोरा च मङ्गला ॥
1.85.m: Jayā, Vijayā, Ajitā, and Aparājitā, / Nityā, Vilāsinī, Dogdhryaghorā, and Maṅgalā:

1.85.s:
pīṭhasya śaktayo māyātmane hṛtpīṭhamantrakaḥ /
śivarūpaśavaśthāṃ ca śivābhirdikṣu veṣṭitām //
1.85.d:
पीठस्य शक्तयो मायात्मने हृत्पीठमन्त्रकः ।
शिवरूपशवश्थां च शिवाभिर्दिक्षु वेष्टिताम् ॥
1.85.m: These are the powers of the ritual seat; the heart-mantra of the ritual seat belongs to the nature of Māyā. / [Meditating on her] seated on a corpse in the form of Śiva, surrounded in all directions by jackals,

1.85.s:
mahākālaratāsaktāṃ dhyātvāṅgānyarcayetpurā /
kālīṃ kapālinīṃ kullāṃ kurukullāṃ virodhinīm //
1.85.d:
महाकालरतासक्तां ध्यात्वाङ्गान्यर्चयेत्पुरा ।
कालीं कपालिनीं कुल्लां कुरुकुल्लां विरोधिनीम् ॥
1.85.m: Engaged in amorous union with Mahākāla, he should first worship the limbs; / then Kāli, Kapālinī, Kullā, Kurukullā, Virodhinī,

1.85.s:
vipracittāṃ ca ṣaṭkoṇe navakoṇe tator'cayet /
ugrāmuṣṇaprabhāṃ dīptāṃ nīlādhānāṃ balākikām //
1.85.d:
विप्रचित्तां च षट्कोणे नवकोणे ततोर्ऽचयेत् ।
उग्रामुष्णप्रभां दीप्तां नीलाधानां बलाकिकाम् ॥
1.85.m: And Vipracittā in the six-pointed figure; then in the nine-pointed figure he should worship / Ugrā, Uṣṇaprabhā, Dīptā, Nīlādhānā, Balākikā,

1.85.s:
mātrāṃ mudrāṃ tathā mitrāṃ pūjyāḥ patreṣu mātaraḥ /
padmasyāsya suyatnena brāhmī nārāyaṇītyapi //
1.85.d:
मात्रां मुद्रां तथा मित्रां पूज्याः पत्रेषु मातरः ।
पद्मस्यास्य सुयत्नेन ब्राह्मी नारायणीत्यपि ॥
1.85.m: Mātrā, Mudrā, and likewise Mitrā. The mothers are to be worshipped on the petals / of this lotus with great effort: Brāhmī, Nārāyaṇī as well,

1.85.s:
māheśvarī ca cāmuṇḍā kaumārī cāparājitā /
vārāhī nārasiṃhā ca punaretāstu bhūpure //
1.85.d:
माहेश्वरी च चामुण्डा कौमारी चापराजिता ।
वाराही नारसिंहा च पुनरेतास्तु भूपुरे ॥
1.85.m: Māheśvarī, Cāmuṇḍā, Kaumārī, Aparājitā, / Vārāhī, and Nārasiṃhī; and then these in the bhūpura:

1.85.s:
bhairavīṃ mahadādyāṃ tāṃ siṃhādyāṃ dhūmrapūrvikām /
bhīmonmattādikāṃ cāpi vaśīkaraṇabhairavīm //
1.85.d:
भैरवीं महदाद्यां तां सिंहाद्यां धूम्रपूर्विकाम् ।
भीमोन्मत्तादिकां चापि वशीकरणभैरवीम् ॥
1.85.m: Bhairavī beginning with Mahat, Siṃhādyā, Dhūmrapūrvikā, / Bhīmonmattādikā as well, and Vaśīkaraṇabhairavī,

1.85.s:
mohanādyāṃ samārādhya śakrādīnyāyudhānyapi /
evamārādhitā kālī siddhā bhavati mantriṇām //
1.85.d:
मोहनाद्यां समाराध्य शक्रादीन्यायुधान्यपि ।
एवमाराधिता काली सिद्धा भवति मन्त्रिणाम् ॥
1.85.m: And worshiping the one beginning with Mohana, along with Indra and the others and the weapons. / Worshipped in this manner, Kālī becomes accomplished for practitioners of mantras.

1.85.s:
tataḥ prayogānkurvīta mahābhairavabhāṣitān /
ātmano vā parasyārthaṃ kṣiprasiddhipradāyakān //
1.85.d:
ततः प्रयोगान्कुर्वीत महाभैरवभाषितान् ।
आत्मनो वा परस्यार्थं क्षिप्रसिद्धिप्रदायकान् ॥
1.85.m: Then he may perform the ritual applications proclaimed by Mahābhairava, / which grant swift accomplishment for oneself or for another's sake.

1.85.s:
strīṇāṃ prahāraṃ nindāṃ ca kauṭilyaṃ vāpriyaṃ vacaḥ /
ātmano hitamanvicchan kālībhakto vivarjayet //
1.85.d:
स्त्रीणां प्रहारं निन्दां च कौटिल्यं वाप्रियं वचः ।
आत्मनो हितमन्विच्छन् कालीभक्तो विवर्जयेत् ॥
1.85.m: Beating women, speaking ill of them, deceit, or unpleasant speech— / seeking his own welfare, a devotee of Kālī must avoid these.

1.85.s:
sudṛśo madanāvāsaṃ paśyanyaḥ prajapenmanum /
ayutaṃ so 'cirādeva vākpateḥ samatāmiyāt //
1.85.d:
सुदृशो मदनावासं पश्यन्यः प्रजपेन्मनुम् ।
अयुतं सो ऽचिरादेव वाक्पतेः समतामियात् ॥
1.85.m: Looking upon the abode of love of a fair-eyed woman, whoever recites the mantra / ten thousand times would quickly attain equality with the lord of speech.

1.85.s:
digambaro muktakeśaḥ śmaśānastho 'dhiyāmini /
japedyo 'yutametasya bhaveyuḥ sarvasiddhayaḥ //
1.85.d:
दिगम्बरो मुक्तकेशः श्मशानस्थो ऽधियामिनि ।
जपेद्यो ऽयुतमेतस्य भवेयुः सर्वसिद्धयः ॥
1.85.m: Sky-clad, with dishevelled hair, standing in a cremation ground in the dead of night, / whoever recites ten thousand times—to him all accomplishments shall belong.

1.85.s:
śavasya hṛdaye sthitvā nirvāsāḥ pretabhūmigaḥ /
arkapuṣpasahasreṇābhyaktena svīyaretasā //
1.85.d:
शवस्य हृदये स्थित्वा निर्वासाः प्रेतभूमिगः ।
अर्कपुष्पसहस्रेणाभ्यक्तेन स्वीयरेतसा ॥
1.85.m: Standing upon the heart of a corpse, naked, gone to the cemetery, / with a thousand arka flowers anointed with his own semen,

1.85.s:
devīṃ yaḥ pūjayedbhaktyā japannekaikaśo manum /
so 'careṇaiva kālena dharaṇīprabhutāṃ vrajet //
1.85.d:
देवीं यः पूजयेद्भक्त्या जपन्नेकैकशो मनुम् ।
सो ऽचरेणैव कालेन धरणीप्रभुतां व्रजेत् ॥
1.85.m: Whoever worships the goddess with devotion, reciting the mantra one by one, / would attain sovereignty over the earth in no time at all.

1.85.s:
rajaḥ kīrṇaṃ bhagaṃ nāryā dhyāyanyo hyayutaṃ japet /
sakavitvena ramyeṇa janānmohayati dhruvam //
1.85.d:
रजः कीर्णं भगं नार्या ध्यायन्यो ह्ययुतं जपेत् ।
सकवित्वेन रम्येण जनान्मोहयति ध्रुवम् ॥
1.85.m: Meditating on a woman’s vulva filled with menstrual fluid, whoever recites ten thousand times / surely bewilders people with delightful poetic skill.

1.85.s:
tripañcāre mahāpīṭhe śivasya hṛdi saṃsthitām /
mahākālena devena mārayuddhaṃ prakurvatīm //
1.85.d:
त्रिपञ्चारे महापीठे शिवस्य हृदि संस्थिताम् ।
महाकालेन देवेन मारयुद्धं प्रकुर्वतीम् ॥
1.85.m: Situated on the great seat of fifteen spokes upon the heart of Śiva, / engaged in erotic combat with the god Mahākāla,

1.85.s:
tāṃ dhyāyansmeravadanāṃ vidadhatsurataṃ svayam /
japetsahasramapi yaḥ sa śaṅkarasamo bhavet //
1.85.d:
तां ध्यायन्स्मेरवदनां विदधत्सुरतं स्वयम् ।
जपेत्सहस्रमपि यः स शङ्करसमो भवेत् ॥
1.85.m: Meditating on her with a smiling face while personally engaging in intercourse, / whoever recites even a thousand times becomes equal to Śaṅkara.

1.85.s:
asthilomatvacāyuktaṃ māṃsaṃ mārjārameṣayoḥ /
uṣṭrasya mahiṣasyāpi baliṃ yastu samarpayet //
1.85.d:
अस्थिलोमत्वचायुक्तं मांसं मार्जारमेषयोः ।
उष्ट्रस्य महिषस्यापि बलिं यस्तु समर्पयेत् ॥
1.85.m: Offering as an oblation flesh accompanied by bones, hair, and skin / of a cat, a ram, a camel, or a buffalo,

1.85.s:
bhūtāṣṭamyormadhyarātre vaśyāḥ syustasya jantavaḥ /
vidyālakṣmīyaśaḥputraiḥ sa ciraṃ sukhamedhate //
1.85.d:
भूताष्टम्योर्मध्यरात्रे वश्याः स्युस्तस्य जन्तवः ।
विद्यालक्ष्मीयशःपुत्रैः स चिरं सुखमेधते ॥
1.85.m: At midnight on the fourteenth or eighth lunar day, living beings will be subdued by him; / he thrives happily for a long time with knowledge, fortune, fame, and sons.

1.85.s:
yo haviṣyāśanarato divā devīṃ smaran japet /
naktaṃ nidhuvanāsakto lakṣaṃ sa syāddharāpatiḥ //
1.85.d:
यो हविष्याशनरतो दिवा देवीं स्मरन् जपेत् ।
नक्तं निधुवनासक्तो लक्षं स स्याद्धरापतिः ॥
1.85.m: Whoever, devoted to eating sacrificial offerings, recites recalling the goddess by day, / and is devoted to lovemaking by night, [for] a hundred thousand times, becomes an earthly ruler.

1.85.s:
raktāṃbhojairhunenmantrī dhanairjayati vittapam /
bilvapatrairbhavedrājyaṃ raktapuṣpairvaśīkṛtiḥ //
1.85.d:
रक्तांभोजैर्हुनेन्मन्त्री धनैर्जयति वित्तपम् ।
बिल्वपत्रैर्भवेद्राज्यं रक्तपुष्पैर्वशीकृतिः ॥
1.85.m: Offering oblations with red lotuses, the practitioner of mantras surpasses Kubera in wealth; / with bilva leaves comes kingship, and with red flowers comes subjugation.

1.85.s:
asṛjī mahiṣādīnāṃ kālikāṃ yastu tarpayet /
tasya syuracirādeva karasthāḥ sarvasiddhayaḥ //
1.85.d:
असृजी महिषादीनां कालिकां यस्तु तर्पयेत् ।
तस्य स्युरचिरादेव करस्थाः सर्वसिद्धयः ॥
1.85.m: Whoever satisfies Kālikā with the blood of buffaloes and the like, / in his hands all accomplishments shall swiftly rest.

1.85.s:
yo lakṣaṃ prajapenmantraṃ śavamāruhya mantravit /
tasya siddho manuḥ sadyaḥ sarvepsitaphalapradaḥ //
1.85.d:
यो लक्षं प्रजपेन्मन्त्रं शवमारुह्य मन्त्रवित् ।
तस्य सिद्धो मनुः सद्यः सर्वेप्सितफलप्रदः ॥
1.85.m: Whoever, knowing the mantras, recites the mantra a hundred thousand times having mounted a corpse, / for him the mantra is instantly accomplished, yielding all desired fruits.

1.85.s:
tenāśvamedhapramukhairyāgauriṣṭaṃ sujanmanā /
dattaṃ dānaṃ tapastaptaṃ upāste yastu kālikām //
1.85.d:
तेनाश्वमेधप्रमुखैर्यागौरिष्टं सुजन्मना ।
दत्तं दानं तपस्तप्तं उपास्ते यस्तु कालिकाम् ॥
1.85.m: By him sacrifices headed by the horse sacrifice have been offered, he of noble birth; / gifts have been given, austerities practiced by him who worships Kālikā.

1.85.s:
brahmā viṣṇuḥ śivo gaurī lakṣmīrgaṇapatī raviḥ /
pūjitāḥ sakalā devā yaḥ kālīṃ pūjayetsadā //
1.85.d:
ब्रह्मा विष्णुः शिवो गौरी लक्ष्मीर्गणपती रविः ।
पूजिताः सकला देवा यः कालीं पूजयेत्सदा ॥
1.85.m: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Gaurī, Lakṣmī, Gaṇapati, and the Sun— / all gods are worshipped by him who constantly worships Kālī.

1.85.s:
athāparaḥ sarasvatyā hyavatāro nigadyate /
yāṃ niṣevya narā loke kṛtārthāḥ syurna saṃśayaḥ //
1.85.d:
अथापरः सरस्वत्या ह्यवतारो निगद्यते ।
यां निषेव्य नरा लोके कृतार्थाः स्युर्न संशयः ॥
1.85.m: Now another incarnation of Sarasvatī is proclaimed, / by serving whom men in the world become fulfilled, without a doubt.

1.85.s:
āpyāyinī candrayuktā māyā ca vadanāntare /
sakāmikā krudhā śāntiścandrālaṅkṛtamastakā //
1.85.d:
आप्यायिनी चन्द्रयुक्ता माया च वदनान्तरे ।
सकामिका क्रुधा शान्तिश्चन्द्रालङ्कृतमस्तका ॥
1.85.m: Āpyāyinī joined with the moon, and Māyā in the middle of the mouth, / Sakāmikā, with anger, Śānti adorned with the moon on her head,

1.85.s:
dīpikā sāsanā candrayugastraṃ manurīritaḥ /
munirakṣobhya uddiṣṭaśchandastu bṛhatī matam //
1.85.d:
दीपिका सासना चन्द्रयुगस्त्रं मनुरीरितः ।
मुनिरक्षोभ्य उद्दिष्टश्छन्दस्तु बृहती मतम् ॥
1.85.m: Dīpikā seated, the two moons, and the weapon: the mantra is stated. / The sage is declared to be Akṣobhya, and the meter is regarded as Bṛhatī.

1.85.s:
tārākhyā devatā bījaṃ dvitīyañca caturthakam /
śaktiḥ ṣaḍdīrghayuktena dvitīyenāṅgakalpanam //
1.85.d:
ताराख्या देवता बीजं द्वितीयञ्च चतुर्थकम् ।
शक्तिः षड्दीर्घयुक्तेन द्वितीयेनाङ्गकल्पनम् ॥
1.85.m: The deity is called Tārā; the second is the seed-syllable, and the fourth / is the power; the arrangement of the limbs is performed with the second [syllable] joined with the six long [vowels].

1.85.s:
ṣoḍhā nyāsaṃ tataḥ kuryāttārāyāḥ sarvasiddhim /
śrīkaṇṭhādīnnyasedrudrānmātṛkāvarṇapūrvakān //
1.85.d:
षोढा न्यासं ततः कुर्यात्तारायाः सर्वसिद्धिम् ।
श्रीकण्ठादीन्न्यसेद्रुद्रान्मातृकावर्णपूर्वकान् ॥
1.85.m: Then he should perform the sixfold ritual placement of Tārā, which yields all accomplishments. / He should place the Rudras beginning with Śrīkaṇṭha preceded by the letters of the alphabet,

1.85.s:
mātṛkoktasthale māyā tṛtīyakrodhapūrvakān /
caturthīnamasāyuktānprathamo nyāsa īritaḥ //
1.85.d:
मातृकोक्तस्थले माया तृतीयक्रोधपूर्वकान् ।
चतुर्थीनमसायुक्तान्प्रथमो न्यास ईरितः ॥
1.85.m: At the places stated for the alphabet, preceded by Māyā, the third [syllable], and Krodha, / and accompanied by the dative case and namas; this is declared as the first ritual placement.

1.85.s:
śavapīṭhasamāsīnāṃ nīlakāntiṃ trilocanām /
arddhenduśekharāṃ nānābhūṣaṇāḍhyāṃ smarannyaset //
1.85.d:
शवपीठसमासीनां नीलकान्तिं त्रिलोचनाम् ।
अर्द्धेन्दुशेखरां नानाभूषणाढ्यां स्मरन्न्यसेत् ॥
1.85.m: Seated upon a corpse-seat, blue-complexioned, three-eyed, / crested with the crescent moon, adorned with various ornaments—recalling her, he should place [them].

1.85.s:
dvitīye tu grahanyāsaṃ kuryāttāṃ samanusmaran /
tribījasvarapūrvaṃ tu raktasūya hṛdi nyaset //
1.85.d:
द्वितीये तु ग्रहन्यासं कुर्यात्तां समनुस्मरन् ।
त्रिबीजस्वरपूर्वं तु रक्तसूय हृदि न्यसेत् ॥
1.85.m: In the second, he should perform the ritual placement of planets, remembering her well: / preceded by the three seed-syllables and vowels, he should place the red Sun in the heart;

1.85.s:
tathā pavargapūrvaṃ tu śuklaṃ lomaṃ bhruvodveye /
kavargapūrvaṃ raktābhaṃ maṅgalaṃ locanatrayam //
1.85.d:
तथा पवर्गपूर्वं तु शुक्लं लोमं भ्रुवोद्वेये ।
कवर्गपूर्वं रक्ताभं मङ्गलं लोचनत्रयम् ॥
1.85.m: Likewise, preceded by the pa-class [of consonants], the white Moon on both eyebrows; / preceded by the ka-class, the red-hued Mars on the triad of eyes;

1.85.s:
cavargādyaṃ budhaṃ śyāmaṃ nyasedvakṣaghasthale budhaḥ /
ḍhavargādyaṃ pītavarṇaṃ kaṭhṇakūpe bṛhaspatim //
1.85.d:
चवर्गाद्यं बुधं श्यामं न्यसेद्वक्षघस्थले बुधः ।
ढवर्गाद्यं पीतवर्णं कठ्णकूपे बृहस्पतिम् ॥
1.85.m: Preceded by the ca-class, the wise man should place dark Mercury on the chest; / preceded by the ḍha-class, yellow Jupiter in the throat-well;

1.85.s:
tavargādyaṃ śvetavarṇaṃ ghaṭikāyāṃ tu bhārgavam /
nīlavarṇaṃ pavargādyaṃ nābhideśe śanaiścaram //
1.85.d:
तवर्गाद्यं श्वेतवर्णं घटिकायां तु भार्गवम् ।
नीलवर्णं पवर्गाद्यं नाभिदेशे शनैश्चरम् ॥
1.85.m: Preceded by the ta-class, white Venus in the nape of the neck; / preceded by the pa-class, blue-colored Saturn in the region of the navel;

1.85.s:
śavargādyaṃ dhūmravarṇaṃ dhyātvā rāhuṃ mukhe nyaset /
tribījapūrvakaścaivaṃ grahanyāsaḥ samīritaḥ //
1.85.d:
शवर्गाद्यं धूम्रवर्णं ध्यात्वा राहुं मुखे न्यसेत् ।
त्रिबीजपूर्वकश्चैवं ग्रहन्यासः समीरितः ॥
1.85.m: Preceded by the śa-class, meditating on smoke-colored Rāhu, he should place him in the mouth. / Thus the ritual placement of planets preceded by the three seed-syllables is proclaimed.

1.85.s:
tṛtīyaṃ lokapālānāṃ nyāsaṃ kuryātprayatnataḥ /
māyādibījatritayapūrvakaṃ sarvasiddhaye //
1.85.d:
तृतीयं लोकपालानां न्यासं कुर्यात्प्रयत्नतः ।
मायादिबीजत्रितयपूर्वकं सर्वसिद्धये ॥
1.85.m: Thirdly, he should carefully perform the ritual placement of the world guardians, / preceded by the triad of seed-syllables beginning with Māyā, for all accomplishments,

1.85.s:
svamastake lalāṭādi dikṣvaṣṭasvadhaurddhvataḥ /
hrasvadīrghakādikāṣṭavargapūrvāndiśādhipān //
1.85.d:
स्वमस्तके ललाटादि दिक्ष्वष्टस्वधौर्द्ध्वतः ।
ह्रस्वदीर्घकादिकाष्टवर्गपूर्वान्दिशाधिपान् ॥
1.85.m: On his own head, forehead, and so forth, in the eight directions, below, and above— / the regents of the directions preceded by the short, long, and the eight classes beginning with ka.

1.85.s:
śivaśaktyabhidhe nyāsaṃ caturthe tu samācaret /
tribījapūrvakānnyasyetṣaṭśivāñchaktisaṃyutān //
1.85.d:
शिवशक्त्यभिधे न्यासं चतुर्थे तु समाचरेत् ।
त्रिबीजपूर्वकान्न्यस्येत्षट्शिवाञ्छक्तिसंयुतान् ॥
1.85.m: In the fourth, he should perform the ritual placement named after Śiva and Śakti: / preceded by the three seed-syllables, he should place the six Śivas accompanied by their powers,

1.85.s:
ādhārādiṣu cakreṣu svacakravarṇapūrvakān /
brahmāṇaṃ ḍākinīyuktaṃ vādisāṃtārṇapūrvakam //
1.85.d:
आधारादिषु चक्रेषु स्वचक्रवर्णपूर्वकान् ।
ब्रह्माणं डाकिनीयुक्तं वादिसांतार्णपूर्वकम् ॥
1.85.m: In the cakras beginning with the mūlādhāra, preceded by the syllables of their respective cakras: / Brahmā joined with Ḍākinī, preceded by the letters from va to sa,

1.85.s:
mūlādhāre vinyasecca caturddalasamanvitam /
śrīviṣṇuṃ rākiṇīyuktabādilāntārṇapūrvakam //
1.85.d:
मूलाधारे विन्यसेच्च चतुर्द्दलसमन्वितम् ।
श्रीविष्णुं राकिणीयुक्तबादिलान्तार्णपूर्वकम् ॥
1.85.m: He should place in the four-petalled mūlādhāra; / Śrīviṣṇu joined with Rākiṇī, preceded by the letters from ba to la,

1.85.s:
svādhiṣṭhanābhidhe cakre liṅgasthe ṣaḍdale nyaset /
rudraṃ tu ḍākinīyuktaṃ ḍādiphaāntārṇapūrvakam //
1.85.d:
स्वाधिष्ठनाभिधे चक्रे लिङ्गस्थे षड्दले न्यसेत् ।
रुद्रं तु डाकिनीयुक्तं डादिफआन्तार्णपूर्वकम् ॥
1.85.m: He should place in the six-petalled cakra named svādhiṣṭhāna situated at the genitals; / Rudra joined with Lākinī, preceded by the letters from ḍa to pha,

1.85.s:
cakre daśadale nyasyennābhisthe maṇipūrake /
īśvaraṃ kādiṭhāntārṇapūrvakaṃ śākinīyutam //
1.85.d:
चक्रे दशदले न्यस्येन्नाभिस्थे मणिपूरके ।
ईश्वरं कादिठान्तार्णपूर्वकं शाकिनीयुतम् ॥
1.85.m: He should place in the ten-petalled cakra situated at the navel, the maṇipūraka; / Īśvara accompanied by Kākinī, preceded by the letters from ka to ṭha,

1.85.s:
vinyaseddvādaśadalehṛdayasthe tvanāhate /
sadāśivaṃ śākinīṃ ca ṣoḍaśasvarapūrvakam //
1.85.d:
विन्यसेद्द्वादशदलेहृदयस्थे त्वनाहते ।
सदाशिवं शाकिनीं च षोडशस्वरपूर्वकम् ॥
1.85.m: One should place in the twelve-petalled [cakra], the anāhata situated in the heart, / Sadāśiva and Śākinī, preceded by the sixteen vowels.

1.85.s:
kaṇṭhasthe ṣoḍaśadale viśuddhākhye pravinyaset /
ājñācakre paraśivaṃ hākinīsaṃyutaṃ nyaset //
1.85.d:
कण्ठस्थे षोडशदले विशुद्धाख्ये प्रविन्यसेत् ।
आज्ञाचक्रे परशिवं हाकिनीसंयुतं न्यसेत् ॥
1.85.m: one should place them in the sixteen-petalled [lotus] in the throat named the Viśuddha; / in the ājñā-cakra, one should place Paraśiva accompanied by Hākinī.

1.85.s:
lakṣārṇapūvaṃ bhrūmadhyasaṃsthite 'timanohare /
tārādipañcamaṃ nyāsaṃ kuryātsarveṣṭasiddhaye //
1.85.d:
लक्षार्णपूवं भ्रूमध्यसंस्थिते ऽतिमनोहरे ।
तारादिपञ्चमं न्यासं कुर्यात्सर्वेष्टसिद्धये ॥
1.85.m: In that most captivating [centre] situated between the eyebrows, preceded by the syllables of lakṣa, / one should perform the fifth ritual placement beginning with Tārā for the attainment of all desires.

1.85.s:
aṣṭau vargānsvaradvandvapūrvakān bījasaṃyutān /
tārādyā nyāsapūrvāśca prayojyā aṣṭaśaktayaḥ //
1.85.d:
अष्टौ वर्गान्स्वरद्वन्द्वपूर्वकान् बीजसंयुतान् ।
ताराद्या न्यासपूर्वाश्च प्रयोज्या अष्टशक्तयः ॥
1.85.m: The eight groups preceded by pairs of vowels, combined with seed-syllables / and preceded by the Tārā-seed, are to be used in the ritual placement of the eight energies:

1.85.s:
tārāthogrā mahogrāpi vajrā kālī sarasvatī /
kāmeśvarī ca cāmuṇḍā ityaṣṭau tārikāḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.85.d:
ताराथोग्रा महोग्रापि वज्रा काली सरस्वती ।
कामेश्वरी च चामुण्डा इत्यष्टौ तारिकाः स्मृताः ॥
1.85.m: Tārā, then Ugrā, and Mahogrā, Vajrā, Kālī, Sarasvatī, / Kāmeśvarī, and Cāmuṇḍā—these are remembered as the eight saviouresses.

1.85.s:
brahmarandhre lalāṭe ca bhrūmadhye kaṇṭhadeśataḥ /
hṛdi nābhau phale mūlādhāre cetāḥ kramānnyaset //
1.85.d:
ब्रह्मरन्ध्रे ललाटे च भ्रूमध्ये कण्ठदेशतः ।
हृदि नाभौ फले मूलाधारे चेताः क्रमान्न्यसेत् ॥
1.85.m: At the aperture of Brahman, on the forehead, between the eyebrows, in the region of the throat, / in the heart, at the navel, on the sexual organ, and at the mūlādhāra—one should place these in order.

1.85.s:
aṅganyāsaṃ tataḥ kuryātpīṭhākhyaṃ sarvasiddhidam /
ādhāre kāmarūpākhyaṃ bījaṃ hrasvārṇapūrvakam //
1.85.d:
अङ्गन्यासं ततः कुर्यात्पीठाख्यं सर्वसिद्धिदम् ।
आधारे कामरूपाख्यं बीजं ह्रस्वार्णपूर्वकम् ॥
1.85.m: Then one should perform the ritual placement of the limbs called that of the sacred seats, which grants all perfections: / at the base, the seed-syllable named Kāmarūpa, preceded by short vowels;

1.85.s:
hṛdi jālandharaṃ bījaṃ dīrghapūrvaṃ pravinyaset /
lalāṭe pūrṇagiryākhyaṃ kavargādyaṃ nyasetsudhīḥ //
1.85.d:
हृदि जालन्धरं बीजं दीर्घपूर्वं प्रविन्यसेत् ।
ललाटे पूर्णगिर्याख्यं कवर्गाद्यं न्यसेत्सुधीः ॥
1.85.m: in the heart, the wise man should place the seed-syllable Jālandhara, preceded by long vowels; / on the forehead, that named Pūrṇagiri, beginning with the ka-group;

1.85.s:
uḍḍīyānaṃ cavargādyaṃ keśasandhau pravinyaset /
kaṇṭhe tu mathurāpīṭhaṃ daśama yādikaṃ nyaset //
1.85.d:
उड्डीयानं चवर्गाद्यं केशसन्धौ प्रविन्यसेत् ।
कण्ठे तु मथुरापीठं दशम यादिकं न्यसेत् ॥
1.85.m: at the hairline, one should place Uḍḍīyāna, beginning with the ca-group; / and in the throat, one should place the sacred seat Mathurā, [beginning with] the tenth syllable, ya and so on.

1.85.s:
ṣoḍhā nyāsastu tārāyāḥ prokto 'bhīṣṭapradāyakaḥ /
hṛdi śrīmadekajaṭāṃ tāriṇīṃ śirasi nyaset //
1.85.d:
षोढा न्यासस्तु तारायाः प्रोक्तो ऽभीष्टप्रदायकः ।
हृदि श्रीमदेकजटां तारिणीं शिरसि न्यसेत् ॥
1.85.m: The sixfold ritual placement of Tārā is declared as granting desires: / one should place the glorious Ekajaṭā on the heart, and Tāriṇī on the head;

1.85.s:
vajrodake śikhāṃ pātu ugratārāṃ tu varmaṇi /
mahogrā vatsare netre piṅgāgraikajaṭāstrake //
1.85.d:
वज्रोदके शिखां पातु उग्रतारां तु वर्मणि ।
महोग्रा वत्सरे नेत्रे पिङ्गाग्रैकजटास्त्रके ॥
1.85.m: 'May Vajrodakā protect the crest; and Ugratārā on the armour; / Mahogrā on the chest; [Tārā] on the eyes; Piṅgāgraikajaṭā on the weapon.'

1.85.s:
ṣaḍradīrgayuktamāyāyā etānyaṣṭau ṣaḍaṅgake /
aṅguṣṭhādiṣvaṅgulīṣu pūrvaṃ vinyasya yatnataḥ //
1.85.d:
षड्रदीर्गयुक्तमायाया एतान्यष्टौ षडङ्गके ।
अङ्गुष्ठादिष्वङ्गुलीषु पूर्वं विन्यस्य यत्नतः ॥
1.85.m: With the māyā-seed joined to the six long vowels, these eight in the six limbs: / having first placed them with care on the fingers, beginning with the thumb,

1.85.s:
tarjanīmadhyamābhyāṃ tu kṛtvā tālatrayaṃ tataḥ /
choṭikāmudrāyā kuryāddigbandhaṃ devatāṃ smaran //
1.85.d:
तर्जनीमध्यमाभ्यां तु कृत्वा तालत्रयं ततः ।
छोटिकामुद्राया कुर्याद्दिग्बन्धं देवतां स्मरन् ॥
1.85.m: and then clapping thrice with the forefinger and middle finger, / one should perform the boundary-sealing with the snapping mudrā while remembering the deity.

1.85.s:
vidyayā tārapuṭayā vyāpakaṃ saptadhā caret /
ugratārāṃ tato dhyāyetsadyo vāde 'tisiddhidām //
1.85.d:
विद्यया तारपुटया व्यापकं सप्तधा चरेत् ।
उग्रतारां ततो ध्यायेत्सद्यो वादे ऽतिसिद्धिदाम् ॥
1.85.m: Enclosed by the vidyā and the syllable oṃ, one should perform the pervasion seven times; / then one should meditate upon Ugratārā, who grants immediate great success in debate:

1.85.s:
layābdhāvaṃbujanmasthāṃ nīlābhāṃ divyabhūṣaṇām /
kambuṃ khaḍgaṃ kapālaṃ ca nīlābjaṃ dadhatīṃ karaiḥ //
1.85.d:
लयाब्धावंबुजन्मस्थां नीलाभां दिव्यभूषणाम् ।
कम्बुं खड्गं कपालं च नीलाब्जं दधतीं करैः ॥
1.85.m: standing on a lotus in the ocean of dissolution, shining blue, with divine ornaments, / holding a conch, a sword, a skull-cup, and a blue lotus in her hands;

1.85.s:
nāgaśreṣṭhālaṅkṛtāṅgīṃ raktanetratrayāṃ smaret /
japellakṣacatuṣkaṃ hi daśāṃśaṃ raktapadmakaiḥ //
1.85.d:
नागश्रेष्ठालङ्कृताङ्गीं रक्तनेत्रत्रयां स्मरेत् ।
जपेल्लक्षचतुष्कं हि दशांशं रक्तपद्मकैः ॥
1.85.m: her limbs adorned by the best of serpents, having three red eyes, he should meditate upon her. / He should indeed recite [the mantra] four hundred thousand times, and offer a tenth part in oblation with red lotuses,

1.85.s:
hunetkṣīrājyasaṃmiśraiḥ śaṅkhaṃ saṃsthāpya saṃjapet /
nārīṃ paśyanspṛśangacchanmahāniśi baliṃ caret //
1.85.d:
हुनेत्क्षीराज्यसंमिश्रैः शङ्खं संस्थाप्य संजपेत् ।
नारीं पश्यन्स्पृशन्गच्छन्महानिशि बलिं चरेत् ॥
1.85.m: mixed with milk and clarified butter; having established the conch, he should recite thoroughly. / Looking upon a woman, touching, and approaching, he should offer a sacrificial offering at midnight,

1.85.s:
śmaśāne śūnyasadane devāgāre 'tha nirjane /
parvate vanamadhye vā śavamāruhya mantravit //
1.85.d:
श्मशाने शून्यसदने देवागारे ऽथ निर्जने ।
पर्वते वनमध्ये वा शवमारुह्य मन्त्रवित् ॥
1.85.m: in a cremation ground, an abandoned house, a temple, or a deserted place, / on a mountain, or in the midst of a forest, mounting a corpse, the knower of mantras,

1.85.s:
samare śatrunihataṃ yadvā ṣāṇyāsikaṃ śiśum /
vidyāṃ sādhayataḥ śīghraṃ sādhitaivaṃ prasiddhyati //
1.85.d:
समरे शत्रुनिहतं यद्वा षाण्यासिकं शिशुम् ।
विद्यां साधयतः शीघ्रं साधितैवं प्रसिद्ध्यति ॥
1.85.m: [a corpse] slain by an enemy in battle, or else a six-month-old infant. / For one mastering the vidyā swiftly, when mastered in this way, it brings success.

1.85.s:
medhā prajñā prabhā vidyā dhīvṛttismṛtibuddhayaḥ /
viśveśvarīti saṃproktāḥ pīṭhasya nava śaktayaḥ //
1.85.d:
मेधा प्रज्ञा प्रभा विद्या धीवृत्तिस्मृतिबुद्धयः ।
विश्वेश्वरीति संप्रोक्ताः पीठस्य नव शक्तयः ॥
1.85.m:
Medhā, Prajñā, Prabhā, Vidyā, Dhī, Vṛtti, Smṛti, Buddhi,
and Viśveśvarī: these are declared as the nine powers of the seat.

1.85.s:
bhṛgumanvindusaṃyuktaṃ meghavartma sarasvatī /
yogapīṭhātmane hārddaṃ pīṭhasya manurīritaḥ //
1.85.d:
भृगुमन्विन्दुसंयुक्तं मेघवर्त्म सरस्वती ।
योगपीठात्मने हार्द्दं पीठस्य मनुरीरितः ॥
1.85.m:
Joined with Bhṛgu, Manu, and Bindu, the path of clouds, Sarasvatī,
followed by 'to the soul of the yoga-seat' ending in the heart-mantra: this is stated as the seat-mantra.

1.85.s:
dattvānenāsanaṃ mūrtiṃ mūlamantreṇa kalpayet /
pūjayedvidhivaddevīṃ tadvidhānamathocyate //
1.85.d:
दत्त्वानेनासनं मूर्तिं मूलमन्त्रेण कल्पयेत् ।
पूजयेद्विधिवद्देवीं तद्विधानमथोच्यते ॥
1.85.m:
Having offered the seat with this, he should fashion the form with the root-mantra.
He should worship the Goddess according to rule; that procedure is now explained:

1.85.s:
tāro māyā bhagaṃ brahmā jaṭe sūryaḥ sadīrghakam /
yakṣādhipataye tandrīsopanītaṃ baliṃ tataḥ //
1.85.d:
तारो माया भगं ब्रह्मा जटे सूर्यः सदीर्घकम् ।
यक्षाधिपतये तन्द्रीसोपनीतं बलिं ततः ॥
1.85.m:
The praṇava, Māyā, Bhaga, Brahmā, on matted locks the Sun with a long [vowel],
'to the lord of the Yakṣas, the slumber... the brought bali' then,

1.85.s:
gṛhayugmaṃ śivā svāhā balimantro 'yamīritaḥ /
dadyānnityaṃ baliṃ tena madhyarātre catuṣpathe //
1.85.d:
गृहयुग्मं शिवा स्वाहा बलिमन्त्रो ऽयमीरितः ।
दद्यान्नित्यं बलिं तेन मध्यरात्रे चतुष्पथे ॥
1.85.m:
a pair of Gṛha, Śivā, Svāhā: this is declared as the bali-mantra.
With it he should daily offer a bali at midnight at a crossroads.

1.85.s:
jaladānādikaṃ mantrairvidadhyāddaśabhistataḥ /
dhruvo vajrodake varma phaṭsaptārṇo jalagrahe //
1.85.d:
जलदानादिकं मन्त्रैर्विदध्याद्दशभिस्ततः ।
ध्रुवो वज्रोदके वर्म फट्सप्तार्णो जलग्रहे ॥
1.85.m:
Then, with ten mantras, he should perform the offering of water and the rest:
Dhruva, Vajrodake, Varma, Phaṭ: this seven-syllable [mantra] is for taking water.

1.85.s:
tārādyā vahnijāyāntā māyā hi kṣālane matā /
tāro māyāḥ bhṛguḥ karṇoviśuddhaṃ dharmavarmataḥ //
1.85.d:
ताराद्या वह्निजायान्ता माया हि क्षालने मता ।
तारो मायाः भृगुः कर्णोविशुद्धं धर्मवर्मतः ॥
1.85.m:
Māyā beginning with the praṇava and ending with the wife of Agni is held for washing.
The praṇava, Māyā, Bhṛgu, Karṇa, purified from Dharma-varma,

1.85.s:
sarvapāpāni śāmyante cheto netrayutaṃ jalam /
kalpāntanayanasvāhā mantra ācamane mataḥ //
1.85.d:
सर्वपापानि शाम्यन्ते छेतो नेत्रयुतं जलम् ।
कल्पान्तनयनस्वाहा मन्त्र आचमने मतः ॥
1.85.m:
'may all sins be subdued', Cheto, Jala joined with Netra,
ending in Kalpāntanayana-svāhā: this is considered the mantra for sipping water.

1.85.s:
dhruvo maṇidharītyante vajriṇyakṣiyutā mṛtiḥ /
kharividyāyugrijaśva sarvavānte bako 'bjavān //
1.85.d:
ध्रुवो मणिधरीत्यन्ते वज्रिण्यक्षियुता मृतिः ।
खरिविद्यायुग्रिजश्व सर्ववान्ते बको ऽब्जवान् ॥
1.85.m:
Dhruva, followed by Maṇidhari, Vajriṇī endowed with Akṣi, Mṛti,
Kharividyāyugrijaśva, after Sarvavā the heron endowed with a lotus,

1.85.s:
kāriṇyante dīrghavarma astraṃ vahnipriyāntimaḥ /
trayoviṃśativarṇātmā śikhāyā bandhane manuḥ //
1.85.d:
कारिण्यन्ते दीर्घवर्म अस्त्रं वह्निप्रियान्तिमः ।
त्रयोविंशतिवर्णात्मा शिखाया बन्धने मनुः ॥
1.85.m:
ending in Kāriṇī, the long armor, the weapon, and last the beloved of Agni:
consisting of twenty-three syllables, this is the mantra for tying the topknot.

1.85.s:
praṇavo rakṣayugalaṃ dīrghavarmāstraṭhadvayam /
navārṇenāmunā mantrī kuryādbhūmiviśodhanam //
1.85.d:
प्रणवो रक्षयुगलं दीर्घवर्मास्त्रठद्वयम् ।
नवार्णेनामुना मन्त्री कुर्याद्भूमिविशोधनम् ॥
1.85.m:
The praṇava, a pair of 'protect', the long armor, weapon, and a pair of Ṭha:
with this nine-syllable mantra the practitioner should purify the ground.

1.85.s:
nārānte sarvavighnānutsārayeti padaṃ tataḥ /
huṃ phaṭ svāhā guṇendvarṇo manurvighnanivāraṇam //
1.85.d:
नारान्ते सर्वविघ्नानुत्सारयेति पदं ततः ।
हुं फट् स्वाहा गुणेन्द्वर्णो मनुर्विघ्ननिवारणम् ॥
1.85.m:
Then, after Nārā, the words 'drive away all obstacles',
Huṃ Phaṭ Svāhā: this mantra of thirteen syllables wards off obstacles.

1.85.s:
māyābījaṃ japāpuṣpanibhaṃ nābhau viciṃyet /
tadutthenāgninā dehaṃ dahetsāddhasvapāpmanā //
1.85.d:
मायाबीजं जपापुष्पनिभं नाभौ विचिंयेत् ।
तदुत्थेनाग्निना देहं दहेत्साद्धस्वपाप्मना ॥
1.85.m:
He should visualize the Māyā seed-syllable resembling a hibiscus flower in the navel;
with the fire born from that, he should burn his body together with his sin.

1.85.s:
tārābījaṃ suvarṇābhaṃ cintayeddhṛdi mantravit /
pavanena tadutthena pāpabhasma kṣipedbhuvi //
1.85.d:
ताराबीजं सुवर्णाभं चिन्तयेद्धृदि मन्त्रवित् ।
पवनेन तदुत्थेन पापभस्म क्षिपेद्भुवि ॥
1.85.m:
The practitioner should visualize the Tārā seed-syllable, golden-hued, in the heart;
with the wind born from that, he should cast the ash of sin onto the earth.

1.85.s:
turīyaṃ candrakundābhaṃ bījaṃ dhyātvālalāṭataḥ /
tadutthasudhayāde haṃ svayaṃ vai devatānibham //
1.85.d:
तुरीयं चन्द्रकुन्दाभं बीजं ध्यात्वाललाटतः ।
तदुत्थसुधयादे हं स्वयं वै देवतानिभम् ॥
1.85.m:
Having meditated on the fourth seed-syllable resembling the moon and kunda flower at the forehead,
he himself, with the nectar born from that, becomes a body resembling the deity.

1.85.s:
anayā bhūtaśuddhyā tu devīsādṛśyamāpnuyāt /
tāro 'nanto bhaguḥ karṇo padmanābhayuto balī //
1.85.d:
अनया भूतशुद्ध्या तु देवीसादृश्यमाप्नुयात् ।
तारो ऽनन्तो भगुः कर्णो पद्मनाभयुतो बली ॥
1.85.m:
By this purification of elements, he attains resemblance to the Goddess.
The praṇava, Ananta, Bhagu, Karṇa, the mighty one joined with Padmanābha,

1.85.s:
khe vajrarekhe krodhākhyaṃ bījaṃ pāvakallabhā /
amunā dvādaśārṇena racayenmaṇḍalaṃ śubham //
1.85.d:
खे वज्ररेखे क्रोधाख्यं बीजं पावकल्लभा ।
अमुना द्वादशार्णेन रचयेन्मण्डलं शुभम् ॥
1.85.m:
Kha, Vajrarekhe, the seed-syllable named Krodha, and the beloved of Pāvaka:
with this twelve-syllable mantra he should fashion an auspicious maṇḍala.

1.85.s:
tāro yathāgatā nidrā sadṛkṣekabhṛgurviṣam /
sadīrghasmṛtirau sākṣau mahākālo bhagānvitaḥ //
1.85.d:
तारो यथागता निद्रा सदृक्षेकभृगुर्विषम् ।
सदीर्घस्मृतिरौ साक्षौ महाकालो भगान्वितः ॥
1.85.m:
The praṇava, Nidrā as arrived, Bhṛgu with eyes and Eka, Viṣa,
Smṛti with a long [vowel], Rau, endowed with eyes, Mahākāla joined with Bhaga,

1.85.s:
krodho 'straṃ manuvarṇo 'yaṃ manuḥ puṣpādiśodhane /
tāraḥ pāśaḥ parā svāhā pañcārṇaścittaśodhane //
1.85.d:
क्रोधो ऽस्त्रं मनुवर्णो ऽयं मनुः पुष्पादिशोधने ।
तारः पाशः परा स्वाहा पञ्चार्णश्चित्तशोधने ॥
1.85.m:
Krodha, weapon: this mantra consists of [sixteen] syllables for purifying flowers and the like.
The praṇava, Pāśa, Parā, Svāhā: a five-syllable [mantra] for purifying the mind.

1.85.s:
manavo daśa saṃproktā ardhyasthāpanamucyate /
seṃdubhyāṃ māsato māyā bhuvaṃ saṃsṛjya bhūgṛham //
1.85.d:
मनवो दश संप्रोक्ता अर्ध्यस्थापनमुच्यते ।
सेंदुभ्यां मासतो माया भुवं संसृज्य भूगृहम् ॥
1.85.m:
Ten mantras have been proclaimed; the placement of the offering-water is now explained:
With two moons, Māyā from the moon, having created the earth, an earth-enclosure,

1.85.s:
vṛtaṃ trikoṇasaṃyuktaṃ kuryānmaṇḍalamantrataḥ /
yajettatrādhāraśaktiṃ vahnimaṇḍalamadhyagām /
vahnimaṇḍalamabhyarcya mahāśaṅkhaṃ nidhāpayet //
1.85.d:
वृतं त्रिकोणसंयुक्तं कुर्यान्मण्डलमन्त्रतः ।
यजेत्तत्राधारशक्तिं वह्निमण्डलमध्यगाम् ।
वह्निमण्डलमभ्यर्च्य महाशङ्खं निधापयेत् ॥

1.85.s:
vāmakarṇenduyuktena phaḍantena vihāyasā /
prakṣālitaṃ bhṛgurdaṇḍī trimūrtīntuyutaṃ paṭhet //
1.85.d:
वामकर्णेन्दुयुक्तेन फडन्तेन विहायसा ।
प्रक्षालितं भृगुर्दण्डी त्रिमूर्तीन्तुयुतं पठेत् ॥
1.85.m:
Washed by space endowed with the left ear and moon, ending in Phaṭ,
he should recite Bhṛgu, the staff-bearer, endowed with the three forms and moon.

1.85.s:
tator'cayenmahāśaṅkhaṃ japanmantracatuṣṭayam /
dīrghatrayānvitā māyā kālī sṛṣṭiḥ sadīrghasaḥ //
1.85.d:
ततोर्ऽचयेन्महाशङ्खं जपन्मन्त्रचतुष्टयम् ।
दीर्घत्रयान्विता माया काली सृष्टिः सदीर्घसः ॥
1.85.m:
Then he should worship the great conch, reciting the four mantras:
Māyā endowed with three longs, Kālī, Sṛṣṭi, along with the long Sa,

1.85.s:
pratimāsaṃyutaṃ māsaṃ yavanaṃ hṛdayaṃ tataḥ /
ekādhaśārṇaḥ prathamo mahāśaṅkhārcane manuḥ //
1.85.d:
प्रतिमासंयुतं मासं यवनं हृदयं ततः ।
एकाधशार्णः प्रथमो महाशङ्खार्चने मनुः ॥
1.85.m:
joined with the image, month, Yavana, then Hṛdaya:
this eleven-syllable [mantra] is the first mantra in worshiping the great conch.

1.85.s:
haṃso haribhujaṅgeśayukto dīrghantrayenduyuk /
tāriṇyante kapālāya namonto dvādaśākṣaraḥ //
1.85.d:
हंसो हरिभुजङ्गेशयुक्तो दीर्घन्त्रयेन्दुयुक् ।
तारिण्यन्ते कपालाय नमोन्तो द्वादशाक्षरः ॥
1.85.m:
Haṃsa joined with Hari and the lord of serpents, endowed with three longs and moon,
ending in Tāriṇī, Kapālāya Namaḥ: this is the twelve-syllable mantra.

1.85.s:
svaṃ dīrghatrayamanvāḍhyameṣo vāmadaganvitaḥ /
lokapālāya hṛdayaṃ tṛtīyo 'yaṃ śivākṣaraḥ //
1.85.d:
स्वं दीर्घत्रयमन्वाढ्यमेषो वामदगन्वितः ।
लोकपालाय हृदयं तृतीयो ऽयं शिवाक्षरः ॥
1.85.m:
Sva endowed with three longs and Manu, a ram endowed with the left eye,
'to the world-guardian', Hṛdaya: this third [mantra] has the syllables of Śiva.

1.85.s:
māyāstrībījamarddhaiduyutaṃ svaṃ svargakhādimaḥ /
pālāya sarvādhārāya sarvaḥ sarvodbhavastathā //
1.85.d:
मायास्त्रीबीजमर्द्धैदुयुतं स्वं स्वर्गखादिमः ।
पालाय सर्वाधाराय सर्वः सर्वोद्भवस्तथा ॥
1.85.m:
Māyā, Strī seed-syllable joined with a half-moon, Sva, the first of sky and heaven,
to the protector, to the foundation of all, all, born of all, and so on,

1.85.s:
sarvaśuddhimayaśceti ṅeṃtāḥ sarvāsurāntikam /
rudhirā ratidīrghā ca vāyuḥ śubhrānilaḥ surā //
1.85.d:
सर्वशुद्धिमयश्चेति ङेंताः सर्वासुरान्तिकम् ।
रुधिरा रतिदीर्घा च वायुः शुभ्रानिलः सुरा ॥
1.85.m:
consisting of all purity, ending in the dative, near all demons,
Rudhirā, Rati with a long [vowel], Vāyu, white wind, wine,

1.85.s:
bhājanāya bhagī satyā vikapālāya hṛnmanuḥ /
turyo raseṣu varṇo 'yaṃ mahāśaṅkhaprapūjane //
1.85.d:
भाजनाय भगी सत्या विकपालाय हृन्मनुः ।
तुर्यो रसेषु वर्णो ऽयं महाशङ्खप्रपूजने ॥
1.85.m:
Bhājanāya, Bhagī, Satyā, Vikapālāya, the Hṛd mantra:
this fourth mantra of six syllables is used in worshiping the great conch.

1.85.s:
navārkamaṇḍalaṃ ceṣṭvā salilaṃ mūlamantrataḥ /
prapūrayetsudhābuddhyā gandhapuṣpākṣatādibhiḥ //
1.85.d:
नवार्कमण्डलं चेष्ट्वा सलिलं मूलमन्त्रतः ।
प्रपूरयेत्सुधाबुद्ध्या गन्धपुष्पाक्षतादिभिः ॥
1.85.m:
Having envisioned the circle of nine suns, he should fill the water with the root-mantra,
conceiving it as nectar, with fragrant paste, flowers, unhusked barley, and the like.

1.85.s:
mudrāṃ trikhaṇḍāṃ saṃdarśya pūjayeccandramaṇḍalam /
vāksatyapadmāgagane rephaānugrahabinduyuk //
1.85.d:
मुद्रां त्रिखण्डां संदर्श्य पूजयेच्चन्द्रमण्डलम् ।
वाक्सत्यपद्मागगने रेफआनुग्रहबिन्दुयुक् ॥
1.85.m:
Displaying the three-part mudrā, he should worship the moon-circle:
Speech, Satyā, Padmā, in the sky the letter Ra joined with grace and Bindu,

1.85.s:
mūlamantro vipaddhvaṃsamanusargasamanvitam /
aṣṭakṛtvo 'munā mantrī mantrayetprayato jalam //
1.85.d:
मूलमन्त्रो विपद्ध्वंसमनुसर्गसमन्वितम् ।
अष्टकृत्वो ऽमुना मन्त्री मन्त्रयेत्प्रयतो जलम् ॥
1.85.m:
the root-mantra joined with the mantra that destroys misfortune and with emission:
with this the practitioner, restrained, should consecrate the water eight times.

1.85.s:
māyayā madiśaṃ kṣiptvā khaṃ yoniṃ ca pradarśayet /
tatra vṛttāṣṭaṣaṭkoṇaṃ dhyātvā devīṃ vicintayet //
1.85.d:
मायया मदिशं क्षिप्त्वा खं योनिं च प्रदर्शयेत् ।
तत्र वृत्ताष्टषट्कोणं ध्यात्वा देवीं विचिन्तयेत् ॥
1.85.m:
Throwing wine with the Māyā-mantra, he should display the womb-mudrā and the sky;
having meditated there on a circular, six-cornered [figure] with eight [petals], he should envision the Goddess.

1.85.s:
pūrvoktāṃ pūjayettvenāṃ mūlenātha pratarpayet /
tarjanūmadhyamānāmākaniṣṭhābhirmaheśvarīm //
1.85.d:
पूर्वोक्तां पूजयेत्त्वेनां मूलेनाथ प्रतर्पयेत् ।
तर्जनूमध्यमानामाकनिष्ठाभिर्महेश्वरीम् ॥
1.85.m:
He should worship the previously mentioned Great Goddess and then offer libation with the root-mantra,
with the forefinger, middle finger, ring finger, and little finger,

1.85.s:
sāṃguṣṭhāniścuturvāraṃ mahāśaṅkhasthite jale /
khaṃrephamanubindvāḍhyāṃ bhṛgumanvinduyuktayā //
1.85.d:
सांगुष्ठानिश्चुतुर्वारं महाशङ्खस्थिते जले ।
खंरेफमनुबिन्द्वाढ्यां भृगुमन्विन्दुयुक्तया ॥
1.85.m:
with the thumb, four times, in the water placed in the great conch.
With [the syllable] endowed with Kha, Repha, Manu, and Bindu, joined with Bhṛgu, Manu, and the moon,

1.85.s:
dhruvādyena namontena tarpyādānandabhairavam /
tatastenārdhatoyena prokṣetpūjanasādhanam //
1.85.d:
ध्रुवाद्येन नमोन्तेन तर्प्यादानन्दभैरवम् ।
ततस्तेनार्धतोयेन प्रोक्षेत्पूजनसाधनम् ॥
1.85.m:
beginning with Dhruva and ending with Namaḥ, having offered libations to Ānandabhairava,
he should then sprinkle the implements of worship with half that water.

1.85.s:
yomimudrāṃ pradarśyāpi praṇamedbhavatāriṇīm /
vidhānamarghe saṃproktaṃ sarvasiddhipradāyakam //
1.85.d:
योमिमुद्रां प्रदर्श्यापि प्रणमेद्भवतारिणीम् ।
विधानमर्घे संप्रोक्तं सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायकम् ॥
1.85.m:
Displaying the womb-mudrā, he should also bow to the Savior from existence.
This procedure for the offering-water has been proclaimed, bestowing all accomplishments.

1.85.s:
pūrvokte pūjayetpīṭhe padme ṣaṭkoṇakarṇike /
dharāgṛhāvṛte ramye devīṃ ramyopacārakaiḥ //
1.85.d:
पूर्वोक्ते पूजयेत्पीठे पद्मे षट्कोणकर्णिके ।
धरागृहावृते रम्ये देवीं रम्योपचारकैः ॥
1.85.m:
On the previously mentioned seat, on a lotus with a pericarp of six corners,
enclosed in an earth-house, charming, he should worship the Goddess with delightful offerings.

1.85.s:
mahīgṛhe caturdikṣu gaṇeśādīnprapūjayet /
pāśāṅkuśau kapālaṃ ca triśūlaṃ dadhataṃ karaiḥ //
1.85.d:
महीगृहे चतुर्दिक्षु गणेशादीन्प्रपूजयेत् ।
पाशाङ्कुशौ कपालं च त्रिशूलं दधतं करैः ॥
1.85.m:
In the earth-house in the four directions he should worship Gaṇeśa and the others;
holding a noose, goad, skull-cup, and trident with his hands,

1.85.s:
alaṅkāracayopetaṃ gaṇeśaṃ prāktamarcayet /
kapālaśūle hastābhyāṃ dadhataṃ sarpabhūṣaṇam //
1.85.d:
अलङ्कारचयोपेतं गणेशं प्राक्तमर्चयेत् ।
कपालशूले हस्ताभ्यां दधतं सर्पभूषणम् ॥
1.85.m:
endowed with an array of ornaments, he should first worship Gaṇeśa in the east;
holding a skull-cup and spear with his hands, adorned with serpents,

1.85.s:
svayūthaveṣṭitaṃ ramyaṃ baṭukaṃ dakṣiṇer'cayet /
asiśūlakapālāni ḍamaruṃ dadhataṃ karaiḥ //
1.85.d:
स्वयूथवेष्टितं रम्यं बटुकं दक्षिणेर्ऽचयेत् ।
असिशूलकपालानि डमरुं दधतं करैः ॥
1.85.m:
surrounded by his own troop, charming, he should worship Baṭuka in the south;
holding a sword, spear, skull-cup, and hourglass-drum in his hands,

1.85.s:
kṛṣṇaṃ digaṃbaraṃ krūraṃ kṣetrapālaṃ ca paścime /
kapālaṃ ḍamaruṃ pāśaṃ liṅgaṃ śaṃbibhratīṃ karaiḥ //
1.85.d:
कृष्णं दिगंबरं क्रूरं क्षेत्रपालं च पश्चिमे ।
कपालं डमरुं पाशं लिङ्गं शंबिभ्रतीं करैः ॥
1.85.m:
dark, sky-clad, and fierce, he should worship Kṣetrapāla in the west;
holding a skull-cup, hourglass-drum, noose, and auspicious linga in her hands,

1.85.s:
adhyākanyā raktavastrā yoginīruttare yajet /
akṣobhyaṃ prayajenmūrdhni devyā mantraṛṣiṃ śubham //
1.85.d:
अध्याकन्या रक्तवस्त्रा योगिनीरुत्तरे यजेत् ।
अक्षोभ्यं प्रयजेन्मूर्ध्नि देव्या मन्त्रऋषिं शुभम् ॥
1.85.m:
a primeval maiden clad in red garments, he should worship the Yoginī in the north.
On the head of the Goddess, he should worship Akṣobhya, the auspicious seer of the mantra.

1.85.s:
akṣobhyaṃ vastrapuṣpaṃ ca pratīcchānavallabhā /
akṣobhyapūjane mantraḥ ṣaṭkogakam //
1.85.d:
अक्षोभ्यं वस्त्रपुष्पं च प्रतीच्छानवल्लभा ।
अक्षोभ्यपूजने मन्त्रः षट्कोगकम् ॥
1.85.m:
'O Akṣobhya, accept the garment and flower, Svāhā':
this is the six-limbed mantra in the worship of Akṣobhya.

1.85.s:
vairācanaṃ cāmitābhaṃ padmanābhibhidhaṃ tathā /
śaṅkhaṃ pāṇḍurasaṃjñaṃ ca digdaleṣu prapūjayet //
1.85.d:
वैराचनं चामिताभं पद्मनाभिभिधं तथा ।
शङ्खं पाण्डुरसंज्ञं च दिग्दलेषु प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.85.m:
Vairācana, Amitābha, the one named Padmanābhi,
Śaṅkha, and the one named Pāṇḍura: these he should worship on the directional petals.

1.85.s:
lābhakāṃ mānakāṃ caiva pāṇḍurāṃ tārakāṃ tathā /
vidiggatābjapatreṣu pūjayediṣṭasiddhaye //
1.85.d:
लाभकां मानकां चैव पाण्डुरां तारकां तथा ।
विदिग्गताब्जपत्रेषु पूजयेदिष्टसिद्धये ॥
1.85.m:
Lābhakā, Mānakā, Pāṇḍurā, and Tārakā:
he should worship these on the intermediate lotus petals for the attainment of desired ends.

1.85.s:
bindunāmādivarṇādyāḥ saṃbuddhyantāstathābhidhāḥ /
vrajapuṣpaṃ pratīcchāgnipriyāntāḥ praṇavādikāḥ //
1.85.d:
बिन्दुनामादिवर्णाद्याः संबुद्ध्यन्तास्तथाभिधाः ।
व्रजपुष्पं प्रतीच्छाग्निप्रियान्ताः प्रणवादिकाः ॥
1.85.m:
Beginning with Bindu and the initial phoneme of the name, ending in the vocative case,
'accept the thunderbolt-flower', ending in Svāhā and beginning with the praṇava.

1.85.s:
vairācanādi pūjāyāṃ manavaḥ parikīrtitāḥ /
bhūdharaśca caturdvārṣu padmāntakayamāntakau //
1.85.d:
वैराचनादि पूजायां मनवः परिकीर्तिताः ।
भूधरश्च चतुर्द्वार्षु पद्मान्तकयमान्तकौ ॥
1.85.m: The mantras are declared for the worship of Vairācana and the others. / Bhūdhara and, at the four gates, Padmāntaka and Yamāntaka,

1.85.s:
vidyāntakābhidhaḥ paścānnarāntaka imānyajet /
śakrādīṃścaiva vajrādīnprajapettadanantaram //
1.85.d:
विद्यान्तकाभिधः पश्चान्नरान्तक इमान्यजेत् ।
शक्रादींश्चैव वज्रादीन्प्रजपेत्तदनन्तरम् ॥
1.85.m: then the one named Vidyāntaka, and Narāntaka: one should worship these. / Immediately thereafter one should recite [the mantras of] Śakra and the others, and the vajra and the other [weapons].

1.85.s:
evaṃ saṃpūjayandevīṃ pāṇḍityaṃ dhanamadbhutam /
putrānpautrāñchubhāṃ kīrtiṃ labhate janavaśyatām //
1.85.d:
एवं संपूजयन्देवीं पाण्डित्यं धनमद्भुतम् ।
पुत्रान्पौत्राञ्छुभां कीर्तिं लभते जनवश्यताम् ॥
1.85.m: Worshipping the goddess thus, he obtains learning, wondrous wealth, / sons, grandsons, auspicious renown, and the subjugation of people.

1.85.s:
tāro māyā śrīmadakajaṭe nīlasarasvatī /
mahopratāre devāsaḥ sanetro gadiyugmakam //
1.85.d:
तारो माया श्रीमदकजटे नीलसरस्वती ।
महोप्रतारे देवासः सनेत्रो गदियुग्मकम् ॥
1.85.m: Tāra, māyā, ‘śrīmadakajaṭe nīlasarasvatī’, / ‘mahopratāre’, ‘devāsaḥ’, accompanied by netra, the pair of ‘gadi’,

1.85.s:
sarvadevapiśākarmo dīrghogrirmarusānmasa /
abhragumama jāḍyaṃ ca chedayadvitayaṃ ramā //
1.85.d:
सर्वदेवपिशाकर्मो दीर्घोग्रिर्मरुसान्मस ।
अभ्रगुमम जाड्यं च छेदयद्वितयं रमा ॥
1.85.m: ‘sarvadevapiśākarmo dīrghogrirmarusānmasa’, / ‘abhragumama’, and ‘jāḍyaṃ chedaya’ twice, ‘ramā’,

1.85.s:
māyāstrāgnipriyānto 'yaṃ dvipañcāśallipirmanuḥ /
anena nityaṃ pūjati'nvahaṃ devyai baliṃ haret //
1.85.d:
मायास्त्राग्निप्रियान्तो ऽयं द्विपञ्चाशल्लिपिर्मनुः ।
अनेन नित्यं पूजतिऽन्वहं देव्यै बलिं हरेत् ॥
1.85.m: ending with māyā, astra, and the beloved of Agni (svāhā)—this is the fifty-two-syllable mantra. / Worshipping constantly with this, he should offer a bali-oblation every day to the goddess.

1.85.s:
evaṃ siddhe manau mantrī prayogānvidadhāti ca /
jātamātrasya bālasya divasatritayādadhaḥ //
1.85.d:
एवं सिद्धे मनौ मन्त्री प्रयोगान्विदधाति च ।
जातमात्रस्य बालस्य दिवसत्रितयादधः ॥
1.85.m: When the mantra is thus mastered, the practitioner performs applications: / within three days of an infant’s birth,

1.85.s:
jihvāyāṃ vilikhenmantraṃ madhvājyābhyāṃ śalākayā /
suvarṇa kṛtayā yadvā mantrī dhavaladūrvayā //
1.85.d:
जिह्वायां विलिखेन्मन्त्रं मध्वाज्याभ्यां शलाकया ।
सुवर्ण कृतया यद्वा मन्त्री धवलदूर्वया ॥
1.85.m: the practitioner should write the mantra on its tongue with honey and ghee using a gold probe, / or alternatively with white dūrvā grass.

1.85.s:
gate 'ṣṭame 'bde bālo 'pi jāyate kaviradbutam /
tathāparairajeyo 'pi bhūpasaṃghairddhanārcitaḥ //
1.85.d:
गते ऽष्टमे ऽब्दे बालो ऽपि जायते कविरद्बुतम् ।
तथापरैरजेयो ऽपि भूपसंघैर्द्धनार्चितः ॥
1.85.m: When the eighth year has passed, that child becomes a wondrous poet; / likewise, though invincible to others, he is worshipped with wealth by multitudes of kings.

1.85.s:
uparāge datānīva naradārusarojale /
nirmāya kīlakaṃ tena tailamadhvamṛtairlikhet //
1.85.d:
उपरागे दतानीव नरदारुसरोजले ।
निर्माय कीलकं तेन तैलमध्वमृतैर्लिखेत् ॥
1.85.m: During an eclipse, in lotus-water with cedar-wood [paste] as if given [in ritual], / fashioning a peg, with that one should write with oil, honey, and nectar

1.85.s:
sarojinīdale mantraṃ veṣṭayenmātṛkākṣaraiḥ /
nikhāya tadalaṃ kuṇḍe caturasre samekhale //
1.85.d:
सरोजिनीदले मन्त्रं वेष्टयेन्मातृकाक्षरैः ।
निखाय तदलं कुण्डे चतुरस्रे समेखले ॥
1.85.m: the mantra on a lotus leaf, and surround it with the mātṛkā syllables. / Having buried that leaf in a four-sided fire-pit provided with girdles,

1.85.s:
saṃsthāpya pāvakaṃ tatra juhuyānmanunāmunā /
sahasraṃ raktapadmānāṃ dhenudugdhajalāplutam //
1.85.d:
संस्थाप्य पावकं तत्र जुहुयान्मनुनामुना ।
सहस्रं रक्तपद्मानां धेनुदुग्धजलाप्लुतम् ॥
1.85.m: and establishing the sacred fire there, one should offer with this mantra / a thousand red lotuses moistened with cow’s milk and water.

1.85.s:
homānte vivadhai ratnaiḥ palairapi baliṃ haret /
baliṃ mantreṇa vidhivadbalimantraḥ prakāśyate //
1.85.d:
होमान्ते विवधै रत्नैः पलैरपि बलिं हरेत् ।
बलिं मन्त्रेण विधिवद्बलिमन्त्रः प्रकाश्यते ॥
1.85.m: At the end of the fire oblation, he should offer a bali with various jewels and meat / according to rule with the bali mantra; the bali mantra is now revealed:

1.85.s:
tāraḥ padme yuga tandrī viyaddīrghaṃ ca lohitaḥ /
atrirviṣabhagārūḍho vadatpadmāvatīpadam //
1.85.d:
तारः पद्मे युग तन्द्री वियद्दीर्घं च लोहितः ।
अत्रिर्विषभगारूढो वदत्पद्मावतीपदम् ॥
1.85.m: Tāra, padme, the pair of tandrī, long viyat, and lohita, / Atri mounted on the viṣa-bhaga, the word ‘vadatpadmāvatī’,

1.85.s:
jhiṇṭīśāḍhyonilasvāhā ṣoḍaśārṇo balermanuḥ /
tato niśīthe ca baliṃ pūrvoktamanunā haret //
1.85.d:
झिण्टीशाढ्योनिलस्वाहा षोडशार्णो बलेर्मनुः ।
ततो निशीथे च बलिं पूर्वोक्तमनुना हरेत् ॥
1.85.m: jhiṇṭīśa combined with anila, and svāhā: this is the sixteen-syllable bali mantra. / Then at midnight he should offer the bali with the previously stated mantra.

1.85.s:
evaṃ kṛte paṇḍitānāṃ sa jayī kavirāḍ bhavet /
nivāso bhāratīlakṣmyorjanatārañjanakṣamaḥ //
1.85.d:
एवं कृते पण्डितानां स जयी कविराड् भवेत् ।
निवासो भारतीलक्ष्म्योर्जनतारञ्जनक्षमः ॥
1.85.m: When this is done, he becomes victorious among scholars, a king of poets, / an abode of Bhāratī and Lakṣmī, and able to delight people.

1.85.s:
śatābhijaptyā yo mantrī rocanāṃ mastāke dharet /
yaṃ yaṃ paśyati tasyāsau dāsavajjāyate kṣaṇāt //
1.85.d:
शताभिजप्त्या यो मन्त्री रोचनां मस्ताके धरेत् ।
यं यं पश्यति तस्यासौ दासवज्जायते क्षणात् ॥
1.85.m: The practitioner who places rocanā upon his head after reciting it a hundred times— / whomever he looks upon becomes like his servant in an instant.

1.85.s:
śmaśānāṅgāramāśritya pūrvāyāṃ kujavāsare /
tena matreṇa saṃveṣṭya nibaddhaṃ raktatantubhiḥ //
1.85.d:
श्मशानाङ्गारमाश्रित्य पूर्वायां कुजवासरे ।
तेन मत्रेण संवेष्ट्य निबद्धं रक्ततन्तुभिः ॥
1.85.m: Taking charcoal from a cremation ground on a Tuesday under the Pūrvā asterism, / surrounded with that mantra and bound with red threads,

1.85.s:
śatābhijaptaṃ mūlena nikṣipedvairiveśmani /
uccāṭayati saptāhātsakuṇṭubānvirodhinaḥ //
1.85.d:
शताभिजप्तं मूलेन निक्षिपेद्वैरिवेश्मनि ।
उच्चाटयति सप्ताहात्सकुण्टुबान्विरोधिनः ॥
1.85.m: recited over a hundred times with the root mantra, one should throw it into an enemy’s dwelling; / within seven days it expels the adversaries along with their families.

1.85.s:
kṣīrāḍhyayā niśāmantraṃ likhitvā pauruṣe 'sthani /
ravivāre niśīthinyāṃ sahasramabhimantrayet //
1.85.d:
क्षीराढ्यया निशामन्त्रं लिखित्वा पौरुषे ऽस्थनि ।
रविवारे निशीथिन्यां सहस्रमभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥
1.85.m: Writing the mantra with turmeric mixed with milk on a human bone / on a Sunday at midnight, one should consecrate it a thousand times.

1.85.s:
tatkṣiptaṃ śatrusadane maṇḍalādbhraṃśakaṃ bhavet /
kṣetre kṣiptaṃ sasyahānyojavahṛtturamālayet //
1.85.d:
तत्क्षिप्तं शत्रुसदने मण्डलाद्भ्रंशकं भवेत् ।
क्षेत्रे क्षिप्तं सस्यहान्योजवहृत्तुरमालयेत् ॥
1.85.m: Thrown into an enemy’s house, it causes his expulsion from the region; / thrown into a field, it destroys the crops, robs vigor, and ruins horses.

1.85.s:
ṣaṭkoṇāntarlikhenmūlaṃ sādhyārṇaṃ keśare svaraiḥ /
bāhye 'ṣṭavargayukpatraṃ padmabhūmiparāvṛtam //
1.85.d:
षट्कोणान्तर्लिखेन्मूलं साध्यार्णं केशरे स्वरैः ।
बाह्ये ऽष्टवर्गयुक्पत्रं पद्मभूमिपरावृतम् ॥
1.85.m: One should write the root mantra inside a hexagon, with the name of the target in the filaments surrounded by vowels, / and on the outside, [eight] petals endowed with the eight classes [of consonants], surrounded by a lotus-earth [figure].

1.85.s:
yantraṃ bhūrje jahurasairlikhetpūtāmbarāvṛtam /
paṭṭasūtreṇa sannaddhaṃ śiśukaṇṭhagataṃ dhruvam //
1.85.d:
यन्त्रं भूर्जे जहुरसैर्लिखेत्पूताम्बरावृतम् ।
पट्टसूत्रेण सन्नद्धं शिशुकण्ठगतं ध्रुवम् ॥
1.85.m: One should draw this yantra on birch bark with marking-nut juice, cover it with a purified cloth, / bind it with silk thread, and place it on a child’s neck; certainly,

1.85.s:
bhūtabhītiharaṃ vāmavāhau strīṇāṃ ca putradam /
nṛṇāṃ dakṣiṇabāhusthaṃ nirdhanānāṃ dhanapradam //
1.85.d:
भूतभीतिहरं वामवाहौ स्त्रीणां च पुत्रदम् ।
नृणां दक्षिणबाहुस्थं निर्धनानां धनप्रदम् ॥
1.85.m: it removes fear of spirits; on the left arm of women it grants sons; / placed on the right arm of men, it gives wealth to the destitute;

1.85.s:
jñānadaṃ jñānamicchūnāṃ rājñāṃ tu vijayapradam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde yakṣiṇīmantrabhedanirūpaṇaṃ nāma pañcāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.85.d:
ज्ञानदं ज्ञानमिच्छूनां राज्ञां तु विजयप्रदम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे यक्षिणीमन्त्रभेदनिरूपणं नाम पञ्चाशीतितमो ऽध्यायः
1.85.m:
it gives knowledge to those desiring knowledge, and victory to kings.

Thus ends the eighty-fifth chapter, entitled 'Determination of the Varieties of Yakṣiṇī Mantras', in the third quarter of the Great Narrative in the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.86.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
sarasvatyavatārāste kathitāḥ siddhidā nṛṇām /
atha lakṣmyavatārāṃste vakṣye sarvārthasiddhidān //
1.86.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
सरस्वत्यवतारास्ते कथिताः सिद्धिदा नृणाम् ।
अथ लक्ष्म्यवतारांस्ते वक्ष्ये सर्वार्थसिद्धिदान् ॥
1.86.m: Sanatkumāra said: / The incarnations of Sarasvatī that grant success to mortals have been declared to you; / now I shall speak to you of the incarnations of Lakṣmī that grant success in all aims.

1.86.s:
vāṇīmanmathaśaktyākhyaṃ bījatritayamīritam /
ṛṣiḥ syāddakṣiṇāmūrtiḥ paṅktiśchandaḥ prakīrtitam //
1.86.d:
वाणीमन्मथशक्त्याख्यं बीजत्रितयमीरितम् ।
ऋषिः स्याद्दक्षिणामूर्तिः पङ्क्तिश्छन्दः प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
1.86.m: The triad of seed-syllables named after Vāṇī, Manmatha, and Śakti is stated. / The seer is Dakṣiṇāmūrti, and the meter is declared to be paṅkti.

1.86.s:
devatā tripurā bālā madhyānte śaktibījake /
nābherāpādamādyaṃ tu nābhyantaṃ hṛdayātparam //
1.86.d:
देवता त्रिपुरा बाला मध्यान्ते शक्तिबीजके ।
नाभेरापादमाद्यं तु नाभ्यन्तं हृदयात्परम् ॥
1.86.m: The deity is Tripurā Bālā; in the middle and at the end are the śakti-seeds. / The first [extends] from the navel down to the feet; the second, from the heart down to the navel;

1.86.s:
mṛrdhno hradantaṃ tartīyaṃ kramāddeheṣu vinyaset /
ādyaṃ vāmakare dakṣakare tadubhayoḥ param //
1.86.d:
मृर्ध्नो ह्रदन्तं तर्तीयं क्रमाद्देहेषु विन्यसेत् ।
आद्यं वामकरे दक्षकरे तदुभयोः परम् ॥
1.86.m: the third, from the crown of the head to the heart: one should place these successively in the body. / The first in the left hand, [the second] in the right hand, and the subsequent one in both.

1.86.s:
punarbījatrayaṃ nyasya mūrdhni guhye ca vakṣasi /
nava yonpābhidhaṃ nyāse navakṛtvo manuṃ nyaset //
1.86.d:
पुनर्बीजत्रयं न्यस्य मूर्ध्नि गुह्ये च वक्षसि ।
नव योन्पाभिधं न्यासे नवकृत्वो मनुं न्यसेत् ॥
1.86.m: Having placed the triad of seed-syllables again on the crown, the private parts, and the chest, / in the ritual placement called the nine yonis, one should place the mantra nine times:

1.86.s:
karṇayościbuke nyasyecchaṅkhayormukhapaṅkaje /
netrayornāsikāyāṃ ca skandhayorudare tathā //
1.86.d:
कर्णयोश्चिबुके न्यस्येच्छङ्खयोर्मुखपङ्कजे ।
नेत्रयोर्नासिकायां च स्कन्धयोरुदरे तथा ॥
1.86.m: one should place it on the two ears, on the chin, on the two temples, on the lotus-face, / on the two eyes, on the nose, on the two shoulders, and on the belly;

1.86.s:
nyasetkūrparayornābhau jānunorliṅgamastake /
pādayorapi guhye ca pārśvayorhṛdaye punaḥ //
1.86.d:
न्यसेत्कूर्परयोर्नाभौ जानुनोर्लिङ्गमस्तके ।
पादयोरपि गुह्ये च पार्श्वयोर्हृदये पुनः ॥
1.86.m: one should place it on the two elbows, on the navel, on the two knees, on the head of the phallus, / on the two feet, on the private parts, on the two sides, and again on the heart,

1.86.s:
stanayoḥ kaṇṭhadeśe ca vāmāṅgādiṣu vinyaset /
vāgbhavādyāṃ ratiṃ guhye prītimatyādikāṃ hṛdi //
1.86.d:
स्तनयोः कण्ठदेशे च वामाङ्गादिषु विन्यसेत् ।
वाग्भवाद्यां रतिं गुह्ये प्रीतिमत्यादिकां हृदि ॥
1.86.m: on the two breasts, in the region of the neck, and on the left limbs and others. / One should place Rati preceded by the vāgbhava seed in the private parts, Prītimatī and the others in the heart;

1.86.s:
kāmabījādikānpaśyedbhūmadhye tu manobhavām /
punarvāgakātmamādyāstisraeva ca vinyaset //
1.86.d:
कामबीजादिकान्पश्येद्भूमध्ये तु मनोभवाम् ।
पुनर्वागकात्ममाद्यास्तिस्रएव च विन्यसेत् ॥
1.86.m: one should see those beginning with the kāma-seed [there], and Manobhavā between the eyebrows. / Again one should place the three beginning with the essence of speech;

1.86.s:
amṛteśīṃ ca yogeśīṃ viśvayoniṃ tṛtīyakām /
mūrdhniṃ vaktre hṛdi nyasyedguhye caraṇayorapi //
1.86.d:
अमृतेशीं च योगेशीं विश्वयोनिं तृतीयकाम् ।
मूर्ध्निं वक्त्रे हृदि न्यस्येद्गुह्ये चरणयोरपि ॥
1.86.m: Amṛteśī, Yogeśī, and the third, Viśvayoni, / one should place on the crown of the head, on the mouth, on the heart, on the private parts, and on the two feet.

1.86.s:
kāmeśī pañcabījāḍhyāṃ smarātpañcanyasetkramāt /
māyākāmau ca vāglakṣmī kāmeśī pañcabījakam //
1.86.d:
कामेशी पञ्चबीजाढ्यां स्मरात्पञ्चन्यसेत्क्रमात् ।
मायाकामौ च वाग्लक्ष्मी कामेशी पञ्चबीजकम् ॥
1.86.m: Endowed with five seed-syllables, one should place the five Kāmeśīs successively after Smara. / Māyā, Kāma, Vāc, and Lakṣmī: these are the five seeds of Kāmeśī.

1.86.s:
manobhavaśca makaradhvajakandarpamanmathāḥ /
kāmadevaḥ smaraḥ pañca kīrtitānyāsasiddhidāḥ //
1.86.d:
मनोभवश्च मकरध्वजकन्दर्पमन्मथाः ।
कामदेवः स्मरः पञ्च कीर्तितान्याससिद्धिदाः ॥
1.86.m: Manobhava, Makaradhvaja, Kandarpa, Manmatha, / and Kāmadeva: these five Smaras are declared to grant success in ritual placement.

1.86.s:
śiraḥpanmukhāguhyeṣu hṛdaye bāṇadevatāḥ /
drāviṇyādyāḥ kramānnyasyedvāṇeśībījapūrvakaḥ //
1.86.d:
शिरःपन्मुखागुह्येषु हृदये बाणदेवताः ।
द्राविण्याद्याः क्रमान्न्यस्येद्वाणेशीबीजपूर्वकः ॥
1.86.m: On the head, feet, face, private parts, and heart, one should place the arrow-deities, / Drāviṇī and the others, in order, preceded by the seed-syllables of the goddess of the arrows.

1.86.s:
drāndrīṃ klīñjūṃsa iti vaibāṇeśabījakaṃ ca kam /
drāviṇī kṣobhiṇī vaśīkaraṇyāṅkarṣaṇī tathā //
1.86.d:
द्रान्द्रीं क्लीञ्जूंस इति वैबाणेशबीजकं च कम् ।
द्राविणी क्षोभिणी वशीकरण्याङ्कर्षणी तथा ॥
1.86.m: ‘Drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ blūṃ saḥ’—these are the seed-syllables of the lord of the arrows. / Drāviṇī, Kṣobhiṇī, Vaśīkaraṇī, Ākarṣaṇī,

1.86.s:
saṃmohanī ca bāṇānāṃ devatāḥ pañca kīrtitāḥ /
tārtīyavāgmadhyagena kāmena syātṣaḍaṅgakam //
1.86.d:
संमोहनी च बाणानां देवताः पञ्च कीर्तिताः ।
तार्तीयवाग्मध्यगेन कामेन स्यात्षडङ्गकम् ॥
1.86.m: and Saṃmohanī: these are declared to be the five deities of the arrows. / With the Kāma-seed located between the third [seed] and speech, the six limbs are formed,

1.86.s:
ṣaḍdīrghasvarayuktena tato devīṃ vicintayet /
dhyāyedraktasarojasthāṃ raktavastrāṃ trilocanam //
1.86.d:
षड्दीर्घस्वरयुक्तेन ततो देवीं विचिन्तयेत् ।
ध्यायेद्रक्तसरोजस्थां रक्तवस्त्रां त्रिलोचनम् ॥
1.86.m: provided with the six long vowels. Then one should meditate on the goddess: / one should meditate on her as standing on a red lotus, wearing red garments, three-eyed,

1.86.s:
udyadarkanibhāṃ vidyāṃ mālābhayavarodvahām /
lakṣatrayaṃ japenmantraṃ daśāṃśaṃ kiṃśukodbhavaiḥ //
1.86.d:
उद्यदर्कनिभां विद्यां मालाभयवरोद्वहाम् ।
लक्षत्रयं जपेन्मन्त्रं दशांशं किंशुकोद्भवैः ॥
1.86.m: resembling the rising sun, bearing a book, a rosary, and the gestures of fearlessness and granting boons. / One should recite the mantra three hundred thousand times, and make a tenth part as a fire oblation with flowers

1.86.s:
puṣpairhayārijairvāpi juhuyānmadhurānvitaiḥ /
navayonyātmakaṃ yantraṃ bahiraṣṭadalāvṛtam //
1.86.d:
पुष्पैर्हयारिजैर्वापि जुहुयान्मधुरान्वितैः ।
नवयोन्यात्मकं यन्त्रं बहिरष्टदलावृतम् ॥
1.86.m: of kiṃśuka or oleander mixed with sweet substances. / A yantra consisting of nine yonis, surrounded on the outside by eight petals,

1.86.s:
kesareṣu svarānnyasyedvargānaṣṭaudaleṣvapi /
dalāgreṣu triśūlāni padma tu mātṛkāvṛtam //
1.86.d:
केसरेषु स्वरान्न्यस्येद्वर्गानष्टौदलेष्वपि ।
दलाग्रेषु त्रिशूलानि पद्म तु मातृकावृतम् ॥
1.86.m: one should place the vowels in the filaments, and the eight consonant classes on the petals; / on the petal-tips trident-figures, and the lotus surrounded by the mātṛkā letters.

1.86.s:
evaṃ vilikhite yantre pīṭhaśaktīḥ prapūjayet /
icchā jñānā kriyā caiva kāminī kāmadāyinī //
1.86.d:
एवं विलिखिते यन्त्रे पीठशक्तीः प्रपूजयेत् ।
इच्छा ज्ञाना क्रिया चैव कामिनी कामदायिनी ॥
1.86.m: When the yantra has been drawn in this manner, one should worship the powers of the ritual seat: / Icchā, Jñānā, Kriyā, Kāminī, Kāmadāyinī,

1.86.s:
ratī ratipriyā nandā manonmanyapi coditāḥ /
pīṭhaśaktīrimā iṣṭvā pīṭhaṃ tanmanunā diśet //
1.86.d:
रती रतिप्रिया नन्दा मनोन्मन्यपि चोदिताः ।
पीठशक्तीरिमा इष्ट्वा पीठं तन्मनुना दिशेत् ॥
1.86.m: Ratī, Ratipriyā, Nandā, and Manonmanī are proclaimed. / Having worshipped these powers of the ritual seat, one should assign the seat with its mantra:

1.86.s:
vyomapūrve tu tārtīyaṃ sadāśivamahāpadam /
pretapadmāsanaṃ ṅeṃtaṃ namontaḥ pīṭhamantrakaḥ //
1.86.d:
व्योमपूर्वे तु तार्तीयं सदाशिवमहापदम् ।
प्रेतपद्मासनं ङेंतं नमोन्तः पीठमन्त्रकः ॥
1.86.m: Viyat preceding the third, the great word Sadāśiva, / pretapadmāsana ending in the dative case, and namaḥ at the end: this is the seat mantra.

1.86.s:
ṣoḍaśārṇastato mūrtauṃ kḷptāyāṃ mūlamantrataḥ /
āvāhya prajapeddevīmupacāraiḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ //
1.86.d:
षोडशार्णस्ततो मूर्तौं कॢप्तायां मूलमन्त्रतः ।
आवाह्य प्रजपेद्देवीमुपचारैः पृथग्विधैः ॥
1.86.m: Then, having fashioned the sixteen-syllabled [form] upon the physical image by means of the root-mantra, / having invoked the Goddess, he should recite with various kinds of ritual services.

1.86.s:
devīmiṣṭvā madhyayonau trikoṇe ratipūrvikām /
vāmakoṇe ratiṃ dakṣe prītimagre manobhavām //
1.86.d:
देवीमिष्ट्वा मध्ययोनौ त्रिकोणे रतिपूर्विकाम् ।
वामकोणे रतिं दक्षे प्रीतिमग्रे मनोभवाम् ॥
1.86.m: Having worshiped the Goddess in the central triangle, [along with] the ones beginning with Rati in the triangle: / Rati in the left angle, Prīti in the right, and Manobhavā in front;

1.86.s:
yonyantarvahnikoṇādavaṅgānyagnervidikṣvapi /
madhyayomerhahiḥ pūrvādiṣu cāgre smarānapi //
1.86.d:
योन्यन्तर्वह्निकोणादवङ्गान्यग्नेर्विदिक्ष्वपि ।
मध्ययोमेर्हहिः पूर्वादिषु चाग्रे स्मरानपि ॥
1.86.m: inside the triangle, beginning from the southeast corner, the limbs [of the mantra] in the intermediate directions of Agni, / and outside the central triangle in the east and other [cardinal points], and in front the [forms of] Smara;

1.86.s:
vāṇadevīstadvadeva śaktīraṣṭasu yoniṣu /
subhagākhyā bhāgā paścāttṛtīyā bhagasarpiṇī //
1.86.d:
वाणदेवीस्तद्वदेव शक्तीरष्टसु योनिषु ।
सुभगाख्या भागा पश्चात्तृतीया भगसर्पिणी ॥
1.86.m: likewise the Bāṇadevīs, the Śaktis in the eight triangles: / the one named Subhagā, then Bhāgā, the third Bhagasarpiṇī,

1.86.s:
bhagamālā tathānaṅgā nagādyā kusumāparā /
anaṅgamekhalānaṅgamadanetyaṣṭaśaktayaḥ //
1.86.d:
भगमाला तथानङ्गा नगाद्या कुसुमापरा ।
अनङ्गमेखलानङ्गमदनेत्यष्टशक्तयः ॥
1.86.m: Bhagamālā, likewise Anaṅgā, Nagādyā, Kusumā another, / Anaṅgamekhalā, and Anaṅgamadanā—these are the eight Śaktis.

1.86.s:
padmakeśaragā brāhmī mukhāḥ patreṣu bhairavāḥ /
dīrghādyā mātaraḥ pūjyā hrasvādyāścāṣṭabhairavāḥ //
1.86.d:
पद्मकेशरगा ब्राह्मी मुखाः पत्रेषु भैरवाः ।
दीर्घाद्या मातरः पूज्या ह्रस्वाद्याश्चाष्टभैरवाः ॥
1.86.m: The [Mātṛkās] headed by Brāhmī residing on the lotus filaments, and the Bhairavas on the petals: / the Mothers beginning with long [vowels] are to be worshiped, and the eight Bhairavas beginning with short [vowels].

1.86.s:
dalāgreṣvaṣṭapīṭhāni kāmarūpākhyamādimam /
malayaṃ kollagiryyākhyaṃ cauhārākhyaṃ kulāntakam //
1.86.d:
दलाग्रेष्वष्टपीठानि कामरूपाख्यमादिमम् ।
मलयं कोल्लगिर्य्याख्यं चौहाराख्यं कुलान्तकम् ॥
1.86.m: At the tips of the petals are the eight seats: the first named Kāmarūpa, / Malaya, the one called Kollagiri, the one called Cauhāra, Kulāntaka,

1.86.s:
jālandharaṃ tathonnāsaṃ koṭapīṭhamathāṣṭamam /
bhūgṛhe daśadikṣvarceddhetukaṃ tripurāntakam //
1.86.d:
जालन्धरं तथोन्नासं कोटपीठमथाष्टमम् ।
भूगृहे दशदिक्ष्वर्चेद्धेतुकं त्रिपुरान्तकम् ॥
1.86.m: Jālandhara, likewise Unnāsa, and Koṭapīṭha as the eighth. / In the earth-enclosure, in the ten directions, one should worship Hetuka, Tripurāntaka,

1.86.s:
vaitālamagni jihvaṃ ca kamalāntakālinau /
ekapādaṃ bhīmarūpaṃ vimalaṃ hāṭakeśvaram //
1.86.d:
वैतालमग्नि जिह्वं च कमलान्तकालिनौ ।
एकपादं भीमरूपं विमलं हाटकेश्वरम् ॥
1.86.m: Vetāla, Agnijihva, and the pair Kamalāntaka and Kālin, / Ekapāda, Bhīmarūpa, Vimala, and Hāṭakeśvara,

1.86.s:
śakrādyānāyudhaiḥ sārddhaṃ svasvadikṣu samarcayet /
tadbahirdikṣu baṭukaṃ yoginīṃ kṣetranāyakam //
1.86.d:
शक्राद्यानायुधैः सार्द्धं स्वस्वदिक्षु समर्चयेत् ।
तद्बहिर्दिक्षु बटुकं योगिनीं क्षेत्रनायकम् ॥
1.86.m: along with Śakra and the others with their weapons, in their respective directions, one should worship. / Outside that, in the directions, [one should worship] Baṭuka, Yoginī, Kṣetranāyaka,

1.86.s:
gaṇeśaṃ vidiśāsvarcedvasūnsūryācchivāṃstathā /
bhūtāṃścetthaṃ bhajanbālāmīśaḥ syāddhanavidyayoḥ //
1.86.d:
गणेशं विदिशास्वर्चेद्वसून्सूर्याच्छिवांस्तथा ।
भूतांश्चेत्थं भजन्बालामीशः स्याद्धनविद्ययोः ॥
1.86.m: and Gaṇeśa; in the intermediate directions one should worship the Vasus, Sūryas, Śivas, / and the Bhūtas. Worshiping Bālā in this way, one becomes a master of wealth and knowledge.

1.86.s:
raktāṃbhojairhuternāryovaśyāḥ syuḥ sarṣapairnṛpāḥ /
nandyāvartai rājavṛkṣaiḥ kundaiḥ pāṭalacaṃpakaiḥ //
1.86.d:
रक्तांभोजैर्हुतेर्नार्योवश्याः स्युः सर्षपैर्नृपाः ।
नन्द्यावर्तै राजवृक्षैः कुन्दैः पाटलचंपकैः ॥
1.86.m: By offering red lotuses, women become subjugated; by mustard seeds, kings. / With nandyāvarta flowers, rājavṛkṣa, kunda, pāṭala, and campaka,

1.86.s:
puṣpairbilvaphalairvāpi homāllakṣmīḥ sthirā bhavet /
apamṛtyuṃ jayenmantrī guḍūcyā dugdhayuktayā //
1.86.d:
पुष्पैर्बिल्वफलैर्वापि होमाल्लक्ष्मीः स्थिरा भवेत् ।
अपमृत्युं जयेन्मन्त्री गुडूच्या दुग्धयुक्तया ॥
1.86.m: with flowers or with bilva fruits, from fire oblation wealth becomes firm. / The mantra-practitioner conquers premature death with guḍūcī mixed with milk;

1.86.s:
yathoktadūrvāhomena nīrogāyuḥ samaśnute /
jñānaṃ kavitvaṃ labhate candrāgurusurairhutaiḥ //
1.86.d:
यथोक्तदूर्वाहोमेन नीरोगायुः समश्नुते ।
ज्ञानं कवित्वं लभते चन्द्रागुरुसुरैर्हुतैः ॥
1.86.m: by fire oblation of dūrvā grass as prescribed, he enjoys a healthy life. / He gains knowledge and poetic skill through oblations of moon-plant, aguru, and devdāru.

1.86.s:
palāśapuṣpairvāksiddhirannāptiścānnahomataḥ /
surabhikṣīradadhyaktāṃllājānhutvā rujo jayet //
1.86.d:
पलाशपुष्पैर्वाक्सिद्धिरन्नाप्तिश्चान्नहोमतः ।
सुरभिक्षीरदध्यक्तांल्लाजान्हुत्वा रुजो जयेत् ॥
1.86.m: With palāśa flowers comes mastery of speech, and obtaining food through fire oblation of food. / Having offered parched grain smeared with milk and curd from a fragrant cow, he conquers diseases.

1.86.s:
raktacandanakarpūrakarcūrāgururocanāḥ /
candanaṃ keśaraṃ māṃsīṃ kramādbhāgainiṃyojayet //
1.86.d:
रक्तचन्दनकर्पूरकर्चूरागुरुरोचनाः ।
चन्दनं केशरं मांसीं क्रमाद्भागैनिंयोजयेत् ॥
1.86.m: Red sandalwood, camphor, karcūra, aguru, rocanā, / white sandalwood, saffron, and jaṭāmāṃsī: he should combine them in sequence with parts

1.86.s:
bhūmicandraikanandābdhidiksaptanigamonmitaiḥ /
śmaśāne kṛṣṇabhūtasya niśi nīhārapāthasā //
1.86.d:
भूमिचन्द्रैकनन्दाब्धिदिक्सप्तनिगमोन्मितैः ।
श्मशाने कृष्णभूतस्य निशि नीहारपाथसा ॥
1.86.m: measuring earth [one], moon [one], one [one], bliss [nine], ocean [four], direction [ten], seven, and Veda [four], / in a cremation ground, in the dark [fortnight] of the fourteenth day, at night, with dew-water.

1.86.s:
kumāryā peṣayettāni mantreṇāthābhimantrya ca /
vidaddhyāttilakaṃ tena darśanādvaśayejjanān //
1.86.d:
कुमार्या पेषयेत्तानि मन्त्रेणाथाभिमन्त्र्य च ।
विदद्ध्यात्तिलकं तेन दर्शनाद्वशयेज्जनान् ॥
1.86.m: He should have a maiden grind them, and having consecrated [the paste] with the mantra, / he should apply a sectarian mark with it: by sight he can subjugate people,

1.86.s:
gajasiṃhādibhūtāni rākṣasāñchākinīrapi /
prayojanānāṃ siddhyai tu devyāḥ śāpaṃ nivartya ca //
1.86.d:
गजसिंहादिभूतानि राक्षसाञ्छाकिनीरपि ।
प्रयोजनानां सिद्ध्यै तु देव्याः शापं निवर्त्य च ॥
1.86.m: beings such as elephants and lions, Rākṣasas, and Śākinīs. / But for the attainment of objectives, having reversed the curse of the Goddess,

1.86.s:
vidhāyotkīlitāṃ paścājjapamasya samācaret /
yo japedādime bīje varāhabhṛgupāvakān //
1.86.d:
विधायोत्कीलितां पश्चाज्जपमस्य समाचरेत् ।
यो जपेदादिमे बीजे वराहभृगुपावकान् ॥
1.86.m: and having performed the unpinning, he should thereafter practice the recitation of this [mantra]. / One who recites Varāha, Bhṛgu, and Pāvaka in the first seed-syllable,

1.86.s:
madhyamādau nabhohaṃsau madhyamānte tu pāvakam /
ādāvante ca tārtūyakramātsvaṃ dhūmraketanam //
1.86.d:
मध्यमादौ नभोहंसौ मध्यमान्ते तु पावकम् ।
आदावन्ते च तार्तूयक्रमात्स्वं धूम्रकेतनम् ॥
1.86.m: Nabhas and Haṃsa in the beginning of the middle, and Pāvaka at the end of the middle, / and at the beginning and the end the third, respectively one's own [seed] and Dhūmraketana,

1.86.s:
evaṃ japtvā śataṃ vidyā śāpahīnā phalapradā /
yadvādye carame bīje naiva rephaṃ viyojayet //
1.86.d:
एवं जप्त्वा शतं विद्या शापहीना फलप्रदा ।
यद्वाद्ये चरमे बीजे नैव रेफं वियोजयेत् ॥
1.86.m: having recited thus a hundred times, the vidyā becomes free from curses and bestows results. / Or else, in the first and the last seed-syllable, one should not apply the letter 'r'.

1.86.s:
śāpoddhāraprakāro 'nyo yadvāyaṃ kīrtito budhaiḥ /
ādyamādyaṃ hi tārtīyaṃ kāmaḥ kāmo 'tha vāgbhavam //
1.86.d:
शापोद्धारप्रकारो ऽन्यो यद्वायं कीर्तितो बुधैः ।
आद्यमाद्यं हि तार्तीयं कामः कामो ऽथ वाग्भवम् ॥
1.86.m: Or this other method of removing the curse is proclaimed by the wise: / the first, the first, indeed the third, Kāma, Kāma, then Vāgbhava,

1.86.s:
antyamantthamanaṅgaśca navārṇaḥ kīrtito manuḥ /
japto 'yaṃ śatadhā śāpaṃ bālāyā vinivartayet //
1.86.d:
अन्त्यमन्त्थमनङ्गश्च नवार्णः कीर्तितो मनुः ।
जप्तो ऽयं शतधा शापं बालाया विनिवर्तयेत् ॥
1.86.m: the last, the last, and Anaṅga—the nine-syllabled mantra is proclaimed. / Recited a hundred times, this reverses the curse of Bālā.

1.86.s:
caitanyāhlādinūmantrau japtau niṣkīlatākarau /
trisvarāścetanaṃ mantrī dharaḥ śāntiranugrahaḥ //
1.86.d:
चैतन्याह्लादिनूमन्त्रौ जप्तौ निष्कीलताकरौ ।
त्रिस्वराश्चेतनं मन्त्री धरः शान्तिरनुग्रहः ॥
1.86.m: The two mantras of Caitanyā and Āhlādinī, when recited, produce the unpinning. / The three vowels, Cetana, the mantra-practitioner, Dhara, Śānti, Anugraha,

1.86.s:
tārādihṛdayāntaḥ syātkāma āhlādinīmanuḥ /
tathā trayāṇāṃ bījānāṃ dīpanairmanubhistribhiḥ //
1.86.d:
तारादिहृदयान्तः स्यात्काम आह्लादिनीमनुः ।
तथा त्रयाणां बीजानां दीपनैर्मनुभिस्त्रिभिः ॥
1.86.m: beginning with Tāra and ending with 'hṛdaya', Kāma is the Āhlādinī mantra. / Likewise, having thoroughly illuminated the three seed-syllables / with the three illuminating mantras at first, he should recite them for attaining desires:

1.86.s:
sudīptāni vidhāyādau japettānīṣṭasiddhaye /
vadayugmaṃ sadīrghāṃbu smṛtivālāvanaṅgatau //
1.86.d:
सुदीप्तानि विधायादौ जपेत्तानीष्टसिद्धये ।
वदयुग्मं सदीर्घांबु स्मृतिवालावनङ्गतौ ॥
1.86.m: 'vada' twice, accompanied by long water, Smṛti, Vālā, to Anaṅga,

1.86.s:
satyaḥ sanetro nastādṛgvā vāgvarṇādyadīpinī /
klinne kledini vaikuṇṭho dīrghaṃ svaṃ sadyagontimaḥ //
1.86.d:
सत्यः सनेत्रो नस्तादृग्वा वाग्वर्णाद्यदीपिनी ।
क्लिन्ने क्लेदिनि वैकुण्ठो दीर्घं स्वं सद्यगोन्तिमः ॥
1.86.m: Satya, with eyes, 'na' such, or the first illuminator of the speech syllable. / 'klinne kledini', Vaikuṇṭha, long self, Sadyoga, the last,

1.86.s:
nidrā sacandrā kurvīta śivārṇā madhyadīpinī /
tāro mokṣaṃ ca kurute nāyaṃ varṇāsyadīpinī //
1.86.d:
निद्रा सचन्द्रा कुर्वीत शिवार्णा मध्यदीपिनी ।
तारो मोक्षं च कुरुते नायं वर्णास्यदीपिनी ॥
1.86.m: Nidrā with the moon, one should make; the Śiva syllable is the middle illuminator. / Tāra, and makes liberation, Nāyā—this is the illuminator of the syllable mouth.

1.86.s:
dīpinīmantarā bālā sādhitāpi na siddhyati /
vāgantyakāmān prajayedarīṇā kṣobhahetave //
1.86.d:
दीपिनीमन्तरा बाला साधितापि न सिद्ध्यति ।
वागन्त्यकामान् प्रजयेदरीणा क्षोभहेतवे ॥
1.86.m: Without the illuminator, Bālā, even if accomplished, is not perfected. / One should recite the speech, last, and Kāma [seeds] for the agitation of enemies;

1.86.s:
kāmavāgantyabījāni trailokyasya vaśīkṛtau /
kāmāntyavāṇībījāni muktaye niyato japet //
1.86.d:
कामवागन्त्यबीजानि त्रैलोक्यस्य वशीकृतौ ।
कामान्त्यवाणीबीजानि मुक्तये नियतो जपेत् ॥
1.86.m: the Kāma, speech, and last seed-syllables are for the subjugation of the three worlds; / the Kāma, last, and speech seed-syllables, disciplined, he should recite for liberation.

1.86.s:
pūjāraṃbhe tu bālāyāstrividhānarcayedgurūn /
divyaughaścaiva siddhaugho mānavaugha iti tridhā //
1.86.d:
पूजारंभे तु बालायास्त्रिविधानर्चयेद्गुरून् ।
दिव्यौघश्चैव सिद्धौघो मानवौघ इति त्रिधा ॥
1.86.m: At the beginning of the worship of Bālā, he should worship the three kinds of gurus: / the divine group, the accomplished group, and the human group—thus three kinds.

1.86.s:
paraprakāśaḥ parame śānaḥ paraśivastathā /
kāmeśvarastato mokṣaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ kāmo 'mṛtoṃ'timaḥ //
1.86.d:
परप्रकाशः परमे शानः परशिवस्तथा ।
कामेश्वरस्ततो मोक्षः षष्ठः कामो ऽमृतोंऽतिमः ॥
1.86.m: Paraprakāśa, Parameśāna, likewise Paraśiva, / Kāmeśvara, then Mokṣa, the sixth Kāma, and Amṛta the last:

1.86.s:
ete daptaiva divyaughā ānandapadapaścimāḥ /
īśānākhyastatpuruṣo 'ghorākhyovāmadevakaḥ //
1.86.d:
एते दप्तैव दिव्यौघा आनन्दपदपश्चिमाः ।
ईशानाख्यस्तत्पुरुषो ऽघोराख्योवामदेवकः ॥
1.86.m: these are the seven of the divine group, ending with the word 'ānanda'. / The one named Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, the one named Aghora, Vāmadevaka,

1.86.s:
sadyojāta ime pañca siddhaudhākhyāḥ smṛtā mune /
mānavaughāḥ parijñeyāḥ svaguroḥ sampradāyataḥ //
1.86.d:
सद्योजात इमे पञ्च सिद्धौधाख्याः स्मृता मुने ।
मानवौघाः परिज्ञेयाः स्वगुरोः सम्प्रदायतः ॥
1.86.m: and Sadyojāta: these five are remembered as the accomplished group, O sage. / The human groups are to be known from the tradition of one's own guru.

1.86.s:
navayonyātmake yantre vilikhenmadhyayonitaḥ /
prādakṣiṇyena bījāni trivāraṃ sādhakottamaḥ //
1.86.d:
नवयोन्यात्मके यन्त्रे विलिखेन्मध्ययोनितः ।
प्रादक्षिण्येन बीजानि त्रिवारं साधकोत्तमः ॥
1.86.m: In a diagram consisting of nine triangles, beginning from the central triangle, / the excellent practitioner should write the seed-syllables clockwise three times.

1.86.s:
trīṃstrīnvarṇāṃstu gāyatryā aṣṭapatreṣu saṃlikhet /
bahirmātṛkayā'veṣṭya tadbahirbhūpuradvayam //
1.86.d:
त्रींस्त्रीन्वर्णांस्तु गायत्र्या अष्टपत्रेषु संलिखेत् ।
बहिर्मातृकयाऽवेष्ट्य तद्बहिर्भूपुरद्वयम् ॥
1.86.m: He should write three letters each of the gāyatrī on the eight petals, / having encircled on the outside with the Mātṛkā, and outside that two earth-enclosures,

1.86.s:
kāmabījalasatkoṇana vyatibhinnaṃ parasparam /
patre traipuramākhyātaṃ japasaṃpātasādhitam //
1.86.d:
कामबीजलसत्कोणन व्यतिभिन्नं परस्परम् ।
पत्रे त्रैपुरमाख्यातं जपसंपातसाधितम् ॥
1.86.m: mutually intersected, with corners shining with the Kāma seed-syllable. / It is declared as the Traipura [yantra] on a sheet, accomplished by the infusion of recitation;

1.86.s:
bāhunā vidhṛte dadyāddhanaṃ kīrtiṃ sukhaṃ sutān /
kāmānte tripurā devī vidmahe kaviṣaṃ bhahim //
1.86.d:
बाहुना विधृते दद्याद्धनं कीर्तिं सुखं सुतान् ।
कामान्ते त्रिपुरा देवी विद्महे कविषं भहिम् ॥
1.86.m: worn on the arm, it bestows wealth, fame, happiness, and sons. / After Kāma, 'tripurāyai devyai vidmahe', 'kaviṣaṃbhahim',

1.86.s:
bakaḥ khaḍgī samārūḍhaḥ sanetro 'gniśca dhīmahi /
tatra klinne pracodānte yādityeṣā prakīrtitā //
1.86.d:
बकः खड्गी समारूढः सनेत्रो ऽग्निश्च धीमहि ।
तत्र क्लिन्ने प्रचोदान्ते यादित्येषा प्रकीर्तिता ॥
1.86.m: Baka, holding a sword, mounted, with eyes, and Agni 'dhīmahi'; / there 'tannaḥ klinne pracodayāt'—thus is proclaimed

1.86.s:
gāyatrī traipurā sarsiddhidā surasevitā /
atha lakṣmyavatāro 'nyaḥ kīrtyate siddhido nṛṇām //
1.86.d:
गायत्री त्रैपुरा सर्सिद्धिदा सुरसेविता ।
अथ लक्ष्म्यवतारो ऽन्यः कीर्त्यते सिद्धिदो नृणाम् ॥
1.86.m: the Traipurā Gāyatrī, bestowing all accomplishments, served by the gods. / Now another incarnation of Lakṣmī is proclaimed, bestowing accomplishments upon men.

1.86.s:
vedādirgirijā padmā manyatho hṛdayaṃ bhṛguḥ /
bhagavati māheśvarī ṅente 'nnapūrṇe dahanāṅganā //
1.86.d:
वेदादिर्गिरिजा पद्मा मन्यथो हृदयं भृगुः ।
भगवति माहेश्वरी ङेन्ते ऽन्नपूर्णे दहनाङ्गना ॥
1.86.m: The beginning of the Veda, Girijā, Padmā, Manmatha, hṛdaya, Bhṛgu, / 'bhagavati māheśvari', ending in the dative case 'annapūrṇe', and the wife of fire [svāhā]:

1.86.s:
proktā viṃśativarṇeyaṃ vidyā syāddruhiṇo muniḥ /
dhṛtiśchando 'nnapūrṇeśī devatā parikīrtitā //
1.86.d:
प्रोक्ता विंशतिवर्णेयं विद्या स्याद्द्रुहिणो मुनिः ।
धृतिश्छन्दो ऽन्नपूर्णेशी देवता परिकीर्तिता ॥
1.86.m: this twenty-syllabled vidyā is proclaimed; its sage is Druhiṇa, / the meter is Dhṛti, and the deity is proclaimed to be the ruler Annapūrṇā.

1.86.s:
ṣaḍdīrghāḍhyena hṛllekhābī'jena syātṣaḍaṅgakam /
mukhanāsākṣikarṇāṃsagudeṣu navasu nyaset //
1.86.d:
षड्दीर्घाढ्येन हृल्लेखाबीऽजेन स्यात्षडङ्गकम् ।
मुखनासाक्षिकर्णांसगुदेषु नवसु न्यसेत् ॥
1.86.m: With the Hṛllekhā seed-syllable enriched with the six long [vowels] is the six-limbed [rite]. / He should place the nine words in the nine: mouth, nose, eyes, ears, shoulders, and anus.

1.86.s:
padāni nava tadvarṇasaṃkhyedānīmudīryate /
bhūmicandradharaikākṣivedābdhiyugabāhubhiḥ //
1.86.d:
पदानि नव तद्वर्णसंख्येदानीमुदीर्यते ।
भूमिचन्द्रधरैकाक्षिवेदाब्धियुगबाहुभिः ॥
1.86.m: The number of letters of those nine words is now spoken: / earth [one], moon [one], bearer [one], one [one], eye [two], Veda [four], ocean [four], pair [two], arms [two]—

1.86.s:
padasaṃkhyāmitā varṇaistato dhyāyetsureśvarīm /
svarṇābhāṅgāṃ trinayanāṃ vastrālaṅkāraśobhitām //
1.86.d:
पदसंख्यामिता वर्णैस्ततो ध्यायेत्सुरेश्वरीम् ।
स्वर्णाभाङ्गां त्रिनयनां वस्त्रालङ्कारशोभिताम् ॥
1.86.m: measured by these syllable counts for each word. Then he should meditate on the ruler of goddesses: / her limbs having the radiance of gold, three-eyed, adorned with garments and ornaments,

1.86.s:
bhūramāsaṃ yutāṃ devīṃ svarṇāmatrakarāṃbujām /
lakṣaṃ japo 'yutaṃ homo ghṛtāktacaruṇā tathā //
1.86.d:
भूरमासं युतां देवीं स्वर्णामत्रकरांबुजाम् ।
लक्षं जपो ऽयुतं होमो घृताक्तचरुणा तथा ॥
1.86.m: the Goddess accompanied by Bhū and Ramā, holding a golden vessel in her lotus hands. / One hundred thousand recitations, and a fire oblation of ten thousand with sacrificial offering smeared with ghee;

1.86.s:
jayādinavaśaktayāḍhye pīṭhe pūjā samīritā /
trikoṇā vedapatrāṣṭapatraṣoḍaśapatrake //
1.86.d:
जयादिनवशक्तयाढ्ये पीठे पूजा समीरिता ।
त्रिकोणा वेदपत्राष्टपत्रषोडशपत्रके ॥
1.86.m: the worship is proclaimed on the seat enriched with the nine Śaktis beginning with Jayā, / in [a diagram of] a triangle, four petals, eight petals, and sixteen petals.

1.86.s:
bhūpureṇa yute yantre pradadyānmāyayā manum /
agnyādikoṇatritaye śivavārāhamādhavān //
1.86.d:
भूपुरेण युते यन्त्रे प्रदद्यान्मायया मनुम् ।
अग्न्यादिकोणत्रितये शिववाराहमाधवान् ॥
1.86.m: In the yantra endowed with an earth-city, one should impart the mantra along with Māyā. / In the triad of corners beginning with fire, [one should worship] Śiva, Varāha, and Mādhava;

1.86.s:
acaryayetsvasvamantraistu procyante manavastu te /
praṇavo manucandrāḍhyaṃ gaganaṃ hṛdayaṃ śivā //
1.86.d:
अचर्ययेत्स्वस्वमन्त्रैस्तु प्रोच्यन्ते मनवस्तु ते ।
प्रणवो मनुचन्द्राढ्यं गगनं हृदयं शिवा ॥
1.86.m: One should worship them with their respective mantras; those mantras are now stated: / The praṇava, the sky-letter endowed with the fourteen vowels and the crescent moon, the heart, Śivā,

1.86.s:
mārutaḥ śivamantro 'yaṃ saptārṇaḥ śivapūjane /
vārāhanārāyaṇayormantrau pūrvamudīrayet //
1.86.d:
मारुतः शिवमन्त्रो ऽयं सप्तार्णः शिवपूजने ।
वाराहनारायणयोर्मन्त्रौ पूर्वमुदीरयेत् ॥
1.86.m: And the wind-letter: this seven-syllable Śiva-mantra is used in the worship of Śiva. / One should state the two mantras of Varāha and Nārāyaṇa as mentioned before.

1.86.s:
ṣaḍaṅgāni tato 'bhyarcya vāme dakṣe dharāṃ ramām /
yajetsvasvamanubhyāṃ tu tāvucyete munīśvara //
1.86.d:
षडङ्गानि ततो ऽभ्यर्च्य वामे दक्षे धरां रमाम् ।
यजेत्स्वस्वमनुभ्यां तु तावुच्येते मुनीश्वर ॥
1.86.m: Then, having worshipped the six limbs, one should worship the Earth on the left and Ramā on the right / With their respective mantras; O lord of sages, both are now spoken:

1.86.s:
annaṃ mahyannamityuktvā me dehyannādhiporṇakāḥ /
nayemamannaṃ prāṇānte dāpayānalasuṃdarī //
1.86.d:
अन्नं मह्यन्नमित्युक्त्वा मे देह्यन्नाधिपोर्णकाः ।
नयेममन्नं प्राणान्ते दापयानलसुंदरी ॥
1.86.m: Having said, 'annam mahyannam,' [then] 'me dehyannādhiporṇakāḥ' / 'Nayemamannaṃ prāṇānte,' [and] 'dāpayānalasundarī'—

1.86.s:
