dvāviṃśatyakṣaro mantro bhūmīṣṭau bhūmisaṃpuṭaḥ /
lakṣmīṣṭau śrīpuṭo vipra snṛtirlabhanucandrayuk //
1.86.d:
द्वाविंशत्यक्षरो मन्त्रो भूमीष्टौ भूमिसंपुटः ।
लक्ष्मीष्टौ श्रीपुटो विप्र स्नृतिर्लभनुचन्द्रयुक् ॥
1.86.m: This twenty-two-syllable mantra is encased with the earth-bīja for Earth's desire. / For Lakṣmī's desire, it is encased with the śrī-bīja, O twice-born one. The letter sa, combined with ṛ, la, bha, the sun, and the moon,

1.86.s:
bhuvo bījamiti proktaṃ śrībījaṃ prāgudāhṛtam /
mantrādisthacaturbījapūrvikāḥ paripūjayet //
1.86.d:
भुवो बीजमिति प्रोक्तं श्रीबीजं प्रागुदाहृतम् ।
मन्त्रादिस्थचतुर्बीजपूर्विकाः परिपूजयेत् ॥
1.86.m: Is declared to be the earth-bīja; the śrī-bīja was stated previously. / Preceded by the four bījas placed at the beginning of the mantra, one should fully worship

1.86.s:
śaktīścatasro vedāsre parā ca bhuvaneśvarī /
kamalā subhagā cati brāhmyādyā aṣṭapatragāḥ //
1.86.d:
शक्तीश्चतस्रो वेदास्रे परा च भुवनेश्वरी ।
कमला सुभगा चति ब्राह्म्याद्या अष्टपत्रगाः ॥
1.86.m: The four Śaktis in the four corners: Parā, Bhuvaneśvarī, / Kamalā, and Subhagā; and Brāhmī and the others situated in the eight petals.

1.86.s:
ṣoḍaśāre smṛte cava mānadātuṣṭipuṣṭayaḥ /
prītī ratirhnīḥ śrīścāpi svadhā svāhā daśamyatha //
1.86.d:
षोडशारे स्मृते चव मानदातुष्टिपुष्टयः ।
प्रीती रतिर्ह्नीः श्रीश्चापि स्वधा स्वाहा दशम्यथ ॥
1.86.m: In the sixteen spokes are traditionally taught: Mānadā, Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, / Prīti, Rati, Hrī, Śrī, Svadhā, Svāhā, and as the tenth,

1.86.s:
jyotsnā haimavatī chāyā pūrṇimā saṃhatistathā /
amāvāsyeti saṃpūjyā mantreśe prāṇapūrvikā //
1.86.d:
ज्योत्स्ना हैमवती छाया पूर्णिमा संहतिस्तथा ।
अमावास्येति संपूज्या मन्त्रेशे प्राणपूर्विका ॥
1.86.m: Jyotsnā, Haimavatī, Chāyā, Pūrṇimā, Saṃhati, / And Amāvāsyā; these should be worshipped in the master of mantras preceded by Prāṇa.

1.86.s:
bhūpure lokapālāḥ syustadastrāṇi tadagrataḥ /
itthaṃ japādibhiḥ siddhe mantre 'smindhanasaṃcayaiḥ //
1.86.d:
भूपुरे लोकपालाः स्युस्तदस्त्राणि तदग्रतः ।
इत्थं जपादिभिः सिद्धे मन्त्रे ऽस्मिन्धनसंचयैः ॥
1.86.m: In the earth-city are the world-guardians, with their weapons before them. / When this mantra is accomplished in this way through recitation and other rites, through heaps of wealth

1.86.s:
kuberasadṛśo mantrī jāyate janavanditaḥ /
atha lakṣmyavatāro 'nyaḥ kīrtyate munisattama //
1.86.d:
कुबेरसदृशो मन्त्री जायते जनवन्दितः ।
अथ लक्ष्म्यवतारो ऽन्यः कीर्त्यते मुनिसत्तम ॥
1.86.m: The practitioner of mantras becomes equal to Kubera and praised by people. / Now, another incarnation of Lakṣmī is celebrated, O best of sages:

1.86.s:
praṇavaḥ śāntiraruṇākriyāḍhyācandrabhūṣitāḥ /
bagalāmukhasarvānte indhikāhrādinīyutā //
1.86.d:
प्रणवः शान्तिररुणाक्रियाढ्याचन्द्रभूषिताः ।
बगलामुखसर्वान्ते इन्धिकाह्रादिनीयुता ॥
1.86.m: The praṇava, Śānti, Aruṇā combined with Kriyā, adorned with the moon; / At the end of the whole phrase 'bagalāmukha,' endowed with Indhikā and Hrādinī;

1.86.s:
pītājarāyukpratiṣṭhā punardīrdhodasaṃyutā /
vācaṃ mukhaṃ padaṃ staṃbhayānte jihvāpadaṃ vadet //
1.86.d:
पीताजरायुक्प्रतिष्ठा पुनर्दीर्धोदसंयुता ।
वाचं मुखं पदं स्तंभयान्ते जिह्वापदं वदेत् ॥
1.86.m: Endowed with Pītā and Ajarā, Pratiṣṭhā, again joined with the long water-vowel; / One should say, 'vācaṃ mukhaṃ padaṃ stambhaya,' and at the end of the word 'jihvā,'

1.86.s:
kīlayeti ca buddhiṃ vināśayānte svabījakam /
tāro 'gnisuṃdarī mantro bagalāyāḥ prakīrtitaḥ //
1.86.d:
कीलयेति च बुद्धिं विनाशयान्ते स्वबीजकम् ।
तारो ऽग्निसुंदरी मन्त्रो बगलायाः प्रकीर्तितः ॥
1.86.m: And 'kīlaya,' and at the end of 'buddhiṃ vināśaya,' its own bīja, / The tāra, and the fire-beauty [svāhā]: this is declared to be the mantra of Bagalā.

1.86.s:
munistu nāradaśchado bṛhatī bagalāmukhī /
devatā netrapañceṣunavapañcadigarṇakaiḥ //
1.86.d:
मुनिस्तु नारदश्छदो बृहती बगलामुखी ।
देवता नेत्रपञ्चेषुनवपञ्चदिगर्णकैः ॥
1.86.m: The sage is Nārada; the metre is Bṛhatī; Bagalāmukhī / Is the deity. With two, five, five, nine, five, and ten syllables,

1.86.s:
aṅgāni kalpayitvā ca dhyāyetpītāmbarāṃ tataḥ /
svarṇāsanasthāṃ hemābhāṃ staṃbhinīminduśekharām //
1.86.d:
अङ्गानि कल्पयित्वा च ध्यायेत्पीताम्बरां ततः ।
स्वर्णासनस्थां हेमाभां स्तंभिनीमिन्दुशेखराम् ॥
1.86.m: Having arranged the limbs, one should then meditate upon her dressed in yellow garments, / Seated on a golden throne, having a golden luster, the paralyzer, wearing the crescent moon on her crest,

1.86.s:
dadhatīṃ mudgaraṃ pāśaṃ vajraṃ ca rasanāṃ karaiḥ /
evaṃ dhyātvājapellakṣamayutaṃ caṃpakodbhavaiḥ //
1.86.d:
दधतीं मुद्गरं पाशं वज्रं च रसनां करैः ।
एवं ध्यात्वाजपेल्लक्षमयुतं चंपकोद्भवैः ॥
1.86.m: Holding a club, a noose, a thunderbolt, and a tongue with her hands. / Having meditated thus, one should recite [the mantra] a hundred thousand times, and make ten thousand oblations

1.86.s:
kusumairjuhuyātpīṭhe bālāyāḥ pūjayedimām /
candanāgurucandrādyaiḥ pūjārthaṃ yantramālikhet //
1.86.d:
कुसुमैर्जुहुयात्पीठे बालायाः पूजयेदिमाम् ।
चन्दनागुरुचन्द्राद्यैः पूजार्थं यन्त्रमालिखेत् ॥
1.86.m: With flowers born of the campaka tree; on the seat of Bālā one should worship her. / For the sake of worship, one should draw a yantra with sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, and other substances;

1.86.s:
trikoṇaṣaḍdalāṣṭāsraṣoḍaśāre yajedimām /
maṅgalā staṃbhinī caiva jṛṃbhiṇī mohinī tathā //
1.86.d:
त्रिकोणषड्दलाष्टास्रषोडशारे यजेदिमाम् ।
मङ्गला स्तंभिनी चैव जृंभिणी मोहिनी तथा ॥
1.86.m: In a triangle, six petals, eight corners, and sixteen spokes, one should worship her: / Maṅgalā, Stambhinī, Jṛmbhiṇī, Mohinī,

1.86.s:
vaśyā calā balākā ca bhūdharā kalmaṣābhidhā /
dhātrī ca kalanā kālakarṣiṇī bhrāmikāpi ca //
1.86.d:
वश्या चला बलाका च भूधरा कल्मषाभिधा ।
धात्री च कलना कालकर्षिणी भ्रामिकापि च ॥
1.86.m: Vaśyā, Calā, Balākā, Bhūdharā, Kalmaṣā, / Dhātrī, Kalanā, Kālakarṣiṇī, Bhrāmikā,

1.86.s:
mandagāpi ca bhogasthā bhāvikā ṣoḍaśī smṛtā /
bhūgṛhasya caturdikṣu pūrvādiṣu yajetkramāt //
1.86.d:
मन्दगापि च भोगस्था भाविका षोडशी स्मृता ।
भूगृहस्य चतुर्दिक्षु पूर्वादिषु यजेत्क्रमात् ॥
1.86.m: Mandagā, Bhogasthā, and Bhāvikā is remembered as the sixteenth. / In the four directions of the earth-enclosure, beginning with the east, one should worship in order:

1.86.s:
gaṇeśaṃ baṭukaṃ cāpi yoginīḥ kṣetrapālakam /
indrādīṃśca tato bāhye nijāyudhasamanvitān //
1.86.d:
गणेशं बटुकं चापि योगिनीः क्षेत्रपालकम् ।
इन्द्रादींश्च ततो बाह्ये निजायुधसमन्वितान् ॥
1.86.m: Gaṇeśa, Baṭuka, the Yoginīs, and the field-protector, / And outside them Indra and the others, accompanied by their own weapons.

1.86.s:
itthaṃ siddhe manau mantrī staṃbhayeddevatādikān /
pītavastrapadāsīnaḥ pītamālyānulepanaḥ //
1.86.d:
इत्थं सिद्धे मनौ मन्त्री स्तंभयेद्देवतादिकान् ।
पीतवस्त्रपदासीनः पीतमाल्यानुलेपनः ॥
1.86.m: When the mantra is thus accomplished, the practitioner can paralyze deities and others. / Seated on a yellow cloth, wearing yellow garlands and unguents,

1.86.s:
pītapuṣpairyajeddevīṃ haridrotthasrajā japet /
pītāṃ dhyāyanbhagavatīṃ payomadhye 'yutaṃ japet //
1.86.d:
पीतपुष्पैर्यजेद्देवीं हरिद्रोत्थस्रजा जपेत् ।
पीतां ध्यायन्भगवतीं पयोमध्ये ऽयुतं जपेत् ॥
1.86.m: One should worship the goddess with yellow flowers and recite with a rosary made of turmeric. / Meditating on the yellow Goddess, one should recite ten thousand times while in water.

1.86.s:
trimadhvā jyatilairhemo nṝṇāṃ vaśyakaro mataḥ /
madhuratritayāktaiḥ syādākarṣo lavarṇairdhruvam //
1.86.d:
त्रिमध्वा ज्यतिलैर्हेमो नॄणां वश्यकरो मतः ।
मधुरत्रितयाक्तैः स्यादाकर्षो लवर्णैर्ध्रुवम् ॥
1.86.m: Fire oblation with the three sweets, ghee, and sesame seeds is held to subjugate men. / Attraction [of others] will certainly occur with salt smeared with the three sweets.

1.86.s:
tailābhyaktairnimbapatrairhemo vidveṣakārakaḥ /
tālaloṇaharidrābhirdviṣāṃ saṃstaṃbhanaṃ bhavet //
1.86.d:
तैलाभ्यक्तैर्निम्बपत्रैर्हेमो विद्वेषकारकः ।
ताललोणहरिद्राभिर्द्विषां संस्तंभनं भवेत् ॥
1.86.m: Fire oblation with neem leaves smeared with oil causes hatred [between enemies]. / Total paralysis of enemies is effected with yellow orpiment, salt, and turmeric.

1.86.s:
āgāradhūmaṃ rājīśca māhiṣaṃ guggulaṃ niśi /
śmaśāne pāvake hutvā nāśayedacirādarīn //
1.86.d:
आगारधूमं राजीश्च माहिषं गुग्गुलं निशि ।
श्मशाने पावके हुत्वा नाशयेदचिरादरीन् ॥
1.86.m: Having offered into fire soot from the house, black mustard, buffalo ghee, and bdellium at night / In a cremation-ground fire, one quickly destroys enemies.

1.86.s:
garuto gṛdhrakākānāṃ kaṭutailaṃ vibhītakam /
gṛhadhūmaṃ citāvahnau hutvā proccāṭayedripūn //
1.86.d:
गरुतो गृध्रकाकानां कटुतैलं विभीतकम् ।
गृहधूमं चितावह्नौ हुत्वा प्रोच्चाटयेद्रिपून् ॥
1.86.m: Having offered vulture and crow feathers, mustard oil, bibhītaka [seeds], / And house-soot into the funeral-pyre fire, one drives away enemies.

1.86.s:
dūvārguḍūcīlājānyo madhuratritayānvitān /
juhoti so 'khilān rogān śamayeddarśanādapi //
1.86.d:
दूवार्गुडूचीलाजान्यो मधुरत्रितयान्वितान् ।
जुहोति सो ऽखिलान् रोगान् शमयेद्दर्शनादपि ॥
1.86.m: One who makes fire oblation of dūrvā grass, guḍūcī, and puffed rice combined with the three sweets / Calms all diseases, even by his mere sight.

1.86.s:
parvatāgre mahāraṇye nadīsaṃge śivālaye /
brahmacaryarato lakṣaṃ japedakhilasiddhaye //
1.86.d:
पर्वताग्रे महारण्ये नदीसंगे शिवालये ।
ब्रह्मचर्यरतो लक्षं जपेदखिलसिद्धये ॥
1.86.m: On a mountain peak, in a great forest, at a river confluence, or in a temple of Śiva, / Devoted to celibacy, one should recite a hundred thousand times for all accomplishments.

1.86.s:
eka varṇagavīdugdhaṃ śarkarāmadhusaṃyutam /
triśataṃ mantritaṃ pītaṃ hanyādviṣaparābhavam //
1.86.d:
एक वर्णगवीदुग्धं शर्करामधुसंयुतम् ।
त्रिशतं मन्त्रितं पीतं हन्याद्विषपराभवम् ॥
1.86.m: The milk of a cow of single color combined with sugar and honey, / Consecrated three hundred times with the mantra and drunk, destroys the defeat caused by poison.

1.86.s:
śvetapālaśakāṣṭhena racite ramyapādake /
alaktarañjite lakṣaṃ mantrayenmanunāmunā //
1.86.d:
श्वेतपालशकाष्ठेन रचिते रम्यपादके ।
अलक्तरञ्जिते लक्षं मन्त्रयेन्मनुनामुना ॥
1.86.m: On charming wooden sandals crafted from the wood of the white palāśa / And colored with red lac, one should recite this mantra a hundred thousand times.

1.86.s:
tadārūḍhaḥ pumān gacchatkṣaṇena śatayojanam /
pāradaṃ ca śilāṃ tālaṃ piṣṭaṃ madhusamanvitam //
1.86.d:
तदारूढः पुमान् गच्छत्क्षणेन शतयोजनम् ।
पारदं च शिलां तालं पिष्टं मधुसमन्वितम् ॥
1.86.m: A man mounted upon them traverses a hundred yojanas in an instant. / Mercury, realgar, and yellow orpiment ground together with honey,

1.86.s:
manunā mantrayellakṣaṃ liṃpettenākhilāṃ tanum /
adṛśyaḥ syānnṛṇāmeṣa āścaryyaṃ dṛśyatāmidam //
1.86.d:
मनुना मन्त्रयेल्लक्षं लिंपेत्तेनाखिलां तनुम् ।
अदृश्यः स्यान्नृणामेष आश्चर्य्यं दृश्यतामिदम् ॥
1.86.m: One should consecrate with the mantra a hundred thousand times, and smear it over one's entire body; / He becomes invisible to men; behold this wonder!

1.86.s:
ṣaṭkoṇaṃ vilikhadbījaṃ sādhyanāmānvitaṃ manoḥ /
haritālaniśācūrṇairunmatturasasaṃyutaiḥ //
1.86.d:
षट्कोणं विलिखद्बीजं साध्यनामान्वितं मनोः ।
हरितालनिशाचूर्णैरुन्मत्तुरससंयुतैः ॥
1.86.m: Drawing a six-pointed figure, [one should write] the bīja along with the name of the one to be subdued in the mantra / With the powder of yellow orpiment and turmeric mixed with the juice of the thorn apple,

1.86.s:
śeṣākṣaraiḥ samānītaṃ dharāgehavirājitam /
tadyantraṃ sthāpitaprāṇaṃ pītasūtreṇa veṣṭayet //
1.86.d:
शेषाक्षरैः समानीतं धरागेहविराजितम् ।
तद्यन्त्रं स्थापितप्राणं पीतसूत्रेण वेष्टयेत् ॥
1.86.m: Supplied with the remaining syllables, adorned with an earth-house. / Having established the life-breath in that yantra, one should bind it with yellow thread.

1.86.s:
bhrāmyatkulālacakrasthāṃ gṛhītvā mṛttikāṃ tathā /
racayedṛṣabhaṃ ramyaṃ yantraṃ tanmadhyataḥ kṣipet //
1.86.d:
भ्राम्यत्कुलालचक्रस्थां गृहीत्वा मृत्तिकां तथा ।
रचयेदृषभं रम्यं यन्त्रं तन्मध्यतः क्षिपेत् ॥
1.86.m: Taking clay situated upon a rotating potter's wheel, / One should fashion a beautiful bull and cast the yantra into its center.

1.86.s:
haritālena saṃlipya vṛṣaṃ pratyahamarcayet /
staṃbhayedvidviṣāṃ vācaṃ gatiṃ kāryaparaṃparām //
1.86.d:
हरितालेन संलिप्य वृषं प्रत्यहमर्चयेत् ।
स्तंभयेद्विद्विषां वाचं गतिं कार्यपरंपराम् ॥
1.86.m: Having smeared the bull with yellow orpiment, one should worship it every day; / One paralyzes the speech, movement, and continuous actions of enemies.

1.86.s:
ādāya vāmahastena pretabhūsthitakarparam /
aṅgāreṇa citāsthena tatra yantraṃ samālikhet //
1.86.d:
आदाय वामहस्तेन प्रेतभूस्थितकर्परम् ।
अङ्गारेण चितास्थेन तत्र यन्त्रं समालिखेत् ॥
1.86.m: Taking with the left hand a skull situated in a cremation ground, / With charcoal from a funeral pyre one should write the yantra there.

1.86.s:
mantritaṃ nihitaṃ bhūmau ripūṇāṃ staṃbhayedgatim /
pretavastre likhedyantraṃ aṅgāreṇaiva tatpunaḥ //
1.86.d:
मन्त्रितं निहितं भूमौ रिपूणां स्तंभयेद्गतिम् ।
प्रेतवस्त्रे लिखेद्यन्त्रं अङ्गारेणैव तत्पुनः ॥
1.86.m: Consecrated with the mantra and buried in the earth, it paralyzes the movement of enemies. / Again, one should write the yantra on a shroud with charcoal,

1.86.s:
maṇḍūkavadane nyasyetpītasūtreṇa veṣṭitam /
pūjitaṃ pītapuṣpaistadvācaṃ saṃstaṃbhayeddviṣām //
1.86.d:
मण्डूकवदने न्यस्येत्पीतसूत्रेण वेष्टितम् ।
पूजितं पीतपुष्पैस्तद्वाचं संस्तंभयेद्द्विषाम् ॥
1.86.m: Place it inside the mouth of a frog, bound with yellow thread; / Worshipped with yellow flowers, it completely paralyzes the speech of adversaries.

1.86.s:
yadbhūmau bhavitā divyaṃ tatra yantraṃ samālikhet /
mārjitaṃ taddviṣāṃ pātrairdivyastambhanakṛdbhavet //
1.86.d:
यद्भूमौ भविता दिव्यं तत्र यन्त्रं समालिखेत् ।
मार्जितं तद्द्विषां पात्रैर्दिव्यस्तम्भनकृद्भवेत् ॥
1.86.m: Where an ordeal will take place on earth, there one should write the yantra; / Cleaned with vessels of the enemies, it paralyzes the ordeal.

1.86.s:
indravāruṇikāmūlaṃ saptaśo manumantritam /
kṣiptaṃ jale divyakṛtaṃ jalastaṃbhanakārakam //
1.86.d:
इन्द्रवारुणिकामूलं सप्तशो मनुमन्त्रितम् ।
क्षिप्तं जले दिव्यकृतं जलस्तंभनकारकम् ॥
1.86.m: The root of indravāruṇī consecrated seven times with the mantra / And thrown into the water of an ordeal causes the paralysis of water.

1.86.s:
kiṃ bahūktyā sādhakena mantraḥ samyagupāsitaḥ /
śatrūṇāṃ gatibuddhyādeḥ staṃbhano nātra saṃśayaḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde yakṣiṇīmantrasādhananirūpaṇaṃ nāma ṣaḍaśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.86.d:
किं बहूक्त्या साधकेन मन्त्रः सम्यगुपासितः ।
शत्रूणां गतिबुद्ध्यादेः स्तंभनो नात्र संशयः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे यक्षिणीमन्त्रसाधननिरूपणं नाम षडशीतितमो ऽध्यायः
1.86.m:
What need of many words? When the mantra is properly worshipped by the practitioner, / It paralyzes the movement, intellect, and other faculties of enemies; there is no doubt about this.

Thus ends the eighty-sixth chapter, named 'Expounding the Accomplishment of the Yakṣiṇī Mantra,' in the third quarter of the great narrative in the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.87.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
avatāratrayaṃ lakṣmyāḥ kathita te dvijottama /
durgāyāścābhidhāsyāmi sarvalokopakārakān //
1.87.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
अवतारत्रयं लक्ष्म्याः कथित ते द्विजोत्तम ।
दुर्गायाश्चाभिधास्यामि सर्वलोकोपकारकान् ॥
1.87.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Three incarnations of Lakṣmī have been spoken to you, O best of the twice-born; / And I shall declare those of Durgā that are beneficent to all the worlds.

1.87.s:
praṇavaḥ śrīḥ śivāyugmaṃ vāṇīvairocanīpadam /
vajrādyaṃ kṣudhitā sūkṣmā mṛtā svāgnīndusaṃyutā //
1.87.d:
प्रणवः श्रीः शिवायुग्मं वाणीवैरोचनीपदम् ।
वज्राद्यं क्षुधिता सूक्ष्मा मृता स्वाग्नीन्दुसंयुता ॥
1.87.m: The praṇava, Śrī, a pair of Śivās, the word Vāṇīvairocanī, / [the word] beginning with Vajra, Kṣudhitā, Sūkṣmā, Mṛtā, conjoined with their fire and moon,

1.87.s:
pratiṣṭhāpya śivā phaṭ ca svāhānto 'tyaṣṭivarṇavān /
bhairavo 'sya muniḥ samrāṭ chando mantrasya devatā //
1.87.d:
प्रतिष्ठाप्य शिवा फट् च स्वाहान्तो ऽत्यष्टिवर्णवान् ।
भैरवो ऽस्य मुनिः सम्राट् छन्दो मन्त्रस्य देवता ॥
1.87.m: Having placed [the word] Śivā, and phaṭ, ending with svāhā, [this mantra] has twenty-eight syllables. / Bhairava is its seer; the meter is Samrāṭ; the deity of the mantra is [Chinnamastā];

1.87.s:
chinnamastā ramā bījaṃ svāhā śaktirudīritā /
āṃ khaḍgāya hṛdākhyātamīṃ khaḍgāya śiraḥ smṛtam //
1.87.d:
छिन्नमस्ता रमा बीजं स्वाहा शक्तिरुदीरिता ।
आं खड्गाय हृदाख्यातमीं खड्गाय शिरः स्मृतम् ॥
1.87.m: Chinnamastā; Ramā is said to be the seed; svāhā the power. / āṃ khaḍgāya is declared to be the heart; īṃ khaḍgāya is remembered as the head;

1.87.s:
oṃ vajrāya śikhā proktā aiṃ pāśāya tanucchadam /
aumaṅkuśāya netraṃ syādvisargo vasurakṣayuk //
1.87.d:
ओं वज्राय शिखा प्रोक्ता ऐं पाशाय तनुच्छदम् ।
औमङ्कुशाय नेत्रं स्याद्विसर्गो वसुरक्षयुक् ॥
1.87.m: oṃ vajrāya is said to be the crown; aiṃ pāśāya the armor; / auṃ aṅkuśāya is the eye; the visarga conjoined with eight protections,

1.87.s:
māyāyugmaṃ cāstramaṅgaṃ manavaḥ praṇavādikāḥ /
svāhāntāścaivamaṅgāni kṛtvā dhyāyedthāṃbikām //
1.87.d:
मायायुग्मं चास्त्रमङ्गं मनवः प्रणवादिकाः ।
स्वाहान्ताश्चैवमङ्गानि कृत्वा ध्यायेद्थांबिकाम् ॥
1.87.m: And the pair of Māyās is the weapon-limb; the mantras begin with the praṇava / and end with svāhā. Having thus performed the limbs, one should meditate upon the Mother:

1.87.s:
bhānumaṇḍalasaṃsthānāṃ pravikīrṇālakaṃ śiraḥ /
chinnaṃ svakaṃ sphaāramukhaṃ svaraktaṃ prapibadgalat //
1.87.d:
भानुमण्डलसंस्थानां प्रविकीर्णालकं शिरः ।
छिन्नं स्वकं स्फआरमुखं स्वरक्तं प्रपिबद्गलत् ॥
1.87.m: Standing in the orb of the sun, her severed head having disheveled locks of hair, / with a wide open mouth, drinking her own blood dripping down [from her neck],

1.87.s:
uparisthāṃ ratāsaktaratimanmathayornije /
ḍākinīvarṇinīsakhyau dṛṣṭvā modabharākulām //
1.87.d:
उपरिस्थां रतासक्तरतिमन्मथयोर्निजे ।
डाकिनीवर्णिनीसख्यौ दृष्ट्वा मोदभराकुलाम् ॥
1.87.m: Standing upon Rati and Manmatha, who are engaged in lovemaking; / seeing her two companions, Ḍākinī and Varṇinī, overcome with intense delight.

1.87.s:
dhyātvaivaṃ prajapellakṣacatuṣkaṃ taddaśāṃśataḥ /
pālāśairvilvajairvāpi juhuyātkusumaiḥ phalaiḥ //
1.87.d:
ध्यात्वैवं प्रजपेल्लक्षचतुष्कं तद्दशांशतः ।
पालाशैर्विल्वजैर्वापि जुहुयात्कुसुमैः फलैः ॥
1.87.m: Having thus meditated, one should recite four hundred thousand times, and as a tenth part of that, / one should offer fire oblations with blossoms and fruits of the palāśa or the bilva.

1.87.s:
ādhāraśaktimārabhya paratattvāntapūjite /
pīṭhe jayākhyā vijayā jitā cāpi parājitā //
1.87.d:
आधारशक्तिमारभ्य परतत्त्वान्तपूजिते ।
पीठे जयाख्या विजया जिता चापि पराजिता ॥
1.87.m: On the ritual seat, worshiped starting from the base-energy up to the supreme principle, / Jayā, Vijayā, Jitā, and Aparājitā,

1.87.s:
nityā vilāsinī ṣaṣṭhī dogdhya ghorā ca maṅgalā /
dikṣu madhye ca saṃpūjyā nava pīṭhasya śaktayaḥ //
1.87.d:
नित्या विलासिनी षष्ठी दोग्ध्य घोरा च मङ्गला ।
दिक्षु मध्ये च संपूज्या नव पीठस्य शक्तयः ॥
1.87.m: Nityā, Vilāsinī, the sixth Dogdhrī, Aghorā, and Maṅgalā: / these nine energies of the ritual seat are to be worshiped in the directions and in the center.

1.87.s:
sarvabuddhiprade varṇanīye sarvabhṛguḥ sadṛk /
siddhiprade ḍākinīye tāro vajraḥ sabhautikaḥ //
1.87.d:
सर्वबुद्धिप्रदे वर्णनीये सर्वभृगुः सदृक् ।
सिद्धिप्रदे डाकिनीये तारो वज्रः सभौतिकः ॥
1.87.m: "sarvabuddhiprade varṇanīye", "sarva", Bhṛgu accompanied by the eye, / "siddhiprade ḍākinīye", the tārā, the thunderbolt together with the elemental,

1.87.s:
khaḍgīśo rocanīyente bhagaṃ dhehi namontakaḥ /
tārādipīṭhamantro 'yaṃ vedarāmākṣaro mataḥ //
1.87.d:
खड्गीशो रोचनीयेन्ते भगं धेहि नमोन्तकः ।
तारादिपीठमन्त्रो ऽयं वेदरामाक्षरो मतः ॥
1.87.m: "khaḍgīśo rocanīye", at the end, "bhagaṃ dhehi", terminating in "namaḥ". / This ritual-seat mantra beginning with the tārā is considered to have thirty-four syllables.

1.87.s:
samarpyāsanametena tatra saṃpūjayecchivām /
trikoṇamadhyaṣaṭkoṇapadmabhūpuramadhyataḥ //
1.87.d:
समर्प्यासनमेतेन तत्र संपूजयेच्छिवाम् ।
त्रिकोणमध्यषट्कोणपद्मभूपुरमध्यतः ॥
1.87.m: Having offered the seat with this, one should worship Śivā there, / within the earth-citadel, the lotus, the hexagram, and the triangle at its center.

1.87.s:
bāhyāvaraṇamārabhya pūjayetpratilomataḥ /
bhūpure bāhyabhāgeṣu vajrādīni prapūjayet //
1.87.d:
बाह्यावरणमारभ्य पूजयेत्प्रतिलोमतः ।
भूपुरे बाह्यभागेषु वज्रादीनि प्रपूजयेत् ॥
1.87.m: Beginning from the outer enclosure, one should worship in reverse order. / In the outer parts of the earth-citadel, one should worship the thunderbolt and other [weapons];

1.87.s:
tadantaḥ surarājādīnpūjayeddharitāṃ patīn /
bhūpurasya caturdvārṣu dvārapālānyajedatha //
1.87.d:
तदन्तः सुरराजादीन्पूजयेद्धरितां पतीन् ।
भूपुरस्य चतुर्द्वार्षु द्वारपालान्यजेदथ ॥
1.87.m: Inside that, one should worship the king of the gods and the other guardians of the quarters; / then, at the four gates of the earth-citadel, one should worship the doorkeepers:

1.87.s:
karālavikarālākhyāvatikālastṛtīyakaḥ /
mahākālaścaturthaḥ syādatha padmeṣṭaśaktayaḥ //
1.87.d:
करालविकरालाख्यावतिकालस्तृतीयकः ।
महाकालश्चतुर्थः स्यादथ पद्मेष्टशक्तयः ॥
1.87.m: Those named Karāla and Vikarāla, the third being Atikāla, / and Mahākāla is the fourth. Then, on the lotus, the eight energies:

1.87.s:
ekaliṅgā yoginī ca ḍākinī bhairavī tathā /
mahābhairavakendrākṣī tvasitāṅgī tu saptamī //
1.87.d:
एकलिङ्गा योगिनी च डाकिनी भैरवी तथा ।
महाभैरवकेन्द्राक्षी त्वसिताङ्गी तु सप्तमी ॥
1.87.m: Ekaliṅgā, Yoginī, Ḍākinī, Bhairavī, / Mahābhairavī, Kendrākṣī, Asitāṅgī as the seventh,

1.87.s:
saṃhāriṇyaṣṭamī ceti ṣaṭkoṇeṣvaṅgamūrtayaḥ /
trikoṇagā chinnamastā pārśvayostu sakhīdvayam //
1.87.d:
संहारिण्यष्टमी चेति षट्कोणेष्वङ्गमूर्तयः ।
त्रिकोणगा छिन्नमस्ता पार्श्वयोस्तु सखीद्वयम् ॥
1.87.m: And Saṃhāriṇī as the eighth; and on the hexagram, the forms of the limbs. / Chinnamastā resides in the triangle, and at her sides are the two companions,

1.87.s:
ḍākinīvarṇanīsaṃjñaṃ tārāvāgbhyāṃ prapūjayet /
evaṃ pūjādibhiḥ siddhe mantre mantrī manorathān //
1.87.d:
डाकिनीवर्णनीसंज्ञं तारावाग्भ्यां प्रपूजयेत् ।
एवं पूजादिभिः सिद्धे मन्त्रे मन्त्री मनोरथान् ॥
1.87.m: Known as Ḍākinī and Varṇinī; one should worship [them] with the tārā and speech [seeds]. / In this way, when the mantra is mastered through worship and the rest, the practitioner [attains] his desires;

1.87.s:
prāpnuyānnikhilānsadyo durlabhāṃstatprasādataḥ /
śrīpuṣpairlabhate lakṣmīṃ tatphailaśca samīhitam //
1.87.d:
प्राप्नुयान्निखिलान्सद्यो दुर्लभांस्तत्प्रसादतः ।
श्रीपुष्पैर्लभते लक्ष्मीं तत्फैलश्च समीहितम् ॥
1.87.m: Through her grace, he quickly obtains all things that are otherwise hard to attain. / With śrī-flowers he obtains wealth, and with their fruits whatever he desires;

1.87.s:
vāksiddhiṃ mālatīpuṣpaiścaṃpakairhavanātsukham /
ghṛtāktaṃ chāgamāṃsaṃ yo juhuyātpratyahaṃ śatam //
1.87.d:
वाक्सिद्धिं मालतीपुष्पैश्चंपकैर्हवनात्सुखम् ।
घृताक्तं छागमांसं यो जुहुयात्प्रत्यहं शतम् ॥
1.87.m: Success in speech with mālatī flowers, and happiness from oblations of campaka flowers. / He who offers daily one hundred fire oblations of goat's meat smeared with clarified butter,

1.87.s:
māsamekaṃ tu vaśagāstasya syuḥ sarvapārthivāḥ /
karavīrasumaiḥ śvatairlakṣasaṃkhyairjuhoti yaḥ //
1.87.d:
मासमेकं तु वशगास्तस्य स्युः सर्वपार्थिवाः ।
करवीरसुमैः श्वतैर्लक्षसंख्यैर्जुहोति यः ॥
1.87.m: For one month, will have all kings subjected to his will. / He who offers fire oblations with a hundred thousand white oleander flowers,

1.87.s:
rogajālaṃ parābhūya sukhī jīvecchataṃ samāḥ /
raktau statsaṃkhyayā hutvā vaśayenmantriṇo nṛpān //
1.87.d:
रोगजालं पराभूय सुखी जीवेच्छतं समाः ।
रक्तौ स्तत्संख्यया हुत्वा वशयेन्मन्त्रिणो नृपान् ॥
1.87.m: Overcoming the host of diseases, lives happily for a hundred years. / By offering red ones in that same number, he brings kings and ministers under control.

1.87.s:
phalairhutvāmuyāllakṣmīmuduṃbarapalāśajaiḥ /
gomāyumāṃsaistāmeva kavitāṃ pāyasāṃdhasā //
1.87.d:
फलैर्हुत्वामुयाल्लक्ष्मीमुदुंबरपलाशजैः ।
गोमायुमांसैस्तामेव कवितां पायसांधसा ॥
1.87.m: By offering fire oblations with fruits born of udumbara and palāśa, he obtains fortune; / by meat of jackals, the same; poetic gift with milk-rice food;

1.87.s:
bandhūkakusumairbhāgyaṃ karmikāraiḥ samīhitam /
tilataṇḍulahomena vaśayennikhilāñjanān //
1.87.d:
बन्धूककुसुमैर्भाग्यं कर्मिकारैः समीहितम् ।
तिलतण्डुलहोमेन वशयेन्निखिलाञ्जनान् ॥
1.87.m: Good fortune with bandhūka blossoms; desired objects with karṇikāra flowers; / by fire oblations of sesame and raw rice, he subdues all people.

1.87.s:
nārīrajobhirākṛṣṭairmṛgamāṃsaiḥ samīhitam /
staṃbhanaṃ māhiṣairmāṃsaiḥ paṅkajaiḥ saghṛtairapi //
1.87.d:
नारीरजोभिराकृष्टैर्मृगमांसैः समीहितम् ।
स्तंभनं माहिषैर्मांसैः पङ्कजैः सघृतैरपि ॥
1.87.m: With the menstrual fluids of women, desired objects are attracted; with venison, the desired [is gained]; / immobilization [is achieved] with buffalo meat, as well as with lotuses smeared with clarified butter.

1.87.s:
citāgnau parabhṛtpakṣairjurhuyādarimṛtyave /
unmattakāṣṭhadīpte 'gnau tatphalaṃ vāyasacchadaiḥ //
1.87.d:
चिताग्नौ परभृत्पक्षैर्जुर्हुयादरिमृत्यवे ।
उन्मत्तकाष्ठदीप्ते ऽग्नौ तत्फलं वायसच्छदैः ॥
1.87.m: One should offer fire oblations into a funeral pyre with feathers of a cuckoo for the death of an enemy; / that same result [is attained] in a fire kindled with datura wood using crow feathers.

1.87.s:
dyūte vane nṛpadvāre samare vairisaṃkaṭe /
vijayaṃ labhate mantrī dhyāyandevīṃ japanmanum //
1.87.d:
द्यूते वने नृपद्वारे समरे वैरिसंकटे ।
विजयं लभते मन्त्री ध्यायन्देवीं जपन्मनुम् ॥
1.87.m: In gambling, in the forest, at a king's gate, in battle, in danger from enemies, / the practitioner attains victory by meditating on the goddess and reciting the mantra.

1.87.s:
bhuktyai muktyai sitāṃ dhyāyeduccāṭe nīlarociṣam /
raktāṃ vaśye mṛtau dhūmrāṃ staṃbhane kanakaprabhām //
1.87.d:
भुक्त्यै मुक्त्यै सितां ध्यायेदुच्चाटे नीलरोचिषम् ।
रक्तां वश्ये मृतौ धूम्रां स्तंभने कनकप्रभाम् ॥
1.87.m: For enjoyment and liberation, one should meditate on her as white; for driving away [enemies], of blue radiance; / red for subjection; smoke-colored for death; and possessing the luster of gold for immobilization.

1.87.s:
niśi dadyādbaliṃ tasyai siddhaye madirādinā /
gopanīyaḥ prayogo 'ya procyate sarvasiddhidaḥ //
1.87.d:
निशि दद्याद्बलिं तस्यै सिद्धये मदिरादिना ।
गोपनीयः प्रयोगो ऽय प्रोच्यते सर्वसिद्धिदः ॥
1.87.m: At night, one should offer her an animal sacrifice or food offering with liquor and the like for attainment. / This secret practice, which grants all attainments, is declared:

1.87.s:
bhūtāhe kṛṣṇapakṣasya madhyarātre tamoghane /
snāttvā raktāmbaradharo raktamālyānulepanaḥ //
1.87.d:
भूताहे कृष्णपक्षस्य मध्यरात्रे तमोघने ।
स्नात्त्वा रक्ताम्बरधरो रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनः ॥
1.87.m: On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, at midnight when darkness is thick, / having bathed, wearing red garments, adorned with red garlands and ointments,

1.87.s:
ānīya pūjayennārīṃ chinnamastāsvarūpiṇīm /
sundarīṃ yauvanākrāntāṃ narapañcakagāminīm //
1.87.d:
आनीय पूजयेन्नारीं छिन्नमस्तास्वरूपिणीम् ।
सुन्दरीं यौवनाक्रान्तां नरपञ्चकगामिनीम् ॥
1.87.m: Having brought a woman who is the embodiment of Chinnamastā, / beautiful, in the prime of youth, who has known five men,

1.87.s:
susmitāṃ muktakabīrīṃ bhūṣādānapratoṣitām /
vivastrāṃ pūjayitvaināmayutaṃ prajapenmanum //
1.87.d:
सुस्मितां मुक्तकबीरीं भूषादानप्रतोषिताम् ।
विवस्त्रां पूजयित्वैनामयुतं प्रजपेन्मनुम् ॥
1.87.m: Gently smiling, with disheveled hair, gladdened by gifts of ornaments, / having worshiped her unclothed, one should recite the mantra ten thousand times.

1.87.s:
baliṃ dattvā niśāṃ nītvā saṃpreṣya dhanatoṣitām /
bhojayedvividhairannairbrāhmaṇānbhojanādinā //
1.87.d:
बलिं दत्त्वा निशां नीत्वा संप्रेष्य धनतोषिताम् ।
भोजयेद्विविधैरन्नैर्ब्राह्मणान्भोजनादिना ॥
1.87.m: Having offered a bali, passed the night, and sent her away satisfied with wealth, / he should feed brāhmaṇas with various kinds of foods and feasts.

1.87.s:
anena vidhinā lakṣmīṃ putrānpautrāndhanaṃ yaśaḥ /
nārīmāyuḥ sukhaṃ dharmamiṣṭaṃ ca samavāpnuyāt //
1.87.d:
अनेन विधिना लक्ष्मीं पुत्रान्पौत्रान्धनं यशः ।
नारीमायुः सुखं धर्ममिष्टं च समवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.87.m: By this procedure, he obtains wealth, sons, grandsons, riches, fame, / a woman, long life, happiness, righteousness, and whatever is desired.

1.87.s:
tasyāṃ rātrau vrataṃ kāryaṃ vidyākāmena mantriṇā /
manoratheṣu cānyeṣu gacchettāṃ prajapanmanum //
1.87.d:
तस्यां रात्रौ व्रतं कार्यं विद्याकामेन मन्त्रिणा ।
मनोरथेषु चान्येषु गच्छेत्तां प्रजपन्मनुम् ॥
1.87.m: On that night, an observance should be undertaken by the practitioner who desires learning; / and for other desires, he should approach her while reciting the mantra.

1.87.s:
uṣasyutthāya śayyāyāmupaviṣṭo japecchatam /
ṣaṇmāsābhyantaremantrī kavitvena jayetkavim //
1.87.d:
उषस्युत्थाय शय्यायामुपविष्टो जपेच्छतम् ।
षण्मासाभ्यन्तरेमन्त्री कवित्वेन जयेत्कविम् ॥
1.87.m: Having risen at dawn and seated upon his bed, he should recite [it] one hundred times; / within six months, the practitioner will surpass even the poet [Bṛhaspati] in poetic skill.

1.87.s:
śivena kīlitā ceyaṃ tadutkīlanamucyate /
māyāṃ tārapuṭāṃ mantrī japedaṣṭottaraṃ śatam //
1.87.d:
शिवेन कीलिता चेयं तदुत्कीलनमुच्यते ।
मायां तारपुटां मन्त्री जपेदष्टोत्तरं शतम् ॥
1.87.m: This [mantra] was locked by Śiva; its unlocking is now declared: / the practitioner should recite the Māyā-syllable, enclosed by the tārā, one hundred and eight times

1.87.s:
mantrasyādau tathaivānte bhavetsiddhipradā tu sā /
uditā chinnamasteyaṃ kalau śīghramabhīṣṭadā //
1.87.d:
मन्त्रस्यादौ तथैवान्ते भवेत्सिद्धिप्रदा तु सा ।
उदिता छिन्नमस्तेयं कलौ शीघ्रमभीष्टदा ॥
1.87.m: At the beginning of the mantra and likewise at its end; then it becomes the bestower of success. / This Chinnamastā has been described; in the Kali age, she quickly grants desired wishes.

1.87.s:
avatārāntaraṃ devyā vacmi te munisattama /
jñānāmṛtāruṇā śvetākrodhinīndusamanvitā //
1.87.d:
अवतारान्तरं देव्या वच्मि ते मुनिसत्तम ।
ज्ञानामृतारुणा श्वेताक्रोधिनीन्दुसमन्विता ॥
1.87.m: I shall tell you another incarnation of the goddess, O best of sages: / Jñānāmṛtā, Aruṇā, Śvetā, Krodhinī conjoined with the moon,

1.87.s:
śāntistathāvidhā cāpi nīcasargānvitāstathā /
vāgbhavaṃ kāmarājākhyaṃ śaktibījāhvayaṃ tathā //
1.87.d:
शान्तिस्तथाविधा चापि नीचसर्गान्वितास्तथा ।
वाग्भवं कामराजाख्यं शक्तिबीजाह्वयं तथा ॥
1.87.m: Likewise Śānti of that nature, and conjoined with the visarga; / the vāgbhava, the seed named kāmarāja, and the seed called śakti—

1.87.s:
tribhirbījaiḥ pañcakūṭātmikā tripurabhairavī /
ṛṣiḥ syāddakṣiṇāmūrtiśchandaḥ paṅktirudīritā //
1.87.d:
त्रिभिर्बीजैः पञ्चकूटात्मिका त्रिपुरभैरवी ।
ऋषिः स्याद्दक्षिणामूर्तिश्छन्दः पङ्क्तिरुदीरिता ॥
1.87.m: Composed of five peaks by means of these three seeds is Tripurabhairavī. / The seer is Dakṣiṇāmūrti; the meter is declared to be Paṅkti;

1.87.s:
devatā deśikairuktā devī tripurabhairavī /
nābherācaraṇaṃ nyasya vāgbhavaṃ mantravitpunaḥ //
1.87.d:
देवता देशिकैरुक्ता देवी त्रिपुरभैरवी ।
नाभेराचरणं न्यस्य वाग्भवं मन्त्रवित्पुनः ॥
1.87.m: The goddess is said by teachers to be the goddess Tripurabhairavī. / Having rituals placed the vāgbhava from the navel down to the feet, the knower of mantras again

1.87.s:
hṛdayānnābhiparyantaṃ kāmabījaṃ pravinyaset /
śiraso hṛtpradeśāntaṃ tārtīyaṃ vinyasettataḥ //
1.87.d:
हृदयान्नाभिपर्यन्तं कामबीजं प्रविन्यसेत् ।
शिरसो हृत्प्रदेशान्तं तार्तीयं विन्यसेत्ततः ॥
1.87.m: Should place the kāma-seed from the heart to the navel; / then he should place the third seed from the head to the heart region.

1.87.s:
ādyaṃ dvitīyaṃ karayostārtīyamubhayaṃ nyaset /
mūlādhāre hṛdi nyasya bhūyo bījatrayaṃ kramāt //
1.87.d:
आद्यं द्वितीयं करयोस्तार्तीयमुभयं न्यसेत् ।
मूलाधारे हृदि न्यस्य भूयो बीजत्रयं क्रमात् ॥
1.87.m: He should place the first and second on the two hands, and the third on both; / having placed the triad of seeds in the mūlādhāra and in the heart again in succession,

1.87.s:
navayonyātmakaṃ nyāsaṃ kuryādbījaistribhiḥ punaḥ /
bāloditaprakāreṇa mūrtinyāsamathācaret //
1.87.d:
नवयोन्यात्मकं न्यासं कुर्याद्बीजैस्त्रिभिः पुनः ।
बालोदितप्रकारेण मूर्तिन्यासमथाचरेत् ॥
1.87.m: He should perform the ritual placement of the nine yonis once more with the three seeds; / then he should perform the ritual placement of the divine forms in the manner stated for Bālā.

1.87.s:
svasvabījādikaṃ pūrvaṃ mūrdhnīśānamanobhavam /
nyasedvaktre tatpuruṣaṃ makaradhvajamātmavit //
1.87.d:
स्वस्वबीजादिकं पूर्वं मूर्ध्नीशानमनोभवम् ।
न्यसेद्वक्त्रे तत्पुरुषं मकरध्वजमात्मवित् ॥
1.87.m: The knower of the self, having first [uttered] the respective seeds, / should place Īśāna-Manobhava on the head, and Tatpuruṣa-Makaradhvaja on the mouth,

1.87.s:
hṛdyaghorakumārādikandarppaṃ tadanantaram /
guhyadeśe pravinyasyedvāmadevādimanmatham //
1.87.d:
हृद्यघोरकुमारादिकन्दर्प्पं तदनन्तरम् ।
गुह्यदेशे प्रविन्यस्येद्वामदेवादिमन्मथम् ॥
1.87.m: Then Aghora-Kumāra-Kandarpa on the heart, / and should ritually place Vāmadeva-Manmatha on the secret region.

1.87.s:
sadyojātaṃ kāmadevaṃ pādayorvinyasettataḥ /
ūrddhvaṃprāgdakṣiṇodīcyapaścimeṣu mukheṣu tān //
1.87.d:
सद्योजातं कामदेवं पादयोर्विन्यसेत्ततः ।
ऊर्द्ध्वंप्राग्दक्षिणोदीच्यपश्चिमेषु मुखेषु तान् ॥
1.87.m: Then one should place Sadyojāta-Kāmadeva upon the feet; / and one should place them [respectively] on the upper, eastern, southern, northern, and western faces.

1.87.s:
pravinyasedya dhāpūrva bhṛgurvyomāgnisaṃsthitaḥ /
sadyādipañcahrasvādyā bījameṣāṃ prakīrtitam //
1.87.d:
प्रविन्यसेद्य धापूर्व भृगुर्व्योमाग्निसंस्थितः ।
सद्यादिपञ्चह्रस्वाद्या बीजमेषां प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
1.87.m: As before, one should place Bhṛgu seated with ether and fire. / The five short vowels beginning with 'a' are taught as their seed-syllables.

1.87.s:
ṣaḍdīrghayuktenādyena bījenāṅgakriyā matā /
pañcabāṇāṃstato nyasyenmantrī trailokyamohanān //
1.87.d:
षड्दीर्घयुक्तेनाद्येन बीजेनाङ्गक्रिया मता ।
पञ्चबाणांस्ततो न्यस्येन्मन्त्री त्रैलोक्यमोहनान् ॥
1.87.m: The performance of the limbs is considered to be done with the first seed-syllable joined with the six long [vowels]. / Then the practitioner of mantra should place the five arrows that enchant the three worlds:

1.87.s:
drāmādyāṃ drāviṇīṃ mūrdhniṃ drāmādyāṃ kṣobhaṇī pade /
klīṃvaśīkaraṇīṃ vaktre guhye bḷṃ bījapūrvikām //
1.87.d:
द्रामाद्यां द्राविणीं मूर्ध्निं द्रामाद्यां क्षोभणी पदे ।
क्लींवशीकरणीं वक्त्रे गुह्ये बॢं बीजपूर्विकाम् ॥
1.87.m: Drāviṇī, beginning with 'drām', on the head; Kṣobhaṇī, beginning with 'drīm', on the feet; / Vaśīkaraṇī, with 'klīm', on the mouth; and Ākarṣaṇī, preceded by the seed-syllable 'blūm', on the private parts;

1.87.s:
ākarṣaṇīṃ hṛdi punaḥ sarvāntabhṛgusaṃsthitām /
saṃmohanīṃ kramādevaṃ bāṇanyāso 'yamīritaḥ //
1.87.d:
आकर्षणीं हृदि पुनः सर्वान्तभृगुसंस्थिताम् ।
संमोहनीं क्रमादेवं बाणन्यासो ऽयमीरितः ॥
1.87.m: then Saṃmohanī, situated with the last of all, Bhṛgu, on the heart. / In this sequence the ritual placement of the arrows has been proclaimed.

1.87.s:
bhālabhrūmadhyavadane ghaṇṭikākaṇṭhahṛtsu ca /
nābhyadhiṣṭhānayoḥ pañca tārādyāḥ subhagādikāḥ //
1.87.d:
भालभ्रूमध्यवदने घण्टिकाकण्ठहृत्सु च ।
नाभ्यधिष्ठानयोः पञ्च ताराद्याः सुभगादिकाः ॥
1.87.m: On the forehead, between the eyebrows, on the face, the uvula, the throat, the heart, / the navel, and the generative organ, the five [syllables] beginning with the praṇava, and [the deities] beginning with Subhagā [should be placed].

1.87.s:
mastakāvidhi nābheśca mantriṇā subhagā bhagā /
bhagasarpiṇyatha parā bhagamālinyanantaram //
1.87.d:
मस्तकाविधि नाभेश्च मन्त्रिणा सुभगा भगा ।
भगसर्पिण्यथ परा भगमालिन्यनन्तरम् ॥
1.87.m: By the practitioner of mantra, from the head down to the navel: Subhagā, Bhagā, / then Bhagasarpiṇī, next the supreme Bhagamālinī;

1.87.s:
anaṅgānaṅgakusumā bhūyaścānaṅgamekhalā /
anaṅgamadanā sarvā madavibhramamantharā //
1.87.d:
अनङ्गानङ्गकुसुमा भूयश्चानङ्गमेखला ।
अनङ्गमदना सर्वा मदविभ्रममन्थरा ॥
1.87.m: Anaṅgā, Anaṅgakusumā, and further Anaṅgamekhalā, / and Anaṅgamadanā—all languid with the intoxication of passion,

1.87.s:
pradhānadevatā varṇabhūṣaṇādyairalaṅkṛtāḥ /
akṣasrakpustakābhītivaradāḍhyakarāṃbujāḥ //
1.87.d:
प्रधानदेवता वर्णभूषणाद्यैरलङ्कृताः ।
अक्षस्रक्पुस्तकाभीतिवरदाढ्यकरांबुजाः ॥
1.87.m: adorned with the complexions, ornaments, and attributes of the principal deity, / their lotus hands furnished with a rosary, a book, the gesture of fearlessness, and the gesture of granting boons.

1.87.s:
vākkāmablūṃ strīṃ sarānte tārāḥ pañca prakīrtitāḥ /
tataḥ kuryādbhūṣaṇākhyaṃ nyāsamuktadiśā mune //
1.87.d:
वाक्कामब्लूं स्त्रीं सरान्ते ताराः पञ्च प्रकीर्तिताः ।
ततः कुर्याद्भूषणाख्यं न्यासमुक्तदिशा मुने ॥
1.87.m: The five praṇavas are taught as Vāc, Kāma, 'blūṃ', 'strīṃ', and ending with 'saḥ' and 'ra'. / Then, O sage, one should perform the ritual placement called Bhūṣaṇa in the manner described.

1.87.s:
evaṃ nyastaśarīro 'sau dhyāyettripurabhairavīm /
sahasrabhānusaṃkāśāmaruṇakṣaumavāsasīm //
1.87.d:
एवं न्यस्तशरीरो ऽसौ ध्यायेत्त्रिपुरभैरवीम् ।
सहस्रभानुसंकाशामरुणक्षौमवाससीम् ॥
1.87.m: Having thus placed [the deities upon] his body, he should meditate upon Tripurabhairavī, / resembling a thousand suns, wearing garments of red silk,

1.87.s:
śiromālāmasṛgliptastanīṃ japavaṭīṃ karaiḥ /
vidyāmabhītiṃ ca varaṃ dadhatīṃ trīkṣaṇānanām //
1.87.d:
शिरोमालामसृग्लिप्तस्तनीं जपवटीं करैः ।
विद्यामभीतिं च वरं दधतीं त्रीक्षणाननाम् ॥
1.87.m: with a garland of severed heads, her breasts smeared with blood, holding in her hands a rosary, / sacred knowledge, and the gestures of fearlessness and boon-granting, her face possessing three eyes.

1.87.s:
dīkṣāṃ prāpya japenmantraṃ tattvalakṣaṃ jitendriyaḥ /
puṣpairbhānusahasrāṇi juhuyādbahmavṛkṣajaiḥ //
1.87.d:
दीक्षां प्राप्य जपेन्मन्त्रं तत्त्वलक्षं जितेन्द्रियः ।
पुष्पैर्भानुसहस्राणि जुहुयाद्बह्मवृक्षजैः ॥
1.87.m: Having obtained initiation, with senses subdued, he should recite the mantra twenty-four hundred thousand times; / he should offer twelve thousand fire oblations with flowers produced from the Palāśa tree,

1.87.s:
trimadhvaktaiḥ prasūnairvā karavīrasamudbhavaiḥ /
padmaṃ vasudalopetaṃ navayonyaṣṭakarṇikam //
1.87.d:
त्रिमध्वक्तैः प्रसूनैर्वा करवीरसमुद्भवैः ।
पद्मं वसुदलोपेतं नवयोन्यष्टकर्णिकम् ॥
1.87.m: or with oleander blossoms smeared with the three sweet substances. / A lotus endowed with eight petals, having nine yonis and an eight-[seeded] pericarp,

1.87.s:
icchādiśaktibhiryuktaṃ bhairavyāḥ pīṭhamarcayet /
icchā jñānā kriyā paścātkāminī kāmadāyinī //
1.87.d:
इच्छादिशक्तिभिर्युक्तं भैरव्याः पीठमर्चयेत् ।
इच्छा ज्ञाना क्रिया पश्चात्कामिनी कामदायिनी ॥
1.87.m: endowed with the powers such as Icchā—one should worship this ritual seat of Bhairavī: / Icchā, Jñānā, Kriyā, then Kāminī, Kāmadāyinī,

1.87.s:
ratipriyā madānandā navamī syānmanonmanī /
varadābhayadhāriṇyaḥ saṃproktā nava śaktayaḥ //
1.87.d:
रतिप्रिया मदानन्दा नवमी स्यान्मनोन्मनी ।
वरदाभयधारिण्यः संप्रोक्ता नव शक्तयः ॥
1.87.m: Ratipriyā, Madānandā, and the ninth is Manonmanī; / the nine powers are proclaimed as bearing the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.

1.87.s:
vāgbhavaṃ lohito rāyai śrīkaṇṭho lohito 'nalaḥ /
dīrghavānyai parā paścādaparāyau hasau yutaḥ //
1.87.d:
वाग्भवं लोहितो रायै श्रीकण्ठो लोहितो ऽनलः ।
दीर्घवान्यै परा पश्चादपरायौ हसौ युतः ॥
1.87.m: Vāgbhava, Lohita, with 'rāyai', Śrīkaṇṭha, Lohita, Anala / having a long vowel with 'yai', next Parā, and Aparā, joined with 'hasau',

1.87.s:
sadāśivamahāpretaṅeṃtaṃ padmāsanaṃ namaḥ /
anena manunā dadyādāsanaṃ śrīgurukramam //
1.87.d:
सदाशिवमहाप्रेतङेंतं पद्मासनं नमः ।
अनेन मनुना दद्यादासनं श्रीगुरुक्रमम् ॥
1.87.m: ending with the dative of Sadāśivamahāpreta, and 'padmāsanāya namaḥ'— / by means of this mantra according to the tradition of the auspicious guru, one should assign the seat.

1.87.s:
prāṅmadhyayonyantarāle pūjayetkalpayettataḥ /
pañcabhiḥ praṇavairmūrtiṃ tasyāmāvāhya devatām //
1.87.d:
प्राङ्मध्ययोन्यन्तराले पूजयेत्कल्पयेत्ततः ।
पञ्चभिः प्रणवैर्मूर्तिं तस्यामावाह्य देवताम् ॥
1.87.m: Then in the space between the eastern and central yonis he should worship and envision / the form [of the deity] with five praṇavas, invoking the deity into it.

1.87.s:
pūjayedagamoktena vidhānena samāhitaḥ /
tārāvākchaktikamalā hasakhūphreṃ hasauḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.87.d:
पूजयेदगमोक्तेन विधानेन समाहितः ।
तारावाक्छक्तिकमला हसखूफ्रें हसौः स्मृताः ॥
1.87.m: Collected in mind, he should worship according to the rule taught in the scriptures. / The praṇava, Vāc, Śakti, Kamalā, 'hasakhphreṃ', and 'hasauḥ' are traditionally remembered.

1.87.s:
vāmakoṇe yajeddevyā ratimindusamaprabhām /
sṛṇipāśadharāṃ saumyāṃ madavibhramavihvalām //
1.87.d:
वामकोणे यजेद्देव्या रतिमिन्दुसमप्रभाम् ।
सृणिपाशधरां सौम्यां मदविभ्रमविह्वलाम् ॥
1.87.m: In the left corner one should worship the goddess Rati, radiant like the moon, / bearing a goad and a noose, gentle, agitated by the intoxication of passion.

1.87.s:
prītiṃ takṣiṇakoṇasthāṃ taptakāñcanasannibhām /
aṅkuśaṃ praṇataṃ dobhyāṃ dhārayantīṃ samarcayet //
1.87.d:
प्रीतिं तक्षिणकोणस्थां तप्तकाञ्चनसन्निभाम् ।
अङ्कुशं प्रणतं दोभ्यां धारयन्तीं समर्चयेत् ॥
1.87.m: One should worship Prīti seated in the right corner, resembling molten gold, / holding a goad and [a hand] bowed in respect with both arms.

1.87.s:
agre manobhavāṃ raktāṃ raktapuṣpādyalaṅkṛtām /
ikṣukārmukapuṣpeṣudhāriṇīṃ sasmitānanām //
1.87.d:
अग्रे मनोभवां रक्तां रक्तपुष्पाद्यलङ्कृताम् ।
इक्षुकार्मुकपुष्पेषुधारिणीं सस्मिताननाम् ॥
1.87.m: In front, Manobhavā: red, adorned with red flowers and ornaments, / bearing a sugarcane bow and flower arrows, with a smiling face.

1.87.s:
aṅgānyabhyarcayetpaścādyathāpūrvaṃ vidhānavit /
dikṣvagre ca nijairmantraiḥ pūjayedbāṇadevatāḥ //
1.87.d:
अङ्गान्यभ्यर्चयेत्पश्चाद्यथापूर्वं विधानवित् ।
दिक्ष्वग्रे च निजैर्मन्त्रैः पूजयेद्बाणदेवताः ॥
1.87.m: Then, knowing the ritual procedure, he should worship the limbs as before. / In the directions and in front, he should worship the deities of the arrows with their own mantras,

1.87.s:
hastābjairdhṛtapuṣpeṣupraṇāmāmṛtasaprabhāḥ /
aṣṭayoniṣvaṣṭaśaktīḥ pūjayetsubhagādikāḥ //
1.87.d:
हस्ताब्जैर्धृतपुष्पेषुप्रणामामृतसप्रभाः ।
अष्टयोनिष्वष्टशक्तीः पूजयेत्सुभगादिकाः ॥
1.87.m: having the radiance of nectar, bowing and holding flower arrows with their lotus hands. / In the eight yonis one should worship the eight powers beginning with Subhagā.

1.87.s:
mātaro bhairavāṅkasthā madavibhramavihvalāḥ /
aṣṭapatreṣu saṃpūjyā yathāvatkusumādibhiḥ //
1.87.d:
मातरो भैरवाङ्कस्था मदविभ्रमविह्वलाः ।
अष्टपत्रेषु संपूज्या यथावत्कुसुमादिभिः ॥
1.87.m: The Mothers seated on the lap of Bhairava, agitated by the intoxication of passion, / are to be properly worshipped on the eight petals with flowers and other offerings.

1.87.s:
lokapālāṃstato dikṣu teṣāmastrāṇi tadbahiḥ /
pūrvajanmakṛtaiḥ puṇyairjñātvaināṃ paradevatām //
1.87.d:
लोकपालांस्ततो दिक्षु तेषामस्त्राणि तद्बहिः ।
पूर्वजन्मकृतैः पुण्यैर्ज्ञात्वैनां परदेवताम् ॥
1.87.m: Then [he should worship] the guardians of the world in the directions, and their weapons outside of them. / Having known this supreme deity through the merits accrued in previous lives,

1.87.s:
yo bhajeduktamārgeṇa sa bhavetsaṃpadāṃ padam /
evaṃ siddhamanurmantrī sādhayediṣṭamātmanaḥ //
1.87.d:
यो भजेदुक्तमार्गेण स भवेत्संपदां पदम् ।
एवं सिद्धमनुर्मन्त्री साधयेदिष्टमात्मनः ॥
1.87.m: whoever worships according to the prescribed path becomes an abode of riches. / Thus, having accomplished the mantra, the practitioner will attain his desired goal.

1.87.s:
juhuyādaruṇāṃbhoñjairadoṣairmadhurāplutaiḥ /
lakṣasaṃkhyaṃ tadarddhaṃ vā pratyahaṃ bhojayeddvijān //
1.87.d:
जुहुयादरुणांभोञ्जैरदोषैर्मधुराप्लुतैः ।
लक्षसंख्यं तदर्द्धं वा प्रत्यहं भोजयेद्द्विजान् ॥
1.87.m: He should offer fire oblations with red lotuses that are flawless and soaked in sweet substances, / to the count of one hundred thousand or half of that, and he should feed twice-born men daily.

1.87.s:
vanitā yuvatī ramyāḥ prīṇayeddevatādhiyā /
homānte dhanadhānyādyaistoṣayedgurumātmanaḥ //
1.87.d:
वनिता युवती रम्याः प्रीणयेद्देवताधिया ।
होमान्ते धनधान्याद्यैस्तोषयेद्गुरुमात्मनः ॥
1.87.m: One should gratify charming young women with the thought that they are deities. / At the end of the fire oblation, one should satisfy one's guru with wealth, grain, and other gifts.

1.87.s:
evaṃ kṛte jagadvaśyo ramāyā bhavanaṃ bhavet /
raktotpalaistrimadhvaktairaruṇairvā hayārijaiḥ //
1.87.d:
एवं कृते जगद्वश्यो रमाया भवनं भवेत् ।
रक्तोत्पलैस्त्रिमध्वक्तैररुणैर्वा हयारिजैः ॥
1.87.m: When this is done, the world becomes subject to him, and he becomes an abode of Ramā. / With red lotuses anointed with the three sweets, or with red oleander flowers,

1.87.s:
puṣpaiḥ payonnaiḥ saghṛtairhemādviśvaṃ vaśaṃ nayet /
vāksiddhaṃ labhate mantrī palāśakusumairhutaiḥ //
1.87.d:
पुष्पैः पयोन्नैः सघृतैर्हेमाद्विश्वं वशं नयेत् ।
वाक्सिद्धं लभते मन्त्री पलाशकुसुमैर्हुतैः ॥
1.87.m: or with milk-rice mixed with ghee, he brings the world under his sway from [the height of] Meru. / The practitioner of mantra attains perfection of speech through oblations of palāśa blossoms.

1.87.s:
karpūrāgurusaṃyuktaṃ guggulaṃ juhuyātsudhīḥ /
jñānaṃ divyamavāpnoti tenaiva sa bhavetkaviḥ //
1.87.d:
कर्पूरागुरुसंयुक्तं गुग्गुलं जुहुयात्सुधीः ।
ज्ञानं दिव्यमवाप्नोति तेनैव स भवेत्कविः ॥
1.87.m: The wise man should offer into the fire guggulu mixed with camphor and aguru; / he attains divine knowledge and by that very act becomes a poet.

1.87.s:
kṣīrāktairamṛtākhaṇḍairhemaḥ sarvāpamṛtyujit /
dūrvābhaghirāyuṣe homaḥ kṣīrāktābhirdinatrayam //
1.87.d:
क्षीराक्तैरमृताखण्डैर्हेमः सर्वापमृत्युजित् ।
दूर्वाभघिरायुषे होमः क्षीराक्ताभिर्दिनत्रयम् ॥
1.87.m: A fire oblation with amṛtā pieces anointed with milk conquers every untimely death. / For longevity, a fire oblation of dūrvā grass anointed with milk should be made for three days.

1.87.s:
girikarṇībhavaiḥ puṣpairbrāhmaṇānvaśayeddhutaiḥ /
kahlāraiḥ pārthivānpuṣpaistadvadhūḥ karṇikārajaiḥ //
1.87.d:
गिरिकर्णीभवैः पुष्पैर्ब्राह्मणान्वशयेद्धुतैः ।
कह्लारैः पार्थिवान्पुष्पैस्तद्वधूः कर्णिकारजैः ॥
1.87.m: Through oblations of girikarṇī flowers, he brings brāhmaṇas under his sway; / with white water-lilies, kings; with karṇikāra flowers, their wives;

1.87.s:
mallikākusumairhutvā rājaputrānvaśaṃ nayet /
koraṇṭakusumairvaiṃśyānvṛṣalānpāṭalodbhavaiḥ //
1.87.d:
मल्लिकाकुसुमैर्हुत्वा राजपुत्रान्वशं नयेत् ।
कोरण्टकुसुमैर्वैंश्यान्वृषलान्पाटलोद्भवैः ॥
1.87.m: having offered oblations with mallikā blossoms, he brings princes under his sway; / with yellow amaranth blossoms, the vaiśyas; and the śūdras with trumpet-flower blossoms.

1.87.s:
anulomāṃ vilomāntasthitasādhyāhvayānvitam /
mantramuccārya juhuyānmantrī madhuralolitaiḥ //
1.87.d:
अनुलोमां विलोमान्तस्थितसाध्याह्वयान्वितम् ।
मन्त्रमुच्चार्य जुहुयान्मन्त्री मधुरलोलितैः ॥
1.87.m: Reciting the mantra accompanied by the name of the person to be subjugated placed between the direct and reverse forms, / the practitioner of mantra should offer oblations steeped in the three sweets.

1.87.s:
sarṣapairmadhusaṃmiśrairvaśayetpārthivān kṣaṇāt /
anenaiva vidhānena tatpatnīstatsutānapi //
1.87.d:
सर्षपैर्मधुसंमिश्रैर्वशयेत्पार्थिवान् क्षणात् ।
अनेनैव विधानेन तत्पत्नीस्तत्सुतानपि ॥
1.87.m: With mustard seeds mixed with honey, he instantly brings kings under his sway; / and by this very procedure, their wives and sons as well.

1.87.s:
jātibilvabhavaiḥ puṣpairmadhuratrayasaṃyutaiḥ /
naranārīnarapatīnhomena vaśayetkramāt //
1.87.d:
जातिबिल्वभवैः पुष्पैर्मधुरत्रयसंयुतैः ।
नरनारीनरपतीन्होमेन वशयेत्क्रमात् ॥
1.87.m: With blossoms of jasmine and bilva combined with the three sweets, / one should gradually bring men, women, and kings under sway by fire oblation.

1.87.s:
mālatībakulodbhūtaiḥ puṣpaiścandanalolitaiḥ /
juhuyātkavitāṃ mantrī labhate vatsarāntare //
1.87.d:
मालतीबकुलोद्भूतैः पुष्पैश्चन्दनलोलितैः ।
जुहुयात्कवितां मन्त्री लभते वत्सरान्तरे ॥
1.87.m: With flowers of mālatī and bakula smeared with sandalwood paste, / the practitioner of mantra should make fire oblations; he attains poetic mastery within a year.

1.87.s:
madhuratraghayasaṃyuktaiḥ phalairbilvasamudbhavaiḥ /
juhuyādvāśayellokaṃ śriyaṃ prāpnoti vāñchitām //
1.87.d:
मधुरत्रघयसंयुक्तैः फलैर्बिल्वसमुद्भवैः ।
जुहुयाद्वाशयेल्लोकं श्रियं प्राप्नोति वाञ्छिताम् ॥
1.87.m: With bilva fruits mixed with the three sweets, / he should offer oblations; he subjugates people and obtains the fortune he desires.

1.87.s:
sājyamannaṃ prajuhuyādbhavedannasamṛddhimān /
kastūrīkuṅkumopetaṃ karpūraṃ juhuyādvaśī //
1.87.d:
साज्यमन्नं प्रजुहुयाद्भवेदन्नसमृद्धिमान् ।
कस्तूरीकुङ्कुमोपेतं कर्पूरं जुहुयाद्वशी ॥
1.87.m: He should offer cooked food with ghee into the fire; he becomes rich in food. / A master of self should offer camphor mixed with musk and saffron;

1.87.s:
kandarpādadhikaṃ sadyaḥ saindaryamadhigacchati /
lājānprajuhuyānmantrī dadhikṣīramadhuplutān //
1.87.d:
कन्दर्पादधिकं सद्यः सैन्दर्यमधिगच्छति ।
लाजान्प्रजुहुयान्मन्त्री दधिक्षीरमधुप्लुतान् ॥
1.87.m: he instantly acquires beauty surpassing that of Kandarpa. / The practitioner of mantra should offer oblations of puffed rice drenched in curd, milk, and honey;

1.87.s:
vijitya rogānakhilānsa jīveccharadāṃ śatam /
pādadvayaṃ malayajaṃ pādaṃ kuṅkumakesaram //
1.87.d:
विजित्य रोगानखिलान्स जीवेच्छरदां शतम् ।
पादद्वयं मलयजं पादं कुङ्कुमकेसरम् ॥
1.87.m: having conquered all diseases, he will live for a hundred autumns. / Two parts sandalwood, one part saffron filaments,

1.87.s:
pādaṃ gorocanāntāni trīṇi piṣṭvāhimāṃbhasā /
vidadhyāttilakaṃ bhāle yānpaśyedyairvilokyate //
1.87.d:
पादं गोरोचनान्तानि त्रीणि पिष्ट्वाहिमांभसा ।
विदध्यात्तिलकं भाले यान्पश्येद्यैर्विलोक्यते ॥
1.87.m: and one part gorocanā: having ground these three with cold water, / one should apply a mark on the forehead; whomever one sees, or by whomever one is looked upon,

1.87.s:
yānspṛśetspṛśyate yairvā vaśyāḥ syustasya te 'cirāt /
karpūrakapicorāṇi samabhāgāni kalpayet //
1.87.d:
यान्स्पृशेत्स्पृश्यते यैर्वा वश्याः स्युस्तस्य ते ऽचिरात् ।
कर्पूरकपिचोराणि समभागानि कल्पयेत् ॥
1.87.m: whomever one touches, or by whomever one is touched, will quickly fall under his sway. / One should measure equal parts of camphor and kapicora;

1.87.s:
caturbhujā jaṭāmāṃsī tāvatī rocanā matā /
kuṅkumaṃ samabhāgaṃ syāddigbhātaṃ candanaṃ matam //
1.87.d:
चतुर्भुजा जटामांसी तावती रोचना मता ।
कुङ्कुमं समभागं स्याद्दिग्भातं चन्दनं मतम् ॥
1.87.m: four parts of jaṭāmāṃsī, and an equal amount of gorocanā is prescribed; / saffron should be an equal part, and sandalwood is deemed ten parts;

1.87.s:
agururnavabhāgaṃ syāditibhāgakrameṇa ca /
himādbhiḥ kanyayā piṣṭametatsarvaṃ susādhitam //
1.87.d:
अगुरुर्नवभागं स्यादितिभागक्रमेण च ।
हिमाद्भिः कन्यया पिष्टमेतत्सर्वं सुसाधितम् ॥
1.87.m: aguru should be nine parts—in accordance with this sequence of proportions; / ground by a maiden with cold water, all this is properly prepared.

1.87.s:
ādāya tilakaṃ bhāle kuryyādbhūmipatīnnarān /
vanitāmadagarvāḍhyā madonmattānmatandajān //
1.87.d:
आदाय तिलकं भाले कुर्य्याद्भूमिपतीन्नरान् ।
वनितामदगर्वाढ्या मदोन्मत्तान्मतन्दजान् ॥
1.87.m: Taking it, he should make a mark on his forehead: kings, men, / women rich in passion and pride, rut-maddened elephants,

1.87.s:
siṃhavyāghrānmahāsarpānbhūtavetālarākṣasān /
darśanādeva vaśayettilakaṃ dhārayannaraḥ //
1.87.d:
सिंहव्याघ्रान्महासर्पान्भूतवेतालराक्षसान् ।
दर्शनादेव वशयेत्तिलकं धारयन्नरः ॥
1.87.m: lions, tigers, great serpents, spirits, vetālas, and rākṣasas, / he brings under sway merely by sight, wearing that mark on his forehead.

1.87.s:
ityeṣā bhairavī proktā hyavatārāntaraṃ śṛṇu /
vāṅmāyā kamalā tāro namonte bhagavatyatha //
1.87.d:
इत्येषा भैरवी प्रोक्ता ह्यवतारान्तरं शृणु ।
वाङ्माया कमला तारो नमोन्ते भगवत्यथ ॥
1.87.m: Thus has this Bhairavī been declared; now listen to another manifestation: / the speech-syllable, the māyā-syllable, the kamalā-syllable, and the tāra-syllable, then 'namaḥ' at the end, then 'bhagavati',

1.87.s:
śrīmātaṅgeśvari vadetsarvajanamanohari /
sarvādisukharājyante sarvādisukharañjanī //
1.87.d:
श्रीमातङ्गेश्वरि वदेत्सर्वजनमनोहरि ।
सर्वादिसुखराज्यन्ते सर्वादिसुखरञ्जनी ॥
1.87.m: one should say 'śrīmātaṅgeśvari', then 'sarvajanamanohari', / after 'sarvādisukharājya', 'sarvādisukharañjanī',

1.87.s:
sarvarājavaśaṃ paścātkarisarvapadaṃ vadet /
strīpuruṣavaśaṃ sṛṣṭividyākrodhinikānvitā //
1.87.d:
सर्वराजवशं पश्चात्करिसर्वपदं वदेत् ।
स्त्रीपुरुषवशं सृष्टिविद्याक्रोधिनिकान्विता ॥
1.87.m: then 'sarvarājavaśaṅkari', then one should utter the word 'sarva', / 'strīpuruṣavaśaṅkari', followed by 'vidyākrodhinī',

1.87.s:
sarvaṃ duṣṭamṛgavaśaṃ karisarvapadaṃ tataḥ /
sarvasattvavaśaṅkarisarvalokaṃ tataḥ param //
1.87.d:
सर्वं दुष्टमृगवशं करिसर्वपदं ततः ।
सर्वसत्त्ववशङ्करिसर्वलोकं ततः परम् ॥
1.87.m: 'sarvaduṣṭamṛgavaśaṅkari', then the word 'sarva', / 'sarvasattvavaśaṅkari', and after that 'sarvaloka-',

1.87.s:
amukaṃ me vaśaṃ paścādānayānalasundarī /
aṣṭāśītyakṣaro mantro munyādyā bhairavīgatāḥ //
1.87.d:
अमुकं मे वशं पश्चादानयानलसुन्दरी ।
अष्टाशीत्यक्षरो मन्त्रो मुन्याद्या भैरवीगताः ॥
1.87.m: '[bring] so-and-so into my control', then 'ānaya analasundarī svāhā'. / This is the eighty-eight-syllable mantra; its sage and other [presiding entities] are those belonging to Bhairavī.

1.87.s:
nyāsānmantrī tanau kuryādvakṣyamāṇānyathākramam /
śirolalāṭabhrūmadhye tālukaṇṭhagalorasi //
1.87.d:
न्यासान्मन्त्री तनौ कुर्याद्वक्ष्यमाणान्यथाक्रमम् ।
शिरोललाटभ्रूमध्ये तालुकण्ठगलोरसि ॥
1.87.m: The practitioner of mantra should perform the ritual placements on the body to be described, in due order: / on the head, forehead, between the eyebrows, palate, throat, neck, chest,

1.87.s:
anāhate bhujadvandve jaṭhare nābhimaṇḍale /
svādhiṣṭhāne guptadeśe pādayordakṣavāmayoḥ //
1.87.d:
अनाहते भुजद्वन्द्वे जठरे नाभिमण्डले ।
स्वाधिष्ठाने गुप्तदेशे पादयोर्दक्षवामयोः ॥
1.87.m: the heart-lotus, the pair of arms, the belly, the navel circle, / the svādhiṣṭhāna, the private part, and the right and left feet,

1.87.s:
mūlādhāre gude nyasyetpadānyaṣṭādaśa kramāt /
guṇaikadvicatuḥ ṣaḍbhirvasuparvanavāṣṭabhiḥ //
1.87.d:
मूलाधारे गुदे न्यस्येत्पदान्यष्टादश क्रमात् ।
गुणैकद्विचतुः षड्भिर्वसुपर्वनवाष्टभिः ॥
1.87.m: on the mūlādhāra and the anus, one should place the eighteen parts in order, / with [units of] three, one, two, four, six, eight, joint [six], nine, eight,

1.87.s:
nandapaṅktyaṣṭavedāgnicandrayugmaguṇā kṣibhiḥ /
yadukḷptiriyaṃ proktā mantravarṇairyathākramam //
1.87.d:
नन्दपङ्क्त्यष्टवेदाग्निचन्द्रयुग्मगुणा क्षिभिः ।
यदुकॢप्तिरियं प्रोक्ता मन्त्रवर्णैर्यथाक्रमम् ॥
1.87.m: nine, ten, eight, four, three, one, two, three, and two [syllables]. / This division is proclaimed according to the letters of the mantra in due sequence.

1.87.s:
ratyādyā mṛlahṛdayabhrumadhyeṣu vicakṣaṇaḥ /
vākśaktilakṣmībījādyā mātaṅgyantāḥ pravinyaset //
1.87.d:
रत्याद्या मृलहृदयभ्रुमध्येषु विचक्षणः ।
वाक्शक्तिलक्ष्मीबीजाद्या मातङ्ग्यन्ताः प्रविन्यसेत् ॥
1.87.m: The wise man should place Rati and the other [śaktis] at the mūla, heart, and between the eyebrows, / preceded by the seed-syllables of speech, śakti, and Lakṣmī, ending with 'Mātaṅgī'.

1.87.s:
śirovadanahṛdguhyapādeṣu vidhinā nyaset /
hṛllekhāṃ gaganāṃ raktāṃ bhūyo mantrī karālikām //
1.87.d:
शिरोवदनहृद्गुह्यपादेषु विधिना न्यसेत् ।
हृल्लेखां गगनां रक्तां भूयो मन्त्री करालिकाम् ॥
1.87.m: He should place them according to rule on the head, face, heart, private region, and feet. / The practitioner of mantra should again place Hṛllekhā, Gaganā, Raktā, Karālikā,

1.87.s:
mahocchuṣmāṃ svanāmādivarṇabījapuraḥ sarāḥ /
mātaṅgyantāḥ ṣaḍaṅgāni tataḥ kurvīta sādhakaḥ //
1.87.d:
महोच्छुष्मां स्वनामादिवर्णबीजपुरः सराः ।
मातङ्ग्यन्ताः षडङ्गानि ततः कुर्वीत साधकः ॥
1.87.m: and Mahocchuṣmā, preceded by the seed-letters of their own names, / and ending with 'Mātaṅgī'. Then the adept should perform the six limbs.

1.87.s:
varṇaiścaturviṃśatibhirhṛttrayodaśabhiḥ śiraḥ /
śikhāṣṭādaśabhiḥ proktā varma tāvadbhirakṣaraiḥ //
1.87.d:
वर्णैश्चतुर्विंशतिभिर्हृत्त्रयोदशभिः शिरः ।
शिखाष्टादशभिः प्रोक्ता वर्म तावद्भिरक्षरैः ॥
1.87.m: The heart is taught with twenty-four syllables, the head with thirteen, / the topknot with eighteen, and the armor with as many syllables;

1.87.s:
syāttrayodaśabhirnetraṃ dvābhyāmastraṃ prakīrtitam /
bāṇanyāsaṃ tataḥ kuryādbhairavīproktavartmanā //
1.87.d:
स्यात्त्रयोदशभिर्नेत्रं द्वाभ्यामस्त्रं प्रकीर्तितम् ।
बाणन्यासं ततः कुर्याद्भैरवीप्रोक्तवर्त्मना ॥
1.87.m: the eyes with thirteen, and the weapon is declared to be with two. / Then he should perform the arrow placement according to the path taught for Bhairavī.

1.87.s:
mātaṅgīpadayoścānyaṃ manmathānvadanāṃśayoḥ /
pārsvakaṭyornābhideśe kaṭipārśvāṃśake punaḥ //
1.87.d:
मातङ्गीपदयोश्चान्यं मन्मथान्वदनांशयोः ।
पार्स्वकट्योर्नाभिदेशे कटिपार्श्वांशके पुनः ॥
1.87.m: Ending with the word 'Mātaṅgī', and the other with Manmatha, on the face and shoulders, / on the flanks and hips, in the navel region, and again on the hips, flanks, and shoulders,

1.87.s:
bījatrayādikānmantrī manmathaṃ makaradhvajam /
madanaṃ puṣpadhanvānaṃ pañcamaṃ kusumāyudham //
1.87.d:
बीजत्रयादिकान्मन्त्री मन्मथं मकरध्वजम् ।
मदनं पुष्पधन्वानं पञ्चमं कुसुमायुधम् ॥
1.87.m: preceded by the three seed-syllables, the practitioner of mantra [places] Manmatha, Makaradhvaja, / Madana, Puṣpadhanvan, and fifth, Kusumāyudha,

1.87.s:
ṣaṣṭhaṃ kandarpanāmānaṃ manobhavaratipriyau /
mātaṅgyantāstato nyasyetsthāneṣveteṣu mantravit //
1.87.d:
षष्ठं कन्दर्पनामानं मनोभवरतिप्रियौ ।
मातङ्ग्यन्तास्ततो न्यस्येत्स्थानेष्वेतेषु मन्त्रवित् ॥
1.87.m: sixth, the one named Kandarpa, Manobhava, and Ratipriya; / ending with 'Mātaṅgī', the knower of mantra should then place them in these positions:

1.87.s:
kusumā mekhalā caiva madanā madanā turā /
madanavegā sambhavā ca bhuvanapālendurekhikā //
1.87.d:
कुसुमा मेखला चैव मदना मदना तुरा ।
मदनवेगा सम्भवा च भुवनपालेन्दुरेखिका ॥
1.87.m: Kusumā, Mekhalā, Madanā, Madanāturā, / Madanavegā, Sambhavā, Bhuvanapālā, and Indurekhikā,

1.87.s:
anaṅgapadapūrvāśca mātaṅgyantāḥ samīritāḥ /
vinyastavyāstato mūle 'dhiṣṭhāne maṇipūrake //
1.87.d:
अनङ्गपदपूर्वाश्च मातङ्ग्यन्ताः समीरिताः ।
विन्यस्तव्यास्ततो मूले ऽधिष्ठाने मणिपूरके ॥
1.87.m: preceded by the word 'Anaṅga' and ending with 'Mātaṅgī', are proclaimed. / They are then to be placed in the mūla, the adhiṣṭhāna, the maṇipūraka,

1.87.s:
hṛtkaṇṭhāsye bhruvormadhye mastake cāpi matriṇā /
ādye lakṣmīsarasvatyau ratiḥ prītiśca kṛttikā //
1.87.d:
हृत्कण्ठास्ये भ्रुवोर्मध्ये मस्तके चापि मत्रिणा ।
आद्ये लक्ष्मीसरस्वत्यौ रतिः प्रीतिश्च कृत्तिका ॥
1.87.m: the heart, the throat, the face, between the eyebrows, and on the head by the practitioner of mantra. / First, Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī, Rati, Prīti, and Kṛttikā,

1.87.s:
śāntiḥ puṣṭiḥ punastuṣṭimārtagaṃpadaśekharā /
mūlamantraṃ pṛthaṅnyasyennijamūrddhani mantravit //
1.87.d:
शान्तिः पुष्टिः पुनस्तुष्टिमार्तगंपदशेखरा ।
मूलमन्त्रं पृथङ्न्यस्येन्निजमूर्द्धनि मन्त्रवित् ॥
1.87.m: Śānti, Puṣṭi, and again Tuṣṭi, crowned with the word 'Mātaṅgī'. / The knower of mantra should place the root mantra separately on his own head,

1.87.s:
ādhāradeśe 'dhiṣṭhāne nābhau paścādanāhate /
kaṇṭhadeśe bhravormadhye bindau bhūyaḥ kalā padoḥ //
1.87.d:
आधारदेशे ऽधिष्ठाने नाभौ पश्चादनाहते ।
कण्ठदेशे भ्रवोर्मध्ये बिन्दौ भूयः कला पदोः ॥
1.87.m: in the region of the ādhāra, in the adhiṣṭhāna, in the navel, next in the anāhata, / in the throat region, between the eyebrows, at the bindu, then at the kalā and the padas,

1.87.s:
nirodhikāyāmarddhendunāde nādāntayoḥ punaḥ /
unnatāṃseṣu vaktre ca dhruvamaṇḍalake śive //
1.87.d:
निरोधिकायामर्द्धेन्दुनादे नादान्तयोः पुनः ।
उन्नतांसेषु वक्त्रे च ध्रुवमण्डलके शिवे ॥
1.87.m: in the nirodhikā, the crescent moon, the sound, and at the ends of the sound, / on the elevated shoulders, in the mouth, and in the dhruvamaṇḍala, the auspicious center.

1.87.s:
mātaṅgyantāḥ pravinyasye dvāmāṃ jyeṣṭhamataḥ param /
raudrīṃ praśāntāṃ śraddhākhyāṃ punarmāheśvarīmatha //
1.87.d:
मातङ्ग्यन्ताः प्रविन्यस्ये द्वामां ज्येष्ठमतः परम् ।
रौद्रीं प्रशान्तां श्रद्धाख्यां पुनर्माहेश्वरीमथ ॥
1.87.m: Ending with 'Mātaṅgī', he should place Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, after that / Raudrī, Praśāntā, the one called Śraddhā, and further Māheśvarī,

1.87.s:
kriyāśaktiṃ sulakṣmīṃ ca sṛṣṭiṃ saṃjñāṃ ca mohinīm /
pramathāśvāsinīṃ vidyullatāṃ cicchaktimapyatha //
1.87.d:
क्रियाशक्तिं सुलक्ष्मीं च सृष्टिं संज्ञां च मोहिनीम् ।
प्रमथाश्वासिनीं विद्युल्लतां चिच्छक्तिमप्यथ ॥
1.87.m: Kriyāśakti, Sulakṣmī, Sṛṣṭi, Saṃjñā, and Mohinī, / Pramathā, Āśvāsinī, Vidyullatā, and Cicchakti,

1.87.s:
tataśca sundarīṃ nindāṃ nandabuddhimimāḥ kramāt /
śirobhālahṛdādhāreṣvetā bījatrayādhikāḥ //
1.87.d:
ततश्च सुन्दरीं निन्दां नन्दबुद्धिमिमाः क्रमात् ।
शिरोभालहृदाधारेष्वेता बीजत्रयाधिकाः ॥
1.87.m: and then Sundarī, Nindā, and Nandabuddhi, in order. / Augmented with the three seed-syllables, on the head, forehead, heart, and ādhāra,

1.87.s:
mātaṅgyādyāḥ pravinyasyedyathāvaddeśikottamaḥ /
mātaṅgīṃ mahadādyāṃ tāṃ mahālakṣmīpadādikām //
1.87.d:
मातङ्ग्याद्याः प्रविन्यस्येद्यथावद्देशिकोत्तमः ।
मातङ्गीं महदाद्यां तां महालक्ष्मीपदादिकाम् ॥
1.87.m: the excellent teacher should duly place these, beginning with 'Mātaṅgī': / Mātaṅgī beginning with Mahat, and that one beginning with the word 'Mahālakṣmī'.

1.87.s:
siddhalakṣmīpadādyāṃ ca mūlamādhāramaṇḍalam /
nyasettenaiva kurvīta vyāpakaṃ deśikottamaḥ //
1.87.d:
सिद्धलक्ष्मीपदाद्यां च मूलमाधारमण्डलम् ।
न्यसेत्तेनैव कुर्वीत व्यापकं देशिकोत्तमः ॥
1.87.m: The best of teachers should perform the ritual placement of the root and the supportive maṇḍala / beginning with the word 'siddhalakṣmī', and with that very [mantra] perform the comprehensive permeation.

1.87.s:
evaṃ nyastaśarīro 'sau cintayenmantradevatām /
śyāmāṃ śukoktiṃ śṛṇvantīṃ nyastaikāṅghriśiroruhām //
1.87.d:
एवं न्यस्तशरीरो ऽसौ चिन्तयेन्मन्त्रदेवताम् ।
श्यामां शुकोक्तिं शृण्वन्तीं न्यस्तैकाङ्घ्रिशिरोरुहाम् ॥
1.87.m: Having thus placed [the mantra upon] his body, he should contemplate the deity of the mantra: / dark-complexioned, listening to the words of a parrot, one foot placed upon the hair of [Śiva's] head,

1.87.s:
śaśikhaṇḍadharāṃ vīṇāṃ vādayantīṃ madhūnmadām /
raktāṃśukāṃ ca kahlāramālāśobhitacūlikām //
1.87.d:
शशिखण्डधरां वीणां वादयन्तीं मधून्मदाम् ।
रक्तांशुकां च कह्लारमालाशोभितचूलिकाम् ॥
1.87.m: bearing the crescent moon, playing the vīṇā, intoxicated with honey-wine, / clad in red garments, her crest of hair adorned with a garland of white water-lilies,

1.87.s:
śaṅkhapatrāṃ tu mātaṅgīṃ citrakodbhāsimastakām /
ayutaṃ prajapenmantraṃ taddaśāṃśaṃ madhūkajaiḥ //
1.87.d:
शङ्खपत्रां तु मातङ्गीं चित्रकोद्भासिमस्तकाम् ।
अयुतं प्रजपेन्मन्त्रं तद्दशांशं मधूकजैः ॥
1.87.m: wearing ear ornaments of conch shell, Mātaṅgī, her forehead gleaming with decorative sectarian marks. / He should recite the mantra ten thousand times, and [offer] a tenth of that with blossoms

1.87.s:
puṣpaistrimadhuropetairjuhuyānmantrasiddhaye /
trikoṇakarṇikaṃ padmamaṣṭapatraṃ prakalpayet //
1.87.d:
पुष्पैस्त्रिमधुरोपेतैर्जुहुयान्मन्त्रसिद्धये ।
त्रिकोणकर्णिकं पद्ममष्टपत्रं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
1.87.m: produced from the Madhūka tree mixed with the three sweet substances, to achieve the mantra's perfection. / One should fashion an eight-petalled lotus whose pericarp is a triangle,

1.87.s:
aṣṭapatrāvṛtaṃ bāhye vṛtaṃ ṣoḍaśabhirdalaiḥ /
caturasrīkṛtaṃ bāhye kāntyā dṛṣṭimanoharam //
1.87.d:
अष्टपत्रावृतं बाह्ये वृतं षोडशभिर्दलैः ।
चतुरस्रीकृतं बाह्ये कान्त्या दृष्टिमनोहरम् ॥
1.87.m: surrounded on the outside by eight petals, surrounded by sixteen petals, / squared on the exterior, delighting the sight with its beauty.

1.87.s:
etasminpūjayetpīṭhe navaśaktīḥ kramādimāḥ /
vibhūtipūrvāḥ pūrvoktā mātaṅgīpadapaścimāḥ //
1.87.d:
एतस्मिन्पूजयेत्पीठे नवशक्तीः क्रमादिमाः ।
विभूतिपूर्वाः पूर्वोक्ता मातङ्गीपदपश्चिमाः ॥
1.87.m: On this ritual seat one should worship these nine powers in proper order: / those mentioned earlier beginning with Vibhūti, and ending with the word 'mātaṅgī';

1.87.s:
sarvānte śaktikamalāsanāya nama ityatha /
vāksatyalakṣmī bījādya uktaḥ pīṭhārcane manuḥ //
1.87.d:
सर्वान्ते शक्तिकमलासनाय नम इत्यथ ।
वाक्सत्यलक्ष्मी बीजाद्य उक्तः पीठार्चने मनुः ॥
1.87.m: then ending with 'śaktikamalāsanāya namaḥ' for all of them. / The mantra beginning with the seed-syllables Vāc, Satya, and Lakṣmī has been declared for worshipping the ritual seat.

1.87.s:
mūlena mūrtiṃ saṃkalpya tasyāmāvāhya devatām /
arcayedvidhinānena vakṣyamāṇena mantravit //
1.87.d:
मूलेन मूर्तिं संकल्प्य तस्यामावाह्य देवताम् ।
अर्चयेद्विधिनानेन वक्ष्यमाणेन मन्त्रवित् ॥
1.87.m: Having visualized the form with the root mantra and invoked the deity into it, / the knower of mantra should worship according to this procedure that will be explained.

1.87.s:
ratyādyāstriṣu koṇeṣu pūjayetpūrvavatsudhīḥ /
hṛhṛllekhāḥ pañcapūjyā madhye dikṣu ca mantriṇā //
1.87.d:
रत्याद्यास्त्रिषु कोणेषु पूजयेत्पूर्ववत्सुधीः ।
हृहृल्लेखाः पञ्चपूज्या मध्ये दिक्षु च मन्त्रिणा ॥
1.87.m: The wise practitioner should worship Rati and the others in the three corners as before. / In the centre and in the directions, five Hṛllekhā mantras should be worshipped by the practitioner,

1.87.s:
pāśāṅkuśābhayābhīṣṭadhāriṇyo bhūtasaprabhāḥ /
aṅgāni pūjayetpaścādyathāpūrvaṃ vidhānavit //
1.87.d:
पाशाङ्कुशाभयाभीष्टधारिण्यो भूतसप्रभाः ।
अङ्गानि पूजयेत्पश्चाद्यथापूर्वं विधानवित् ॥
1.87.m: holding a noose, a goad, the gesture of fearlessness, and the gesture granting desires, radiant like spirits. / Knowing the ritual procedure, he should then worship the limbs as before.

1.87.s:
bāṇānabhyarcayeddikṣu pañcamaṃ purato yajet /
dalamadhye 'tha saṃpūjyā anaṅgakusumādikāḥ //
1.87.d:
बाणानभ्यर्चयेद्दिक्षु पञ्चमं पुरतो यजेत् ।
दलमध्ये ऽथ संपूज्या अनङ्गकुसुमादिकाः ॥
1.87.m: He should worship the arrows in the cardinal directions, and the fifth in front. / Then in the middle of the petals, [the deities] beginning with Anaṅgakusumā are to be worshipped,

1.87.s:
pāśāṅkuśābhayābhīṣṭadhāriṇyo 'ruṇavigrahāḥ /
patrāgreṣu punaḥ pūjyā lakṣmyādyā vallakīkarāḥ //
1.87.d:
पाशाङ्कुशाभयाभीष्टधारिण्यो ऽरुणविग्रहाः ।
पत्राग्रेषु पुनः पूज्या लक्ष्म्याद्या वल्लकीकराः ॥
1.87.m: holding a noose, a goad, the gesture of fearlessness, and the gesture granting desires, with red bodies. / Again, on the tips of the petals, those beginning with Lakṣmī, holding vīṇās in their hands, are to be worshipped.

1.87.s:
bahiraṣṭadaleṣvarcyā manmathādyā madoddhatāḥ /
aparāṅgā niṣaṅgādyāḥ puṣpāstreṣudhanurddharāḥ //
1.87.d:
बहिरष्टदलेष्वर्च्या मन्मथाद्या मदोद्धताः ।
अपराङ्गा निषङ्गाद्याः पुष्पास्त्रेषुधनुर्द्धराः ॥
1.87.m: On the outer eight petals, those beginning with Manmatha, insolent with intoxication, / with other limbs [adorned], equipped with quivers, holding flower arrows and bows, should be worshipped.

1.87.s:
patrasthā mātaraḥ pūjyā brāhmādyāḥ proktalakṣaṇāḥ /
tadagreṣvarcayedvidvānasitāṅgādibhairavān //
1.87.d:
पत्रस्था मातरः पूज्या ब्राह्माद्याः प्रोक्तलक्षणाः ।
तदग्रेष्वर्चयेद्विद्वानसिताङ्गादिभैरवान् ॥
1.87.m: The Mothers positioned on the petals, beginning with Brāhmī and possessing the characteristics described, are to be worshipped. / In front of them the wise practitioner should worship the Bhairavas beginning with Asitāṅga.

1.87.s:
punaḥ ṣoḍaśa patreṣu pūjyāḥ ṣoḍaśa śaktayaḥ /
vāmādyāḥ kalavīṇābhirgāyantyaḥ śyāmavigrahāḥ //
1.87.d:
पुनः षोडश पत्रेषु पूज्याः षोडश शक्तयः ।
वामाद्याः कलवीणाभिर्गायन्त्यः श्यामविग्रहाः ॥
1.87.m: Again, on the sixteen petals the sixteen powers are to be worshipped: / Vāmā and the others, singing with sweet-sounding vīṇās, having dark forms.

1.87.s:
caturasre caturdikṣu catasraḥ pūjayetpunaḥ /
mātaṅgyādyāmadonmattā vīṇollasitapāṇayaḥ //
1.87.d:
चतुरस्रे चतुर्दिक्षु चतस्रः पूजयेत्पुनः ।
मातङ्ग्याद्यामदोन्मत्ता वीणोल्लसितपाणयः ॥
1.87.m: On the square [enclosure], in the four directions, one should again worship the four / beginning with Mātaṅgī, mad with intoxication, their hands resplendent with vīṇās.

1.87.s:
āgneyakoṇe vighneśaṃ durgāṃ naiśācareḥ yajet /
vāyavye baṭukān paścādīśāne kṣetrapaṃ yajet //
1.87.d:
आग्नेयकोणे विघ्नेशं दुर्गां नैशाचरेः यजेत् ।
वायव्ये बटुकान् पश्चादीशाने क्षेत्रपं यजेत् ॥
1.87.m: In the south-eastern corner one should worship Vighneśa, and in the south-western Durga. / In the north-western he should worship the Baṭukas, and subsequently Kṣetrapa in the north-eastern.

1.87.s:
lokapālā bahiḥ pūjyā vajrādyairāyudhaiḥ saha /
mantre 'sminsaṃdhite mantrī sādhayediṣṭamātmanaḥ //
1.87.d:
लोकपाला बहिः पूज्या वज्राद्यैरायुधैः सह ।
मन्त्रे ऽस्मिन्संधिते मन्त्री साधयेदिष्टमात्मनः ॥
1.87.m: The guardians of the world are to be worshipped outside together with their weapons, such as the thunderbolt. / When this mantra is mastered, the practitioner achieves his desired goal.

1.87.s:
mallikājātipunnāgairhemādbhāgyālayo bhavet /
phalaurbilyasamudbhūtaistatpatrairvā hutādbhavet //
1.87.d:
मल्लिकाजातिपुन्नागैर्हेमाद्भाग्यालयो भवेत् ।
फलौर्बिल्यसमुद्भूतैस्तत्पत्रैर्वा हुताद्भवेत् ॥
1.87.m: From a fire oblation with mallikā, jātī, and punnāga flowers, one becomes an abode of good fortune. / From an oblation of bilva fruits or with its leaves,

1.87.s:
rājaputrasya rājyāptiḥ paṅkajaiḥ śriyamāpnuyāt /
utpalairvaśayedviśvaṃ kṣārairmadhvāśritaiḥ striyam //
1.87.d:
राजपुत्रस्य राज्याप्तिः पङ्कजैः श्रियमाप्नुयात् ।
उत्पलैर्वशयेद्विश्वं क्षारैर्मध्वाश्रितैः स्त्रियम् ॥
1.87.m: a prince attains a kingdom. With lotuses one obtains fortune. / With blue water lilies one can subjugate the universe; with ashes mixed with honey, a woman.

1.87.s:
vañjulasya samidbhomo vṛṣṭiṃ vitanute 'cirāt /
kṣīrāktairamṛtākhaṇḍairhemānnāśayati jvaram //
1.87.d:
वञ्जुलस्य समिद्भोमो वृष्टिं वितनुते ऽचिरात् ।
क्षीराक्तैरमृताखण्डैर्हेमान्नाशयति ज्वरम् ॥
1.87.m: A fire oblation with kindling sticks of vañjula quickly causes rain. / By oblations of pieces of amṛtā smeared with milk, he destroys fever.

1.87.s:
dūrvābhirāyurāpnoti tandulairdhanavānbhavet /
kadaṃbairvaśyamāpnoti sarvaṃ trimadhuraplutam //
1.87.d:
दूर्वाभिरायुराप्नोति तन्दुलैर्धनवान्भवेत् ।
कदंबैर्वश्यमाप्नोति सर्वं त्रिमधुरप्लुतम् ॥
1.87.m: Through dūrvā grass he gains long life; through grains of rice he becomes wealthy. / With kadamba flowers he obtains subjugation; everything should be bathed in the three sweets.

1.87.s:
nandyāvartabhavaiḥ puṣpairhemo vāksiddhidāyakaḥ /
niṃbaprasūnairjuhuyādīpsitaśrīsamṛddhaye //
1.87.d:
नन्द्यावर्तभवैः पुष्पैर्हेमो वाक्सिद्धिदायकः ।
निंबप्रसूनैर्जुहुयादीप्सितश्रीसमृद्धये ॥
1.87.m: A fire oblation with flowers born of the nandyāvarta grants perfection of speech. / One should offer with nimba blossoms for prosperity and desired fortune.

1.87.s:
palāśakusumairhemāttejasvī jāyate naraḥ /
candanāgurukastūrī candrakuṅkumarocanāḥ //
1.87.d:
पलाशकुसुमैर्हेमात्तेजस्वी जायते नरः ।
चन्दनागुरुकस्तूरी चन्द्रकुङ्कुमरोचनाः ॥
1.87.m: From a fire oblation with palāśa blossoms, a man becomes radiant. / Sandalwood, agallochum, musk, camphor, saffron, and rocanā,

1.87.s:
vaśyāya ca priyatvāya hutāśca tilakīkṛtāḥ /
nirguṇḍīmūlahomena nigaḍānmucyate naraḥ //
1.87.d:
वश्याय च प्रियत्वाय हुताश्च तिलकीकृताः ।
निर्गुण्डीमूलहोमेन निगडान्मुच्यते नरः ॥
1.87.m: offered in the fire and applied as a forehead mark, lead to subjugation and fondness. / By a fire oblation of nirguṇḍī roots, a man is freed from fetters.

1.87.s:
niṃbatailānvitairloṇairhemaḥ śatruvināśanaḥ /
haridrācūrṇasaṃmiśrairlavaṇaiḥ staṃbhayejjagat //
1.87.d:
निंबतैलान्वितैर्लोणैर्हेमः शत्रुविनाशनः ।
हरिद्राचूर्णसंमिश्रैर्लवणैः स्तंभयेज्जगत् ॥
1.87.m: A fire oblation with salt mixed with nimba oil destroys enemies. / With salt mixed with turmeric powder, one can paralyze the world.

1.87.s:
mātaṅgīsiddhavidyaiṣā proktā te dvijasattama /
avatārāntaraṃ bhūyo varṇayāmi niśāmaya //
1.87.d:
मातङ्गीसिद्धविद्यैषा प्रोक्ता ते द्विजसत्तम ।
अवतारान्तरं भूयो वर्णयामि निशामय ॥
1.87.m: This proven lore of Mātaṅgī has been told to you, O best of the twice-born. / Now hear another incarnation, which I shall describe further.

1.87.s:
dīpakāprīticandrāḍhyā dvidhā cedrañjitāpunaḥ /
vativahnipriyāmantro dhūmāvatyā gajākṣaraḥ //
1.87.d:
दीपकाप्रीतिचन्द्राढ्या द्विधा चेद्रञ्जितापुनः ।
वतिवह्निप्रियामन्त्रो धूमावत्या गजाक्षरः ॥
1.87.m: Provided with dīpaka, aprīti, and the moon, twice colored again, / ending with the wife of fire: such is Dhūmāvatī's eight-syllable mantra.

1.87.s:
pippalādo muniśchando nivṛddhūmāvatīśvarī /
bījena ṣaḍdīrghajātiyuktena parikalpayet //
1.87.d:
पिप्पलादो मुनिश्छन्दो निवृद्धूमावतीश्वरी ।
बीजेन षड्दीर्घजातियुक्तेन परिकल्पयेत् ॥
1.87.m: The sage is Pippalāda; the metre is nivṛt; the deity is Dhūmāvatī. / One should construct [the limbs] with the bīja joined to the six long vowels.

1.87.s:
tato dhūmāvatīṃ dhyāyecchatrunigrahakāriṇīm /
vivarṇāṃ cañcalāṃ duṣṭāṃ dīrghāṃ ca malināṃbarām //
1.87.d:
ततो धूमावतीं ध्यायेच्छत्रुनिग्रहकारिणीम् ।
विवर्णां चञ्चलां दुष्टां दीर्घां च मलिनांबराम् ॥
1.87.m: Then one should meditate upon Dhūmāvatī, who effects the suppression of enemies: / discolored, restless, fierce, tall, wearing soiled garments,

1.87.s:
vimuktakuntalāṃ sūkṣmāṃ vidhavāṃ viraladvijām /
kaṅkadhvajarathārūḍhāṃ pralaṃbitapayodharam //
1.87.d:
विमुक्तकुन्तलां सूक्ष्मां विधवां विरलद्विजाम् ।
कङ्कध्वजरथारूढां प्रलंबितपयोधरम् ॥
1.87.m: with disheveled hair, emaciated, a widow with sparse teeth, / mounted on a chariot with a crow-banner, with hanging breasts,

1.87.s:
sūryahastāṃ nirukṣāṅkadhṛtahastāṃbarānvitām /
pravṛddhalomāṃ tu bhṛśaṃ kuṭilākuṭilekṣaṇām //
1.87.d:
सूर्यहस्तां निरुक्षाङ्कधृतहस्तांबरान्विताम् ।
प्रवृद्धलोमां तु भृशं कुटिलाकुटिलेक्षणाम् ॥
1.87.m: holding a winnowing basket, wearing dry clothes held in hand, / with an excessive growth of hair, and with exceedingly crooked eyes,

1.87.s:
kṣutpipāsārditāṃ nityaṃ bhayadāṃ kalahapriyām /
evaṃvidhāṃ tu saṃcintya namaḥ svāhā phaḍantakam //
1.87.d:
क्षुत्पिपासार्दितां नित्यं भयदां कलहप्रियाम् ।
एवंविधां तु संचिन्त्य नमः स्वाहा फडन्तकम् ॥
1.87.m: constantly tormented by hunger and thirst, terrifying, fond of quarrels. / Having thus meditated upon her, [with the mantra] ending in namaḥ, svāhā, and phaṭ,

1.87.s:
bījaṃ sādhyopari nyasya tasminsthāpya śavaṃ japet /
avaṣṭabhya śavaṃ śatrunāmnātha prajapenmanum //
1.87.d:
बीजं साध्योपरि न्यस्य तस्मिन्स्थाप्य शवं जपेत् ।
अवष्टभ्य शवं शत्रुनाम्नाथ प्रजपेन्मनुम् ॥
1.87.m: placing the bīja upon the target, setting a corpse thereon, one should recite. / Gripping the corpse, one should then recite the mantra with the enemy's name.

1.87.s:
soṣṇīṣakañcuko vidvānkṛṣṇe bhūte divāniśam /
upavāsī śmaśāne vā vipine śūnyamandire //
1.87.d:
सोष्णीषकञ्चुको विद्वान्कृष्णे भूते दिवानिशम् ।
उपवासी श्मशाने वा विपिने शून्यमन्दिरे ॥
1.87.m: Wearing a turban and armor, the learned man, in the dark half, on the fourteenth lunar day, day and night, / fasting in a cremation ground, or in a forest, or an empty house,

1.87.s:
mantrasya siddhyai yatavāgdhyāyandevīṃ nirantaram /
sahasrādūrddhūtaḥ śatrurjvareṇa parigṛhyate //
1.87.d:
मन्त्रस्य सिद्ध्यै यतवाग्ध्यायन्देवीं निरन्तरम् ।
सहस्रादूर्द्धूतः शत्रुर्ज्वरेण परिगृह्यते ॥
1.87.m: restraining his speech for the success of the mantra, meditating constantly on the goddess: / the enemy, agitated from a thousand [recitations], is seized by fever.

1.87.s:
pañcagavyena śāntiḥ syājjvarasya payasāpi vā /
mantrādyā kṣaramālikhya śatrūnāma tataḥ param //
1.87.d:
पञ्चगव्येन शान्तिः स्याज्ज्वरस्य पयसापि वा ।
मन्त्राद्या क्षरमालिख्य शत्रूनाम ततः परम् ॥
1.87.m: Relief of the fever comes from pañcagavya or from milk. / Having inscribed the first syllable of the mantra, then the enemy's name,

1.87.s:
dvitīyaṃ manuvarṇaṃ ca śatrunāmaivamālikhet /
sarvaṃ manudiksahasrajapācchavamṛtirbhavet //
1.87.d:
द्वितीयं मनुवर्णं च शत्रुनामैवमालिखेत् ।
सर्वं मनुदिक्सहस्रजपाच्छवमृतिर्भवेत् ॥
1.87.m: and the second syllable of the mantra, one should thus write the enemy's name. / From ten thousand recitations of the whole mantra, death of the corpse-like person occurs.

1.87.s:
dagdhvā kaṅkaṃ śyaśānāgnau tadbhasmādāya mantravit /
virodhināmnāṣṭaśataṃ japtamuccāṭanaṃ ripoḥ //
1.87.d:
दग्ध्वा कङ्कं श्यशानाग्नौ तद्भस्मादाय मन्त्रवित् ।
विरोधिनाम्नाष्टशतं जप्तमुच्चाटनं रिपोः ॥
1.87.m: Having burned a crow in the fire of the cremation ground and taken its ash, the mantra-knower, / reciting a hundred and eight times with the adversary's name, causes the enemy's expulsion.

1.87.s:
śmaśānabhasmanā kṛtvā śavaṃ tasyopari nyaset /
virodhināmasaṃruddhaṃ kṛṣṇe pakṣe samuccaret //
1.87.d:
श्मशानभस्मना कृत्वा शवं तस्योपरि न्यसेत् ।
विरोधिनामसंरुद्धं कृष्णे पक्षे समुच्चरेत् ॥
1.87.m: Having fashioned a corpse with ash from a cremation ground, one should place [the mantra] upon it; / one should utter it enclosed by the adversary's name during the dark fortnight.

1.87.s:
mahiṣīkṣīradhūpaṃ ca dadyācchatruvipatkaram /
evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ avatāracatuṣṭayam //
1.87.d:
महिषीक्षीरधूपं च दद्याच्छत्रुविपत्करम् ।
एवं संक्षेपतः प्रोक्तं अवतारचतुष्टयम् ॥
1.87.m: One should offer incense of buffalo milk, which causes calamity to the enemy. / Thus the four incarnations have been spoken of in brief

1.87.s:
durgāyā jagadaṃbāyāḥ kiṃ punaḥ praṣṭumicchasi //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde durgāmantracatuṣṭayavarṇanaṃ nāma saptāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.87.d:
दुर्गाया जगदंबायाः किं पुनः प्रष्टुमिच्छसि ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे दुर्गामन्त्रचतुष्टयवर्णनं नाम सप्ताशीतितमो ऽध्यायः
1.87.m:
of Durgā, the Mother of the Universe. What more do you wish to ask?

Thus ends the eighty-seventh chapter, entitled 'Description of the Four Mantras of Durgā,' in the third quarter of the Great Narrative in the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.88.s:
sūta uvāca
śrutvetthaṃ yajanaṃ viprā mantradhyānapuraḥsaram /
sarvāsāmavatārāṇāṃ nārado devadarśanaḥ //
1.88.d:
सूत उवाच
श्रुत्वेत्थं यजनं विप्रा मन्त्रध्यानपुरःसरम् ।
सर्वासामवताराणां नारदो देवदर्शनः ॥
1.88.m: Sūta said: / Having thus heard the worship along with the mantras and meditation, O Brahmins, / of all the incarnations, Nārada, who sees the gods,

1.88.s:
sarvādyāyā jaganmātuḥ śrīrādhāyāḥ samarcanam /
avatārakalānāṃ hi papraccha vinayānvitaḥ //
1.88.d:
सर्वाद्याया जगन्मातुः श्रीराधायाः समर्चनम् ।
अवतारकलानां हि पप्रच्छ विनयान्वितः ॥
1.88.m: asked, full of humility, about the worship of the primeval Mother of the Universe, / the glorious Rādhā, and about the parts of her incarnations.

1.88.s:
nārada uvāca
dhanyo 'smikṛtakṛtyo 'smi jāto 'haṃ tvatprasādataḥ /
pajjaganmātṛmantrāṇāṃ vaibhavaṃ śrutavānmune //
1.88.d:
नारद उवाच
धन्यो ऽस्मिकृतकृत्यो ऽस्मि जातो ऽहं त्वत्प्रसादतः ।
पज्जगन्मातृमन्त्राणां वैभवं श्रुतवान्मुने ॥
1.88.m: Nārada said: / I am blessed! I have accomplished my purpose through your grace, / since I have heard the glory of the mantras of the Mother of the Universe, O sage!

1.88.s:
yathā lakṣmīmukhānāṃ tu avatārāḥ prakīrtitāḥ /
tathā rādhāvatārāṇāṃ śrotumicchāmi vaibhavam //
1.88.d:
यथा लक्ष्मीमुखानां तु अवताराः प्रकीर्तिताः ।
तथा राधावताराणां श्रोतुमिच्छामि वैभवम् ॥
1.88.m: Just as the incarnations of Lakṣmī and others have been proclaimed, / so I wish to hear the glory of the incarnations of Rādhā.

1.88.s:
yatsaṃkhyākāśca yadrūpā yatprabhāvā vidāṃvara /
rādhāvatārāstānsatyaṃ kīrtayāśeṣasiddhidān //
1.88.d:
यत्संख्याकाश्च यद्रूपा यत्प्रभावा विदांवर ।
राधावतारास्तान्सत्यं कीर्तयाशेषसिद्धिदान् ॥
1.88.m: Whatever their number, form, and power, O best among the knowers: / tell truly of those incarnations of Rādhā which grant complete success!

1.88.s:
etacchutvā vacastasya nāradasya vidheḥ sutaḥ /
sanatkumāraḥ provāca dhyātvā rādhāpadāṃbujam //
1.88.d:
एतच्छुत्वा वचस्तस्य नारदस्य विधेः सुतः ।
सनत्कुमारः प्रोवाच ध्यात्वा राधापदांबुजम् ॥
1.88.m: Having heard those words of Nārada, Brahmā's son, / Sanatkumāra, spoke, after meditating on Rādhā's lotus feet.

1.88.s:
sanatkumāra uvāca
śṛṇu vipra pravakṣyāmi rahasyātirahasyakam /
rādhāvatāracaritaṃ bhajatāmiṣṭisiddhidam //
1.88.d:
सनत्कुमार उवाच
शृणु विप्र प्रवक्ष्यामि रहस्यातिरहस्यकम् ।
राधावतारचरितं भजतामिष्टिसिद्धिदम् ॥
1.88.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Listen, O Brahmin, I will declare the secret of secrets, / the deeds of Rādhā's incarnations, granting the fulfillment of wishes to those who worship.

1.88.s:
candrāvalī ca lalitā dve sakhyau supriye sadā /
mālāvatīmukhāṣṭānāṃ candrāvalyadhipāsmṛtā //
1.88.d:
चन्द्रावली च ललिता द्वे सख्यौ सुप्रिये सदा ।
मालावतीमुखाष्टानां चन्द्रावल्यधिपास्मृता ॥
1.88.m: Candrāvalī and Lalitā are always two very dear companions. / Candrāvalī is considered the ruler of the eight headed by Mālāvatī.

1.88.s:
kalāvatīmukhāṣṭānāmīśvarī lalitā matā /
rādhācaraṇapūjāyāmuktā mālāvatīmukhāḥ //
1.88.d:
