1.88.m: Dāha, Aṃbu, Marut, Haṃsa with Agni; this triad again; / Aṃbu and Dāha joined with Marut; then Haṃsa; Nabhas with Dharā;

1.88.s:
tejogninā punaḥ pañca vātaḥ svena samāyutaḥ /
toyaṃ careṇa tatpūrvaṃ toyamagniyutaṃ tataḥ //
1.88.d:
तेजोग्निना पुनः पञ्च वातः स्वेन समायुतः ।
तोयं चरेण तत्पूर्वं तोयमग्नियुतं ततः ॥
1.88.m: Tejas with Agni; then five; Vāta combined with Sva; / Toya with Cara; before that Toya joined with Agni; then

1.88.s:
śūnyaṃ vyāptena śucinā śūnyaṃ śaktyā nabho yutam /
dāho dharā svasaharitastoyaṃ carasamanvitam //
1.88.d:
शून्यं व्याप्तेन शुचिना शून्यं शक्त्या नभो युतम् ।
दाहो धरा स्वसहरितस्तोयं चरसमन्वितम् ॥
1.88.m: Śūnya with pervading Śuci; Śūnya joined with Śakti and Nabhas; / Dāha, Dharā, accompanied by Sva and Harit; Toya combined with Cara;

1.88.s:
etatpūrvamadhuḥ proktaṃ catuṣṭayamataḥ param /
jyākhyena yuktā sacaro rabhaścaitasya pūrvakam //
1.88.d:
एतत्पूर्वमधुः प्रोक्तं चतुष्टयमतः परम् ।
ज्याख्येन युक्ता सचरो रभश्चैतस्य पूर्वकम् ॥
1.88.m: Madhu preceded by this is proclaimed; hereafter a tetrad: / accompanied by what is called Jyā, Cara, Rabha, and that which precedes it;

1.88.s:
raso 'gninā punaḥ proktaṃ catuṣkā apayaṃ tataḥ /
śubhobhratā careṇāpi haṃsaḥ svena sapūrvakam //
1.88.d:
रसो ऽग्निना पुनः प्रोक्तं चतुष्का अपयं ततः ।
शुभोभ्रता चरेणापि हंसः स्वेन सपूर्वकम् ॥
1.88.m: Rasa with Agni; again a tetrad is proclaimed; then Apayam; / Śubha, Abhra, Cara as well, Haṃsa with Sva along with its predecessor;

1.88.s:
haṃso 'gninā prāk tritayaṃ hṛdayaṃ svasamāyutam /
rasaścareṇa tatpūrvamagninā ca raso yutaḥ //
1.88.d:
हंसो ऽग्निना प्राक् त्रितयं हृदयं स्वसमायुतम् ।
रसश्चरेण तत्पूर्वमग्निना च रसो युतः ॥
1.88.m: Haṃsa with Agni, the preceding triad; Hṛdaya combined with Sva; / Rasa with Cara, its predecessor, and Rasa joined with Agni;

1.88.s:
paścāduktastrayaṃ vāto dharayā ca nabhonvitam /
prāṇaḥ svena yutaḥ paścāddhṛdayasvayutaṃ rasaḥ //
1.88.d:
पश्चादुक्तस्त्रयं वातो धरया च नभोन्वितम् ।
प्राणः स्वेन युतः पश्चाद्धृदयस्वयुतं रसः ॥
1.88.m: then the triad mentioned: Vāta and Nabhas combined with Dharā; / Prāṇa joined with Sva; then Rasa joined with Hṛdaya and Sva;

1.88.s:
vyāptametattrayaṃ paścāddāhenāṃbu samanvitam /
gotrābharāyutā sparśo nādayukto javīyutaḥ //
1.88.d:
व्याप्तमेतत्त्रयं पश्चाद्दाहेनांबु समन्वितम् ।
गोत्राभरायुता स्पर्शो नादयुक्तो जवीयुतः ॥
1.88.m: this triad pervaded; then Aṃbu accompanied by Dāha; / Sparśa joined with Gotrā and Bharā, endowed with Nāda and speed;

1.88.s:
dāhena pūrvapūrvaṃ ca pūrvaṃ ca marutā yutam /
śūnyaṃ marutsvasahitaṃ hṛddāhenāṃbunā caraḥ //
1.88.d:
दाहेन पूर्वपूर्वं च पूर्वं च मरुता युतम् ।
शून्यं मरुत्स्वसहितं हृद्दाहेनांबुना चरः ॥
1.88.m: with Dāha each preceding one, and the predecessor joined with Marut; / Śūnya with Marut and Sva; Cara with Hṛt, Dāha, and Aṃbu;

1.88.s:
sparśo marutsvasahito hṛddāhenāṃbusaṃyutam /
jyāgniḥ svasaṃyuto haṃsastathāṃbu marutā saha //
1.88.d:
स्पर्शो मरुत्स्वसहितो हृद्दाहेनांबुसंयुतम् ।
ज्याग्निः स्वसंयुतो हंसस्तथांबु मरुता सह ॥
1.88.m: Sparśa accompanied by Marut and Sva; joined with Hṛt, Dāha, and Aṃbu; / Jyā, Agni joined with Sva, Haṃsa, and likewise Aṃbu with Marut;

1.88.s:
hṛdrūpreṇa svena yutaṃ rasaśca svena saṃyutaḥ /
prāṇadāhau dharāyuktau punastau vahninā viyat //
1.88.d:
हृद्रूप्रेण स्वेन युतं रसश्च स्वेन संयुतः ।
प्राणदाहौ धरायुक्तौ पुनस्तौ वह्निना वियत् ॥
1.88.m: Hṛt joined with Rūpra and Sva, and Rasa combined with Sva; / Prāṇa and Dāha joined with Dharā; again those two with Vahni; Viyat;

1.88.s:
vārddāhayuktamaṃbu syādiṣaṣṭyāsasvasaṃyutam /
pūrvadviruktavarṇau ca śuddhiḥ svena yutastathā //
1.88.d:
वार्द्दाहयुक्तमंबु स्यादिषष्ट्यासस्वसंयुतम् ।
पूर्वद्विरुक्तवर्णौ च शुद्धिः स्वेन युतस्तथा ॥
1.88.m: Aṃbu joined with Vāri and Dāha, joined with I, Ṣaṣṭhī, Asa, and Sva; / and the two syllables previously uttered; Śuddhi joined with Sva likewise;

1.88.s:
sthirā rasā vatasvena dāvau haṃsau dharā svayuk /
yutirnādavatī paścāddhṛdaṃbumarutā yutam //
1.88.d:
स्थिरा रसा वतस्वेन दावौ हंसौ धरा स्वयुक् ।
युतिर्नादवती पश्चाद्धृदंबुमरुता युतम् ॥
1.88.m: Sthirā, Rasā, Vāta with Sva; Dāva, Haṃsa, Dharā joined with Sva; / then a junction endowed with Nāda; Hṛt joined with Aṃbu and Marut;

1.88.s:
haṃsaśca marutā vidyaḥ daśottaraśatākṣarī /
vārāhī pañcamī viśvavijayā bhadrakaumudī //
1.88.d:
हंसश्च मरुता विद्यः दशोत्तरशताक्षरी ।
वाराही पञ्चमी विश्वविजया भद्रकौमुदी ॥
1.88.m: and Haṃsa with Marut—the vidyā of one hundred and ten syllables: / Vārāhī, Pañcamī, Viśvavijayā, Bhadrakaumudī,

1.88.s:
vārtālīti ca vikhyātā staṃbhanādyakhileṣṭadā /
aṅgāni kuryānmantrārṇaiḥ saptabhiṣaḍbhireva ca //
1.88.d:
वार्तालीति च विख्याता स्तंभनाद्यखिलेष्टदा ।
अङ्गानि कुर्यान्मन्त्रार्णैः सप्तभिषड्भिरेव च ॥
1.88.m: and celebrated as Vārtālī, granting all desires such as immobilization. / One should perform the limbs with seven and six syllables of the mantra,

1.88.s:
daśabhiḥ saptabhiḥ saptasaṃkhyairjātibhirditāḥ /
trikoṇavṛttaṣaṭkoṇavṛttadvayasamanvitam //
1.88.d:
दशभिः सप्तभिः सप्तसंख्यैर्जातिभिर्दिताः ।
त्रिकोणवृत्तषट्कोणवृत्तद्वयसमन्वितम् ॥
1.88.m: with ten, seven, and seven, recited with the [respective] jātis. / Having prepared a cakra endowed with a triangle, a circle,

1.88.s:
vidhāya cakraṃ tatraiva svanāmālikhyapūjayet /
dhyāyecca devīṃ kīlāsyāṃ tataḥ kāñcanasannibhām //
1.88.d:
विधाय चक्रं तत्रैव स्वनामालिख्यपूजयेत् ।
ध्यायेच्च देवीं कीलास्यां ततः काञ्चनसन्निभाम् ॥
1.88.m: a hexagon, and two circles, having inscribed one's own name right there, one should worship it. / Then one should meditate on the Goddess having a boar's face, resembling gold,

1.88.s:
ākaṇṭhaṃ vanitārūpāṃ jvalatpiṅgasaroruhām /
trinetrāmaṣṭahastāṃ ca cakraṃ śaṅkhamathāṅkuśam //
1.88.d:
आकण्ठं वनितारूपां ज्वलत्पिङ्गसरोरुहाम् ।
त्रिनेत्रामष्टहस्तां च चक्रं शङ्खमथाङ्कुशम् ॥
1.88.m: having the form of a woman up to her neck, with blazing golden lotuses, / three-eyed, eight-armed, [holding] a discus, a conch, then a goad,

1.88.s:
pāśaṃ ca muśalaṃ śīrṣamabhayaṃ varadaṃ tathā /
dadhānāṃ garuḍaskandhe sukhāsīnāṃ vicintayet //
1.88.d:
पाशं च मुशलं शीर्षमभयं वरदं तथा ।
दधानां गरुडस्कन्धे सुखासीनां विचिन्तयेत् ॥
1.88.m: a noose, a pestle, a severed head, and gestures of freedom from fear and bestowing boons: / one should contemplate her seated comfortably upon the shoulders of Garuḍa.

1.88.s:
nityapūjāsu tacchaktīstatsamānāḥ smarenmune /
prayogeṣu smareddevīṃ siṃhasthāṃ vyāghragāmapi //
1.88.d:
नित्यपूजासु तच्छक्तीस्तत्समानाः स्मरेन्मुने ।
प्रयोगेषु स्मरेद्देवीं सिंहस्थां व्याघ्रगामपि ॥
1.88.m: In daily worships, O sage, one should remember her Śaktis who are similar to her. / In magical rituals, one should remember the Goddess mounted on a lion, or even riding a tiger,

1.88.s:
gajārūḍhāṃ hayārūḍhāṃ tarśyārūḍhāṃ ca śaktibhiḥ /
śyāmāmapyaruṇāṃ pītāmasitāṃbhojavigrahām //
1.88.d:
गजारूढां हयारूढां तर्श्यारूढां च शक्तिभिः ।
श्यामामप्यरुणां पीतामसितांभोजविग्रहाम् ॥
1.88.m: mounted on an elephant, mounted on a horse, or mounted on Garuḍa with her Śaktis, / dark, or reddish, yellow, or with a body like a blue lotus.

1.88.s:
tattattprayogeṣu tathā dhyāyettattadavāptaye /
aruṇāṃ pañcamīṃ vaśye pītāṃ staṃbhanake smaret //
1.88.d:
तत्तत्त्प्रयोगेषु तथा ध्यायेत्तत्तदवाप्तये ।
अरुणां पञ्चमीं वश्ये पीतां स्तंभनके स्मरेत् ॥
1.88.m: In the respective magical rituals, one should meditate in that manner to attain each result: / in subjection, one should remember Pañcamī as red; in immobilization, as yellow;

1.88.s:
śyāmāṃ ca durgame mārge sitāṃ yuddhe 'rinaṣṭaye /
dhūmrāmuccāṭane dhyāyetsādhako dvijasattamaḥ //
1.88.d:
श्यामां च दुर्गमे मार्गे सितां युद्धे ऽरिनष्टये ।
धूम्रामुच्चाटने ध्यायेत्साधको द्विजसत्तमः ॥
1.88.m: on an impassable path as dark; in battle, for the destruction of enemies, as white; / in eradication, the practitioner, best among the twice-born, should meditate upon her as smoky.

1.88.s:
etāḥ ṣoḍaśa nityāste saṃkṣapātsamudīritāḥ /
bhajatāmiṣṭadāḥ sadyaḥ sarvapāpakṣayaṅkarāḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge bṛhadupākhyāne tṛtīyapāde rādhādimantranirūpaṇaṃ nāmāṣṭāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.88.d:
एताः षोडश नित्यास्ते संक्षपात्समुदीरिताः ।
भजतामिष्टदाः सद्यः सर्वपापक्षयङ्कराः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे बृहदुपाख्याने तृतीयपादे राधादिमन्त्रनिरूपणं नामाष्टाशीतितमो ऽध्यायः
1.88.m:
These sixteen Nityās have been proclaimed to you in brief; / they grant desires immediately to those who worship them, and destroy all sins.

Thus ends the eighty-eighth chapter, entitled "Ascertainment of the Mantras of Rādhā and Others," in the third quarter of the major narrative in the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.
